children.text: evaṃ mahāyānamidaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām
children.translated_text: Thus this <s>Mahāyāna</s> (great vehicle) belongs to the bodhisattvas, the great beings.

children.text: atra śikṣitvā bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ sarvajñatā anuprāptā anuprāpsyate anuprāpyate ca ||
children.translated_text: Having trained in this, bodhisattvas, great beings, have attained omniscience, will attain it, and are attaining it.

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputro bhagavantametadavocat ayaṃ bhagavan subhūtiḥ sthaviraḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ kṛtaśo 'dhīṣṭo mahāyānamupadeṣṭavyaṃ manyate
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, this elder <s>Subhūti</s>, appointed for the sake of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (the perfection of wisdom), thinks that the <s>Mahāyāna</s> should be taught."

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat nāhaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāṃ vyatikramya mahāyānamavocam
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, I did not speak of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> by transgressing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>."

children.text: bhagavānāha no hīdaṃ subhūte
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "No indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>.

children.text: anulomatvaṃ subhūte prajñāpāramitāyā mahāyānamupadiśasi
children.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s>, you teach the <s>Mahāyāna</s> in conformity with <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>."

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat buddhānubhāvādbhagavan
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: "It is through the Buddha's power, Blessed One.

children.text: api nu khalu punarbhagavan pūrvāntato bodhisattvo nopaiti aparāntato bodhisattvo nopaiti madhyato bodhisattvo nopaiti
children.translated_text: But then, Blessed One, a bodhisattva is not approached from the prior limit, a bodhisattva is not approached from the later limit, and a bodhisattva is not approached from the middle.

children.text: tatkasya hetornopaiti rūpāparyantatayā hi bodhisattvāparyantatā veditavyā evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? For the boundlessness of the bodhisattva should be known through the boundlessness of form; so too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: vijñānāparyantatayā hi bodhisattvāparyantatā veditavyā
children.translated_text: For the boundlessness of the bodhisattva should be known through the boundlessness of consciousness.

children.text: rūpaṃ bodhisattva iti nopaiti
children.translated_text: He does not approach the notion, 'Form is the bodhisattva.'

children.text: idam api na vidyate nopalabhyate
children.translated_text: This too does not exist and is not apprehended.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: vijñānaṃ bodhisattva iti nopaiti idam api na vidyate nopalabhyate
children.translated_text: He does not approach the notion, 'Consciousness is the bodhisattva.' This too does not exist and is not apprehended.

children.text: evaṃ bhagavan sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ bodhisattvadharmam anupalabhamāno nāhaṃ bhagavan taṃ dharmaṃ samanupaśyāmi yasyaitannāmadheyaṃ yaduta bodhisattva iti
children.translated_text: Thus, Blessed One, since in every respect, entirely and in every way, I do not apprehend any bodhisattva-dharma at all, I do not see that dharma to which the name 'bodhisattva' belongs.

children.text: prajñāpāramitām api na samanupaśyāmi nopalabhe
children.translated_text: I also do not see <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, nor do I apprehend it.

children.text: sarvajñatām api na samanupaśyāmi nopalabhe
children.translated_text: I also do not see omniscience, nor do I apprehend it.

children.text: so 'haṃ bhagavan sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ taṃ dharmam anupalabhamāno 'samanupaśyan katamaṃ dharmaṃ katamena dharmeṇa katamasmin dharme 'vavadiṣyāmi anuśāsiṣyāmi buddha iti bhagavan nāmadheyamātram etat
children.translated_text: Since, Blessed One, in every respect, entirely and in every way, I do not apprehend or see that dharma, what dharma shall I instruct, by what dharma, and in what dharma shall I admonish? Blessed One, '<s>Buddha</s>' is merely a name.

children.text: bodhisattva iti bhagavan nāmadheyamātram etat
children.translated_text: Blessed One, 'bodhisattva' is merely a name.

children.text: prajñāpāramiteti bhagavan nāmadheyamātram etat
children.translated_text: Blessed One, '<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' is merely a name.

children.text: tacca nāmadheyam anabhinirvṛttam
children.translated_text: And that name has not come into being.

children.text: yathā ātmā ātmeti ca bhagavannucyate atyantatayā ca bhagavannanabhinirvṛtta ātmā
children.translated_text: Just as, Blessed One, one speaks of 'self, self,' and yet, Blessed One, the self has absolutely not come into being,

children.text: evamasvabhāvānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ katamattadrūpaṃ yad agrāhyam anabhinirvṛttam katame te vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ katamattadvijñānaṃ yad agrāhyam anabhinirvṛttam evameteṣāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ yā asvabhāvatā sā anabhinirvṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: so, among all dharmas that are without own-being, what is that form which is ungraspable and has not come into being? What are those feelings, perceptions, and formations? What is that consciousness which is ungraspable and has not come into being? Thus the absence of own-being of all these dharmas is their not coming into being.

children.text: yā ca sarvadharmāṇām anabhinirvṛttirna te dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: And because there is this not coming into being of all dharmas, those dharmas are not dharmas.

children.text: tat kim anabhinirvṛttim anabhinirvṛttyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāmavavadiṣyāmyanuśāsiṣyāmi na cānyatra bhagavan anabhinirvṛttitaḥ sarvadharmā vā buddhadharmā vā bodhisattvadharmā vā upalabhyante yo vā bodhāya caret
children.translated_text: What then shall I instruct and admonish by means of non-coming-into-being, in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> that has not come into being? And apart from non-coming-into-being, Blessed One, no dharmas at all, no Buddha-dharmas, no bodhisattva-dharmas, nor anyone who courses toward awakening, are apprehended.

children.text: sacedbhagavan evaṃ bhāṣyamāṇe evaṃ deśyamāne evamupadiśyamāne bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya cittaṃ nāvalīyate na saṃlīyate na viṣīdati na viṣādamāpadyate nāsya vipṛṣṭhībhavati mānasaṃ na bhagnapṛṣṭhībhavati nottrasyati na saṃtrasyati na saṃtrāsamāpadyate evaṃ veditavyam caratyayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyām
children.translated_text: If, Blessed One, while this is being spoken, taught, and explained in this way, the mind of a bodhisattva, a great being, does not sink, does not collapse, does not despond, does not fall into despondency, if his mind does not turn its back, does not become broken-backed, does not tremble, does not panic, and does not fall into panic, then it should be known that this bodhisattva, this great being, courses in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: bhāvayatyayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitām
children.translated_text: This bodhisattva, this great being, cultivates <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: upaparīkṣate 'yaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitām
children.translated_text: This bodhisattva, this great being, examines <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: upanidhyāyatyayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāmiti
children.translated_text: This bodhisattva, this great being, contemplates <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ yasmin hi samaye bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ imān dharmān prajñāpāramitāyāṃ vyupaparīkṣate tasmin samaye na rūpamupaiti na rūpamupagacchati na rūpasyotpādaṃ samanupaśyati na rūpasya nirodhaṃ samanupaśyati
children.translated_text: Why is that? For at the time, Blessed One, when a bodhisattva, a great being, thoroughly examines these dharmas in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, at that time he does not approach form, does not go toward form, does not see the arising of form, and does not see the cessation of form.

children.text: evaṃ na vedanāṃ na saṃjñāṃ na saṃskārān
children.translated_text: So too he does not approach feeling, perception, or formations.

children.text: na vijñānamupaiti na vijñānamupagacchati na vijñānasyotpādaṃ samanupaśyati na vijñānasya nirodhaṃ samanupaśyati
children.translated_text: He does not approach consciousness, does not go toward consciousness, does not see the arising of consciousness, and does not see the cessation of consciousness.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi yo rūpasyānutpādo na tadrūpam
children.translated_text: Why is that? For indeed, what is the non-arising of form is not that form.

children.text: yo rūpasyāvyayo na tadrūpam
children.translated_text: What is the imperishability of form is not that form.

children.text: ityanutpādaś ca rūpaṃ ca advayametad advaidhīkāram
children.translated_text: Thus non-arising and form are non-dual; this is non-division.

children.text: ityavyayaś ca rūpaṃ ca advayam etad advaidhīkāram
children.translated_text: Thus imperishability and form are non-dual; this is non-division.

children.text: yatpunaretaducyate rūpamiti advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā
children.translated_text: And what is called 'form' is a designation of the non-dual.

children.text: evaṃ tathā hi yo vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām
children.translated_text: So too, indeed, with what pertains to feeling, perception, and formations:

children.text: tathā hi yo vijñānasyānutpādo na tadvijñānam yo vijñānasyāvyayo na tadvijñānam
children.translated_text: indeed, what is the non-arising of consciousness is not that consciousness; what is the imperishability of consciousness is not that consciousness.

children.text: ityanutpādaś ca vijñānaṃ ca advayam etad advaidhīkāram
children.translated_text: Thus non-arising and consciousness are non-dual; this is non-division.

children.text: ityavyayaś ca vijñānaṃ ca advayam etad advaidhīkāram
children.translated_text: Thus imperishability and consciousness are non-dual; this is non-division.

children.text: yatpunaretaducyate vijñānamiti advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā
children.translated_text: And what is called 'consciousness' is a designation of the non-dual.

children.text: evaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sarvākāraṃ sarvadharmān vyupaparīkṣamāṇaḥ tasmin samaye na rūpamupaiti na rūpamupagacchati na rūpasyotpādaṃ samanupaśyati na rūpasya nirodhaṃ samanupaśyati
children.translated_text: Thus, Blessed One, when, in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (the perfection of wisdom), he examines all dharmas in every way, at that time he does not approach form, does not go toward form, does not perceive the arising of form, and does not perceive the cessation of form.

children.text: evaṃ na vedanāṃ na saṃjñāṃ na saṃskārān
children.translated_text: So too he does not approach feeling, perception, or formations.

children.text: na vijñānamupaiti na vijñānamupagacchati na vijñānasyotpādaṃ samanupaśyati na vijñānasya nirodhaṃ samanupaśyati
children.translated_text: He does not approach consciousness, does not go toward consciousness, does not perceive the arising of consciousness, and does not perceive the cessation of consciousness.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi yo rūpasyānutpādo na tadrūpam
children.translated_text: Why is that? For what is the non-arising of form is not form.

children.text: yo rūpasyāvyayo na tadrūpam
children.translated_text: What is the non-decay of form is not form.

children.text: ityanutpādaś ca rūpaṃ ca advayam etad advaidhīkāram
children.translated_text: Thus non-arising and form are nondual; this is free from dualization.

children.text: ityavyayaśca rūpaṃ ca advayam etad advaidhīkāram
children.translated_text: Thus non-decay and form are nondual; this is free from dualization.

children.text: yatpunaretaducyate rūpamiti advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā
children.translated_text: And what is called 'form' is a reckoning made of the nondual.

children.text: evaṃ tathā hi yo vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām
children.translated_text: So too, for what is of feeling, of perception, and of formations,

children.text: tathā hi yo vijñānasyānutpādo na tadvijñānam yo vijñānasyāvyayo na tadvijñānam
children.translated_text: for what is the non-arising of consciousness is not consciousness, and what is the non-decay of consciousness is not consciousness.

children.text: ityanutpādaś ca vijñānaṃ ca advayam etad advaidhīkāram
children.translated_text: Thus non-arising and consciousness are nondual; this is free from dualization.

children.text: ityavyayaś ca vijñānaṃ ca advayam etad advaidhīkāram
children.translated_text: Thus non-decay and consciousness are nondual; this is free from dualization.

children.text: yatpunaretaducyate vijñānamiti advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: And what is called 'consciousness' is a reckoning made of the nondual.

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat tena hi yathāhamāyuṣmataḥ subhūterbhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi tathā bodhisattvo 'pyanutpādaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "In that case, as I understand the meaning of what the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> has said, the bodhisattva too is non-arising.

children.text: yadi ca āyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo 'pyanutpādaḥ kiṃ bodhisattvo duṣkaracārikāṃ carati yāni vā tāni sattvānāṃ kṛtaśo duḥkhānyutsahate pratyanubhavitum evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat nāhamāyuṣman śāriputra icchāmi bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ duṣkaracārikāṃ carantam nāpi sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yo duṣkarasaṃjñayā carati
children.translated_text: And if, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the bodhisattva too is non-arising, does the bodhisattva practice a difficult course, or does he undertake to experience those many sufferings of beings?" When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, I do not wish a bodhisattva, a great being, to practice a difficult course; nor is he a bodhisattva, a great being, if he practices with the perception of difficulty.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ na hi āyuṣman śāriputra duṣkarasaṃjñāṃ janayitvā śakyo 'prameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmarthaḥ kartum
children.translated_text: Why is that? For, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, it is not possible to accomplish the welfare of immeasurable, innumerable beings after generating a perception of difficulty.

children.text: api tu sukhasaṃjñāmeva kṛtvā
children.translated_text: Rather, having made only a perception of ease,

children.text: sarvasattvānāmantike mātṛsaṃjñāṃ pitṛsaṃjñāṃ putrasaṃjñāṃ duhitṛsaṃjñāṃ kṛtvā strīpuruṣeṣu
children.translated_text: having made the perception of mother, the perception of father, the perception of son, and the perception of daughter toward all beings, toward women and men,

children.text: evametāḥ saṃjñāḥ kṛtvā bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bodhisattvacārikāṃ carati
children.translated_text: having made these perceptions in this way, a bodhisattva, a great being, practices the bodhisattva course.

children.text: tasmānmātṛsaṃjñā pitṛsaṃjñā putrasaṃjñā duhitṛsaṃjñā bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvasattvānāmantike yāvadātmasaṃjñā utpādayitavyā
children.translated_text: Therefore a bodhisattva, a great being, should generate toward all beings the perception of mother, the perception of father, the perception of son, the perception of daughter, even up to the perception of self.

children.text: yathā ātmā sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ sarvaduḥkhebhyo mocayitavyaḥ evaṃ sarvasattvāḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ sarvaduḥkhebhyo mocayitavyā iti
children.translated_text: Just as the self is to be released, in every respect, entirely and in every way, from all sufferings, so all beings are to be released, in every respect, entirely and in every way, from all sufferings.

children.text: evaṃ ca sarvasattveṣu saṃjñā utpādayitavyā mayaite sarvasattvā na parityaktavyāḥ
children.translated_text: And this perception should be generated toward all beings: 'These all beings are not to be abandoned by me.

children.text: mayaite sarvasattvāḥ parimocayitavyā aparimāṇato duḥkhaskandhāt
children.translated_text: These all beings are to be released by me from an immeasurable mass of suffering.

children.text: na ca mayaiteṣu cittapradoṣa utpādayitavya antaśaḥ śataśo 'pi chidyamāneneti
children.translated_text: And no corruption of mind is to be generated by me toward them, even if I am being cut apart hundreds of times.'

children.text: evaṃ hi bodhisattvena mahāsattvena cittamutpādayitavyam sa ced evaṃcitto vihariṣyati na duṣkarasaṃjñī cariṣyati na duṣkarasaṃjñī vihariṣyati
children.translated_text: For in this way a bodhisattva, a great being, should generate the mind. If he dwells with such a mind, he will not practice with the perception of difficulty and will not dwell with the perception of difficulty.

children.text: punaraparamāyuṣman śāriputra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena evaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam yathā sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvamātmā na vidyate nopalabhyate evaṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ sarvadharmā na saṃvidyante nopalabhyante
children.translated_text: Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, should generate the mind in this way: just as the self is not found and is not apprehended in every respect, entirely and in every way, so all dharmas are not found and are not apprehended in every respect, entirely and in every way.

children.text: evamādhyātmikabāhyeṣu sarvadharmeṣu saṃjñā utpādayitavyā
children.translated_text: Such a perception should be generated with regard to all internal and external dharmas.

children.text: saced evaṃcittaścariṣyati na duṣkarasaṃjñī cariṣyati na duṣkarasaṃjñī vihariṣyati
children.translated_text: If he practices with such a mind, he will not practice with the perception of difficulty and will not dwell with the perception of difficulty.

children.text: yadapyāyuṣman śāriputra evamāha anutpādo bodhisattvo iti
children.translated_text: And as for what you said, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that the bodhisattva is non-arising,

children.text: evametadāyuṣman śāriputra evam etat
children.translated_text: so it is, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>; so it is.

children.text: anutpādo bodhisattva iti ||
children.translated_text: The bodhisattva is non-arising."

children.text: śāriputra āha kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte bodhisattva evānutpādaḥ utāho bodhisattvadharmā apyanutpādaḥ subhūtirāha bodhisattvadharmā api āyuṣman śāriputra anutpādaḥ śāriputra āha kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvadharmā evānutpādaḥ utāho sarvajñatāpyanutpādaḥ subhūtirāha sarvajñatāpyāyuṣman śāriputra anutpādaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śāriputra</s> said: "But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is only the bodhisattva non-arising, or are the bodhisattva-dharmas also non-arising?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the bodhisattva-dharmas also are non-arising." <s>Śāriputra</s> said: "But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are only the bodhisattva-dharmas non-arising, or is omniscience also non-arising?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, omniscience also is non-arising."

children.text: āha kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte sarvajñataivānutpādaḥ utāho sarvajñatādharmā apyanutpādaḥ āha sarvajñatādharmā apyāyuṣman śāriputra anutpādaḥ
children.translated_text: He said: "But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is only omniscience non-arising, or are the dharmas of omniscience also non-arising?" He said: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the dharmas of omniscience also are non-arising."

children.text: āha kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte sarvajñatādharmā evānutpādaḥ utāho pṛthagjano 'pyanutpādaḥ āha pṛthagjano 'pyāyuṣman śāriputra anutpādaḥ
children.translated_text: He said: "But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are only the dharmas of omniscience non-arising, or is the <s>pṛthagjana</s> (ordinary person) also non-arising?" He said: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>pṛthagjana</s> also is non-arising."

children.text: āha kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte pṛthagjana evānutpādaḥ utāho pṛthagjanadharmā apyanutpādaḥ āha pṛthagjanadharmā apyāyuṣman śāriputra anutpādaḥ
children.translated_text: He said: "But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is only the <s>pṛthagjana</s> non-arising, or are the dharmas of the <s>pṛthagjana</s> also non-arising?" He said: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the dharmas of the <s>pṛthagjana</s> also are non-arising."

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat yadyāyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo 'pyanutpādaḥ bodhisattvadharmā apyanutpādaḥ sarvajñatāpyanutpādaḥ sarvajñatādharmā apyanutpādaḥ pṛthagjano 'pyanutpādaḥ pṛthagjanadharmā apyanutpādaḥ nanvāyuṣman subhūte anuprāptaiva ayatnena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvajñatā bhavati
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "If, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, even a bodhisattva is non-arisen, bodhisattva-dharmas too are non-arisen, omniscience too is non-arisen, the dharmas of omniscience too are non-arisen, an ordinary person too is non-arisen, and the dharmas of ordinary persons too are non-arisen, then surely, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, omniscience has been attained by a bodhisattva, a great being, without effort?"

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat nāhamāyuṣman śāriputra anutpannasya dharmasya prāptimicchāmi nāpyabhisamayam
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, I do not wish for the attainment of a non-arisen dharma, nor for its direct realization.

children.text: nāpyanutpannena dharmeṇa anutpannā prāptiḥ prāpyate
children.translated_text: Nor is a non-arisen attainment attained by means of a non-arisen dharma."

children.text: āha kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte anutpannena dharmeṇa anutpannā prāptiḥ prāpyate utāho utpannena dharmeṇa anutpannā prāptiḥ prāpyate āha kiṃ punarāyuṣman śāriputra anutpanno dharma utpannaḥ utāho anutpanna eva dharmo 'nutpannaḥ āha kiṃ punarāyuṣman subhūte utpāda eva dharmo 'nutpādaḥ utāho anutpādo dharma utpādaḥ āha utpādo dharmo 'nutpādo dharma ityāyuṣman śāriputra na pratibhāti jalpitum
children.translated_text: He said, "But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is a non-arisen attainment attained by means of a non-arisen dharma, or is a non-arisen attainment attained by means of an arisen dharma?" He said, "But, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is a non-arisen dharma arisen, or is a non-arisen dharma simply non-arisen?" He said, "But, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is arising itself the dharma non-arising, or is non-arising the dharma arising?" He said, "'Arising is a dharma; non-arising is a dharma'--venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, this does not present itself to be spoken."

children.text: āha anutpādo 'pi te āyuṣman subhūte pratibhāti jalpitum
children.translated_text: He said, "Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does non-arising too present itself to you to be spoken?"

children.text: āha anutpāda evāyuṣman śāriputra jalpaḥ
children.translated_text: He said, "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, speech itself is non-arising.

children.text: anutpāda eva āyuṣman śāriputra pratibhāti
children.translated_text: Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, what presents itself is only non-arising.

children.text: anutpāda eva āyuṣman śāriputra pratibhānam
children.translated_text: Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, eloquence itself is non-arising.

children.text: evamevāyuṣman śāriputra atyantaṃ pratibhāti ||
children.translated_text: In just this way, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, it presents itself completely."

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat dhārmakathikānāmāyuṣmān subhūtiragratāyāṃ sthāpitavyaḥ
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "The venerable <s>Subhūti</s> should be placed in the foremost rank among speakers of dharma.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hyāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ sthaviro yato yata eva paripraśnīkriyate tatastata eva niḥsarati dharmatāyāś ca na calati tāṃ ca dharmatāṃ na virodhayati
children.translated_text: Why is that? For the elder venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, from whatever point he is questioned, from that very point finds a way out; he does not move from <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of dharma), and he does not contradict that <s>dharmatā</s>."

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat dharmataiṣā āyuṣman śāriputra bhagavataḥ śrāvakāṇām aniśritadharmāṇām
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, this is the <s>dharmatā</s> of the Blessed One's disciples, who rely on no dharma.

children.text: te yato yata eva paripraśnīkriyante tatastata eva niḥsaranti dharmatāṃ ca na virodhayanti dharmatāyāś ca na vyativartante
children.translated_text: From whatever point they are questioned, from that very point they find a way out; they do not contradict <s>dharmatā</s>, and they do not turn away from <s>dharmatā</s>.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ yathāpi nāma aniśritatvāt sarvadharmāṇām
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because all dharmas are without support."

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat sādhu sādhu āyuṣman subhūte
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Good, good, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>.

children.text: katamaiṣā sarvadharmāniśritapāramitā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām subhūtirāha prajñāpāramitaiva āyuṣman śāriputra sārvayānikī sarvadharmāniśritatayā sarvadharmāniśritapāramitā ca
children.translated_text: What is this perfection of non-reliance on all dharmas for bodhisattvas, great beings?" <s>Subhūti</s> said, "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, it is precisely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (the perfection of wisdom), belonging to all vehicles because it relies on no dharma at all, and it is the perfection of non-reliance on all dharmas.

children.text: iti hi yasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya evaṃ gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāmevaṃ deśyamānāyām evam upadiśyamānāyāṃ na bhavati cittasya avalīnatvam na bhavati kāṅkṣāyitatvam na bhavati dhandhāyitatvam na bhavati cittasyānyathātvam veditavyam ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo viharatyanena prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa avirahitaścānena manasikāreṇeti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, for whatever bodhisattva, great being, when this profound <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being spoken, taught, and explained in this way, there is no sinking of mind, no doubting, no hesitation, and no alteration of mind, it should be known that this bodhisattva, great being, dwells in this dwelling of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and is not separated from this mental attention."

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmataṃ subhūtimetadavocat kathamāyuṣman subhūte avirahito bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'virahito manasikāreṇa bhavati yaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa viharati yadi hyāyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'virahito manasikāreṇa bhavati evaṃ sa virahitaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa bhavati
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "How, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is a bodhisattva, a great being, not separated, not separated from mental attention, when he dwells in the dwelling of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>? For if, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, is not separated from mental attention, then he is separated from the dwelling of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: yadi ca āyuṣman subhūte avirahito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa bhavati evaṃ sa virahito manasikāreṇa bhavati
children.translated_text: And if, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, is not separated from the dwelling of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, then he is separated from mental attention.

children.text: yadi ca āyuṣman subhūte manasikāreṇāvirahito bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ avirahita eva prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa bhavati
children.translated_text: And if, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, not separated from mental attention is indeed not separated from the dwelling of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>,

children.text: evaṃ sati sarvasattvā apyavirahitā bhaviṣyanti prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa
children.translated_text: then, that being so, all beings too will be not separated from the dwelling of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ sarvasattvā api hyavirahitā manasikāreṇa viharanti ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? For all beings too dwell not separated from mental attention."

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat sādhu sādhu āyuṣman śāriputra
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Good, good, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>.

children.text: api tu upālapsye tvā
children.translated_text: Still, I will take you to task.

children.text: artha eva tvāyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa bhūtapadābhidhānena parigṛhītaḥ
children.translated_text: Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the very meaning has been grasped by you through the expression of the real word.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ sattvāsvabhāvatayā āyuṣman śāriputra manasikārāsvabhāvatā veditavyā
children.translated_text: Why is that? Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, through the absence of own-being in beings, the absence of own-being in mental attention should be understood.

children.text: sattvāsadbhāvatayā āyuṣman śāriputra manasikārāsadbhāvatā veditavyā
children.translated_text: Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, through the non-existence of beings, the non-existence of mental attention should be understood.

children.text: sattvaviviktatayā āyuṣman śāriputra manasikāraviviktatā veditavyā
children.translated_text: Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, through the separateness of beings, the separateness of mental attention should be understood.

children.text: sattvācintyatayā āyuṣman śāriputra manasikārācintyatā veditavyā
children.translated_text: Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, through the inconceivability of beings, the inconceivability of mental attention should be understood."

children.text: sattvānabhisaṃbodhanatayā āyuṣman śāriputra manasikārānabhisaṃbodhanatā veditavyā
children.translated_text: By the non-realization of beings, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the non-realization of mental attention is to be understood.

children.text: sattvāyathābhūtārthābhisaṃbodhanatayā āyuṣman śāriputra manasikārāyathābhūtārthābhisaṃbodhanatā veditavyā
children.translated_text: By the realization of beings according to the meaning as it truly is, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the realization of mental attention according to the meaning as it truly is is to be understood.

children.text: anena āyuṣman śāriputra evaṃrūpeṇa manasikāreṇa icchāmi bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ viharantamanena vihāreṇeti ||
children.translated_text: With such mental attention as this, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, I wish a bodhisattva, a great being, to dwell in this dwelling.

children.text: Chapter 2
tena khalu punaḥ samayena śakro devānāmindrastasyāmeva parṣadi saṃnipatitaḥ saṃniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt catvāriṃśatā trayastriṃśatkāyikair devaputrasahasraiḥ sārdham
children.translated_text: Now at that very time <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, had gathered and sat down in that same assembly, together with forty thousand divine sons belonging to the heaven of the Thirty-three.

children.text: catvāraś ca lokapālā viṃśatyā cāturmahārājakāyikair devaputrasahasraiḥ sārdham
children.translated_text: And the four world-guardians were there, together with twenty thousand divine sons belonging to the heaven of the Four Great Kings.

children.text: brahmāpi sahāpatirdaśabhir brahmakāyikair devaputrasahasraiḥ sārdham
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> also was there, together with ten thousand divine sons belonging to the Brahmā host.

children.text: pañca ca śuddhāvāsānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi tasyāmeva parṣadi saṃnipatitāni saṃniṣaṇṇānyabhūvan
children.translated_text: And five thousand divine sons of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> heavens had gathered and sat down in that same assembly.

children.text: yo 'pi ca devānāṃ svakarmavipākajo 'vabhāsaḥ so 'pi sarvo buddhānubhāvena buddhatejasā buddhādhiṣṭhānenābhibhūto 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: And whatever radiance of the gods was produced by the fruition of their own actions, all of it was overpowered by the power of the Buddha, by the splendor of the Buddha, and by the sustaining force of the Buddha.

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃ sthavirametadavocat imānyārya subhūte saṃbahulāni devaputrasahasrāṇi asyāṃ parṣadi saṃnipatitāni saṃniṣaṇṇāni āryasya subhūterantikātprajñāpāramitāṃ śrotukāmāni bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām upadeśam avavādānuśāsanīṃ ca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s>: "Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, these many thousands of divine sons have gathered and sat down in this assembly, wishing to hear <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> from noble <s>Subhūti</s>, together with instruction, exhortation, and admonition for bodhisattvas, great beings.

children.text: tatkathaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyam kathaṃ śikṣitavyam kathaṃ yogamāpattavyam sthaviraḥ subhūtirāha tena hi kauśika upadekṣyāmi te buddhānubhāvena buddhatejasā buddhādhiṣṭhānena
children.translated_text: How, then, should a bodhisattva, a great being, stand in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>? How should he train? How should he apply himself?" The elder <s>Subhūti</s> said: "In that case, <s>Kauśika</s>, I shall teach you, through the power of the Buddha, through the splendor of the Buddha, and through the sustaining force of the Buddha.

children.text: yairdevaputrairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ notpāditam tairutpādayitavyam
children.translated_text: Those divine sons who have not produced the mind directed toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening should produce it.

children.text: ye tvavakrāntāḥ samyaktvaniyāmam na te bhavyā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayitum
children.translated_text: But those who have entered the fixed course of rightness are not capable of producing the mind directed toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ baddhasīmāno hi te saṃsārasrotasaḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? For the boundaries of the stream of saṃsāra have been fixed for them.

children.text: abhavyā hi te punaḥ punaḥ saṃsaraṇāya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayitum
children.translated_text: For they are not capable, through repeated transmigration, of producing the mind directed toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

children.text: api nu khalu punasteṣāmapyanumode
children.translated_text: Yet I rejoice even in them as well.

children.text: sacette 'pyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādayeran nāhaṃ kuśalamūlasyāntarāyaṃ karomi
children.translated_text: If even they were to produce minds directed toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening, I would not create an obstruction to that root of merit.

children.text: viśiṣṭebhyo hi dharmebhyo viśiṣṭatamā dharmā adhyālambitavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For from excellent dharmas, still more excellent dharmas should be taken up."

children.text: atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimāmantrayate sma sādhu sādhu subhūte sādhu khalu punastvaṃ subhūte yastvaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmutsāhaṃ dadāsi
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Good, good, <s>Subhūti</s>; it is good indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, that you give encouragement to bodhisattvas, great beings.

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat kṛtajñairasmābhirbhagavan bhagavato bhavitavyaṃ nākṛtajñaiḥ
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, we should be grateful to the Blessed One, not ungrateful.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ paurvakāṇāṃ hi bhagavaṃstathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmantike 'smadarthe bhagavān yathā brahmacaryaṃ bodhāya caran pūrvaṃ bodhisattvabhūta eva san yaiḥ śrāvakairavavadito 'nuśiṣṭaś ca pāramitāsu tatra bhagavatā caratā anuttaraṃ jñānamutpāditam
children.translated_text: Why is that? In the presence of former tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened ones, Blessed One, for our sake, while the Blessed One, still previously only in the state of a bodhisattva, was practicing the holy life for awakening, he was exhorted and instructed in the perfections by disciples; and as the Blessed One practiced there, unsurpassed knowledge was produced.

children.text: evaṃ bhagavan asmābhir api bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anuparigrahītavyā anuparivārayitavyāśca samparigrahītavyāḥ saṃparivārayitavyāś ca
children.translated_text: Thus, Blessed One, bodhisattvas, great beings, should also be followed, attended upon, supported, and surrounded by us.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ asmābhir api hi bhagavan bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anuparigṛhītā anuparivāritāśca samparigṛhītāḥ saṃparivāritāś ca kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? For when bodhisattvas, great beings, are followed, attended upon, supported, and surrounded by us, Blessed One, they quickly fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect awakening."

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ śakraṃ devānāmindramāmantrayate sma tena hi kauśika śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te yathā bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyam
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> addressed <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "In that case, <s>Kauśika</s>, listen, and attend well and carefully; I shall tell you how a bodhisattva, a great being, should stand in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: śūnyatāyāṃ kauśika tiṣṭhatā bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyam
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, standing in emptiness should stand in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tena hi kauśika bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhena bhavitavyam
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, should be one who is armed with the great armor.

children.text: na rūpe sthātavyam
children.translated_text: He should not stand in form.

children.text: na vedanāyāṃ na saṃjñāyāṃ na saṃskāreṣu
children.translated_text: He should not stand in feeling, perception, or formations.

children.text: na vijñāne sthātavyam
children.translated_text: He should not stand in consciousness.

children.text: na cakṣuṣi sthātavyam
children.translated_text: He should not stand in the eye.

children.text: na rūpe sthātavyam
children.translated_text: He should not stand in visible form.

children.text: na cakṣurvijñāne sthātavyam
children.translated_text: He should not stand in eye-consciousness.

children.text: na cakṣuḥsaṃsparśe sthātavyam
children.translated_text: He should not stand in eye-contact.

children.text: na cakṣuḥsaṃsparśajāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ sthātavyam
children.translated_text: He should not stand in feeling born from eye-contact.

children.text: evaṃ na śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanaḥsu sthātavyam
children.translated_text: Likewise, he should not stand in the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.

children.text: na śabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmeṣu na śrotravijñāne yāvanna manovijñāne
children.translated_text: He should not stand in sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or dharmas; not in ear-consciousness, down to not in mind-consciousness.

children.text: na manaḥsaṃsparśe na manaḥsaṃsparśajāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ sthātavyam
children.translated_text: He should not stand in mind-contact or in feeling born from mind-contact.

children.text: na pṛthivīdhātau sthātavyam
children.translated_text: He should not stand in the earth element.

children.text: nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau nākāśadhātau na vijñānadhātau sthātavyam
children.translated_text: He should not stand in the water element, the fire element, the wind element, the space element, or the consciousness element.

children.text: na smṛtyupasthāneṣu sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in the establishments of mindfulness.

children.text: na samyakprahāṇarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgeṣu na mārgāṅgeṣu sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in the right efforts, bases of supernormal power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, or factors of the path.

children.text: na srotaāpattiphale sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in the fruit of stream-entry.

children.text: na sakṛdāgāmiphale na anāgāmiphale nārhattve sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in the fruit of once-returning, in the fruit of non-returning, or in arhatship.

children.text: na pratyekabuddhatve sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in pratyekabuddhahood.

children.text: na buddhatve sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in buddhahood.

children.text: iti hi rūpamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'This indeed is form.'

children.text: iti hi vedaneti saṃjñeti saṃskārā iti
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'This indeed is feeling, this is perception, these are formations,'

children.text: iti hi vijñānamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: one should not abide thinking, 'This indeed is consciousness.'

children.text: iti hi cakṣuriti yāvanmanaḥsaṃsparśajā vedaneti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'This indeed is the eye,' and so on up to 'feeling born from contact with the mind.'

children.text: iti hi pṛthivīdhāturiti yāvadvijñānadhāturiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'This indeed is the earth element,' and so on up to 'the consciousness element.'

children.text: iti hi smṛtyupasthānānīti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'These indeed are the establishments of mindfulness.'

children.text: iti hi samyakprahāṇarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgānīti iti hi mārgāṅgānīti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'These indeed are the right efforts, bases of supernormal power, faculties, powers, and factors of awakening,' or 'these indeed are the factors of the path.'

children.text: iti hi srotaāpattiphalamiti na sthātavyam iti hi sakṛdāgāmiphalamiti anāgāmiphalamiti arhattvamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'This indeed is the fruit of stream-entry'; one should not abide thinking, 'This indeed is the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or arhatship.'

children.text: iti hi pratyekabuddhatvamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'This indeed is pratyekabuddhahood.'

children.text: iti hi buddhatvamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'This indeed is buddhahood.'

children.text: rūpaṃ nityamanityamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in form as permanent or impermanent.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: vijñānaṃ nityamanityamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in consciousness as permanent or impermanent.

children.text: rūpaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in form as pleasure or pain.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: vijñānaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in consciousness as pleasure or pain.

children.text: rūpaṃ śūnyamaśūnyamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in form as empty or not empty.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: vijñānaṃ śūnyamaśūnyamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in consciousness as empty or not empty.

children.text: rūpamātmānātmeti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in form as self or not-self.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: vijñānamātmānātmeti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in consciousness as self or not-self.

children.text: rūpaṃ śubhamaśubhamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in form as pure or impure.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: vijñānaṃ śubhamaśubhamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide in consciousness as pure or impure.

children.text: rūpaṃ śūnyamupalabhyate veti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'Form is apprehended as empty.'

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: vijñānaṃ śūnyamupalabhyate veti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'Consciousness is apprehended as empty.'

children.text: srotaāpattiphalamasaṃskṛtaprabhāvitamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking that the fruit of stream-entry is brought about by the unconditioned.

children.text: evaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalamanāgāmiphalamarhattvamasaṃskṛtaprabhāvitamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: So too, one should not abide thinking that the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or arhatship is brought about by the unconditioned.

children.text: pratyekabuddhatvamasaṃskṛtaprabhāvitamiti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking that pratyekabuddhahood is brought about by the unconditioned.

children.text: srotaāpanno dakṣiṇīya iti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'A stream-enterer is worthy of offerings.'

children.text: srotaāpannāḥ saptakṛto bhavaparamā iti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'Stream-enterers have at most seven more births.'

children.text: sakṛdāgāmī dakṣiṇīya iti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'A once-returner is worthy of offerings.'

children.text: sakṛdāgāmyapariniṣṭhitatvāt sakṛd imaṃ lokam āgamya duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyatīti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'Because a once-returner has not yet reached completion, after coming once to this world he will make an end of suffering.'

children.text: anāgāmī dakṣiṇīya iti na sthātavyam anāgāmī anāgamya imaṃ lokaṃ tatraiva parinirvāsyatīti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'A non-returner is worthy of offerings'; one should not abide thinking, 'A non-returner, without coming back to this world, will attain final nirvāṇa right there.'

children.text: arhan dakṣiṇīya iti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'An arhat is worthy of offerings.'

children.text: arhannihaiva anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāsyatīti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'An arhat will here itself attain final nirvāṇa in the nirvāṇa element without remainder of clinging.'

children.text: pratyekabuddho dakṣiṇīya iti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'A pratyekabuddha is worthy of offerings.'

children.text: pratyekabuddho 'tikramya śrāvakabhūmim aprāpya buddhabhūmiṃ parinirvāsyatīti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'A pratyekabuddha, having gone beyond the disciple-ground and without reaching the buddha-ground, will attain final nirvāṇa.'

children.text: buddho dakṣiṇīya iti na sthātavyam
children.translated_text: One should not abide thinking, 'A Buddha is worthy of offerings.'

children.text: buddho 'tikramya pṛthagjanabhūmimatikramya śrāvakabhūmimatikramya pratyekabuddhabhūmim aprameyāṇām asaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmarthaṃ kṛtvā aprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi parinirvāpya aprameyānasaṃkhyeyān sattvān śrāvakapratyekabuddhasamyaksaṃbuddhatvaniyatān kṛtvā buddhabhūmau sthitvā buddhakṛtyaṃ kṛtvā anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau buddhaparinirvāṇena parinirvāsyati ityevamapyanena na sthātavyam ||
children.translated_text: Even in this way one should not abide: 'A Buddha, having gone beyond the ground of ordinary persons, having gone beyond the disciple-ground, having gone beyond the pratyekabuddha-ground, having acted for the benefit of immeasurable and countless beings, having brought immeasurable and countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis and niyutas of beings to final nirvāṇa, having made immeasurable and countless beings destined for discipleship, pratyekabuddhahood, and complete buddhahood, having stood on the buddha-ground and done the work of a Buddha, will attain final nirvāṇa by the final nirvāṇa of a Buddha in the nirvāṇa element without remainder of clinging.'

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitadabhavat yadi buddho 'tikramya pṛthagjanabhūmimatikramya śrāvakabhūmimatikramya pratyekabuddhabhūmimaprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmarthaṃ kṛtvā aprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi parinirvāpya aprameyānasaṃkhyeyān sattvān śrāvakapratyekabuddhasamyaksaṃbuddhatvaniyatān kṛtvā buddhabhūmau sthitvā buddhakṛtyaṃ kṛtvā anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau buddhaparinirvāṇena parinirvāsyati ityevamapyanena na sthātavyam tatkathaṃ punaranena sthātavyaṃ kathaṃ śikṣitavyamiti atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbuddhānubhāvena āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat tatkiṃ manyase āyuṣman śāriputra kva tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sthitaḥ āyuṣmān śāriputra āha na kvacidāyuṣman subhūte tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'If even in this way one should not abide, that a Buddha, having gone beyond the ground of ordinary persons, having gone beyond the disciple-ground, having gone beyond the pratyekabuddha-ground, having acted for the benefit of immeasurable and countless beings, having brought immeasurable and countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis and niyutas of beings to final nirvāṇa, having made immeasurable and countless beings destined for discipleship, pratyekabuddhahood, and complete buddhahood, having stood on the buddha-ground and done the work of a Buddha, will attain final nirvāṇa by the final nirvāṇa of a Buddha in the nirvāṇa element without remainder of clinging, then how should one abide in this? How should one train?' Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, through the Buddha's power, knew with his own mind the thought in the mind of the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'What do you think, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>? Where does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, abide?' The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Nowhere, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, abide.'

children.text: tatkasya hetor apratiṣṭhitamānaso hi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? For the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, has a mind that is not established.

children.text: sa naiva saṃskṛte dhātau sthito nāpyasaṃskṛte dhātau sthito na ca tato vyutthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is not stationed in the conditioned element, nor is he stationed in the unconditioned element, and he has not risen up from that.

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat evameva āyuṣman śāriputra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sthātavyam evaṃ śikṣitavyam yathā tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho na kvacitsthito nāsthito na viṣṭhito nāviṣṭhitaḥ tathā sthāsyāmītyevamanena śikṣitavyam
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Just so, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, should stand thus and train thus: 'As the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one, is not standing anywhere, is not not-standing, is not distinctly standing, and is not distinctly not-standing, so I shall stand.' Thus should he train.

children.text: yathā tathāgatasthānaṃ tathā sthāsyāmīti tathā śikṣiṣye iti yathā tathāgatasthānaṃ tathā sthāsyāmīti tathā śikṣiṣye iti yathā tathāgatasthānaṃ tathā sthāsyāmīti susthito 'sthānayogeneti evamatra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sthātavyamevaṃ śikṣitavyam
children.translated_text: 'As is the standing of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, so shall I stand; thus I shall train. As is the standing of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, so shall I stand; thus I shall train. As is the standing of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, so shall I stand.' In this way, well stationed through the discipline of non-station, a bodhisattva, a great being, should stand here and should train thus.

children.text: evaṃ hi śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo viharatyanena prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa avirahitaścānena manasikāreṇeti ||
children.translated_text: For while training in this way, the bodhisattva, the great being, dwells in this dwelling of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and is not separated from this attention.

children.text: atha khalu tatra parṣadi keṣāṃciddevaputrāṇāmetadabhūt yāni tāni yakṣāṇāṃ yakṣabhāṣitāni yakṣarutāni yakṣapadāni yakṣamantritāni yakṣapravyāhṛtāni tāni vijñāyante jalpyamānāni
children.translated_text: Then it occurred to some devaputras in that assembly: "Those utterances of yakṣas, those sounds of yakṣas, those words of yakṣas, those counsels of yakṣas, those pronouncements of yakṣas, are understood when they are spoken,

children.text: na punaridaṃ vijñāyate yatsubhūtiḥ sthaviro bhāṣate pravyāharati deśayatyupadiśati
children.translated_text: "but this that the elder <s>Subhūti</s> speaks, utters, teaches, and instructs is not understood."

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbuddhānubhāvena teṣāṃ devaputrāṇāmimamevaṃrūpaṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya tān devaputrānāmantrayate sma na vijñāyate na vijñāyate idaṃ devaputrāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, through the power of the Buddha, knew with his own mind this very thought in the minds of those devaputras and addressed those devaputras: "It is not understood, it is not understood, devaputras.

children.text: tathā hi nātra kiṃcitsūcyate nātra kiṃcit śrūyate ||
children.translated_text: For here nothing at all is indicated; here nothing at all is heard."

children.text: atha khalu teṣāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ punarevaitadabhūt uttānīkariṣyati bata ayamāryasubhūtiḥ
children.translated_text: Then once again it occurred to those devaputras: "Surely this noble <s>Subhūti</s> will make it plain.

children.text: uttānīkariṣyati batāyamāryasubhūtiriti
children.translated_text: Surely this noble <s>Subhūti</s> will make it plain."

children.text: dūrāddūrataramāryasubhūtiḥ praviśati sūkṣmātsūkṣmataram
children.translated_text: "Noble <s>Subhūti</s> is entering from far into still farther, from subtle into still subtler.

children.text: gambhīrād gambhīrataram āryasubhūtiḥ praviśati deśayati bhāṣata iti
children.translated_text: Noble <s>Subhūti</s> is entering, teaching, and speaking from deep into still deeper."

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbuddhānubhāvena punar api teṣāmeva devaputrāṇāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya tān devaputrānāmantrayate sma tena hi devaputrāḥ yaḥ srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptukāmaḥ srotaāpattiphale sthātukāmaḥ sa nemāṃ kṣāntim anāgamya peyālam
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, again through the power of the Buddha, knew with his own mind the thought in the minds of those same devaputras and addressed them: "Therefore, devaputras, whoever wishes to attain the fruit of stream-entry and wishes to stand in the fruit of stream-entry cannot do so without coming to this kṣānti (patient acceptance), and so on.

children.text: yaḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptukāmaḥ sakṛdāgāmiphale sthātukāmaḥ yo 'nāgāmiphalaṃ prāptukāmo 'nāgāmiphale sthātukāmaḥ yo 'rhattvaṃ prāptukāmo 'rhattve sthātukāmaḥ yaḥ pratyekabodhiṃ prāptukāmaḥ pratyekabodhau sthātukāmaḥ sa nemāṃ kṣāntim anāgamya
children.translated_text: Whoever wishes to attain the fruit of once-returning and wishes to stand in the fruit of once-returning, whoever wishes to attain the fruit of non-returning and wishes to stand in the fruit of non-returning, whoever wishes to attain arhatship and wishes to stand in arhatship, whoever wishes to attain pratyekabodhi and wishes to stand in pratyekabodhi, cannot do so without coming to this kṣānti.

children.text: yo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ prāptukāmo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau sthātukāmaḥ sa nemāṃ kṣāntim anāgamya ||
children.translated_text: Whoever wishes to attain unsurpassed perfect awakening and wishes to stand in unsurpassed perfect awakening cannot do so without coming to this kṣānti."

children.text: atha khalu punar api teṣāṃ devaputrāṇāmetadabhavat kiṃrūpā asya āryasubhūter dhārmaśravaṇikā eṣṭavyāḥ atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbuddhānubhāvena teṣāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya tān devaputrānāmantrayate sma māyānirmitasadṛśā hi devaputrā mama dhārmaśravaṇikā eṣṭavyāḥ
children.translated_text: Then once again it occurred to those devaputras: "What sort of Dharma-hearers should be sought for this noble <s>Subhūti</s>?" Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, through the power of the Buddha, knew with his own mind the thought in the minds of those devaputras and addressed them: "Devaputras, my Dharma-hearers should be sought as resembling magical creations.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi te naiva śroṣyanti na ca sākṣātkariṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? For they will neither hear nor directly realize."

children.text: atha khalu te devaputrā āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocan kiṃ punarārya subhūte māyopamāste sattvā na te māyā evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtistān devaputrānetadavocat māyopamāste devaputrāḥ sattvāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those devaputras said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "But, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, are beings comparable to illusion, and are they not illusion?" When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to those devaputras: "Devaputras, beings are comparable to illusion.

children.text: svapnopamāste devaputrāḥ sattvāḥ
children.translated_text: Devaputras, beings are comparable to dream.

children.text: iti hi māyā ca sattvāś ca advayametad advaidhīkāram iti hi svapnaś ca sattvāś ca advayam etad advaidhīkāram
children.translated_text: Thus illusion and beings are non-dual; this is without making a duality. Thus dream and beings are non-dual; this is without making a duality.

children.text: sarvadharmā api devaputrā māyopamāḥ svapnopamāḥ
children.translated_text: All dharmas too, devaputras, are comparable to illusion and comparable to dream.

children.text: srotaāpanno 'pi māyopamaḥ svapnopamaḥ
children.translated_text: A stream-enterer too is comparable to illusion and comparable to dream.

children.text: srotaāpattiphalam api māyopamaṃ svapnopamam
children.translated_text: The fruit of stream-entry too is comparable to illusion and comparable to dream.

children.text: evaṃ sakṛdāgāmy api sakṛdāgāmiphalamapi anāgāmy api anāgāmiphalamapi arhann api arhattvam api māyopamaṃ svapnopamam
children.translated_text: So too a once-returner and the fruit of once-returning, a non-returner and the fruit of non-returning, an arhat and arhatship, are comparable to illusion and comparable to dream.

children.text: pratyekabuddho 'pi māyopamaḥ svapnopamaḥ
children.translated_text: A pratyekabuddha too is comparable to illusion and comparable to dream.

children.text: pratyekabuddhatvam api māyopamaṃ svapnopamam
children.translated_text: Pratyekabuddhahood too is comparable to illusion and comparable to dream.

children.text: samyaksaṃbuddho 'pi māyopamaḥ svapnopamaḥ
children.translated_text: A perfectly awakened Buddha too is comparable to illusion and comparable to dream.

children.text: samyaksaṃbuddhatvam api māyopamaṃ svapnopamam
children.translated_text: Perfect buddhahood too is comparable to illusion and comparable to dream."

children.text: atha khalu devaputrā āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocan samyaksaṃbuddho 'pyārya subhūte māyopamaḥ svapnopama iti vadasi samyaksaṃbuddhatvam api māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadasi subhūtirāha nirvāṇam api devaputrā māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadāmi kiṃ punaranyaṃ dharmam
children.translated_text: Then the devaputras said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, do you say that even a perfectly awakened Buddha is comparable to illusion and comparable to dream? Do you say that perfect buddhahood too is comparable to illusion and comparable to dream?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Devaputras, I say that even nirvāṇa is comparable to illusion and comparable to dream; what then of any other dharma?"

children.text: te devaputrā āhuḥ nirvāṇamapyārya subhūte māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadasi āyuṣmān subhūtirāha tadyadi devaputrā nirvāṇādapyanyaḥ kaściddharmo viśiṣṭataraḥ syāt tamapyahaṃ māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadeyam
children.translated_text: The devaputras said, "Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, do you say that even nirvāṇa is like an illusion, like a dream?" Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said, "Devaputras, if there were any dharma more excellent even than nirvāṇa, I would say that too is like an illusion, like a dream."

children.text: iti hi devaputrā māyā ca nirvāṇaṃ ca advayam etad advaidhīkāram
children.translated_text: For, devaputras, illusion and nirvāṇa are nondual; this is free from dualization.

children.text: iti hi svapnaś ca nirvāṇaṃ ca advayam etad advaidhīkāram ||
children.translated_text: For dream and nirvāṇa are nondual; this is free from dualization.

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputraḥ āyuṣmāṃś ca pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputraḥ āyuṣmāṃś ca mahākoṣṭhilaḥ āyuṣmāṃś ca mahākātyāyanaḥ āyuṣmāṃś ca mahākāśyapaḥ anye ca mahāśrāvakā anekairbodhisattvasahasraiḥ sārdhamāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃ sthaviramāmantrayante sma ke 'syā āyuṣman subhūte prajñāpāramitāyā evaṃ nirdiśyamānāyāḥ pratyeṣakā bhaviṣyanti atha khalvāyuṣmānānandastān sthavirānetadavocat te khalvāyuṣmanto veditavyā avinivartanīyā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ dṛṣṭisampannā vā pudgalāḥ arhanto vā kṣīṇāsravāḥ ye 'syāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā evaṃ nirdiśyamānāyāḥ pratyeṣakā bhaviṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākoṣṭhila</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, and other great disciples, together with many thousands of bodhisattvas, addressed the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s>: "Who, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, will seek out this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> when it is being taught in this way?" Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to those elders: "Venerable ones, those who will seek out this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> when it is being taught in this way should be known as irreversible bodhisattvas, great beings, or as persons endowed with right view, or as arhats whose outflows are exhausted."

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ sthavirastān sthavirānetadavocat nāsyā āyuṣmantaḥ prajñāpāramitāyā evaṃ nirdiśyamānāyāḥ kecitpratyeṣakā bhaviṣyanti
children.translated_text: Then the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s> said this to those elders: "Venerable ones, no one will seek out this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> when it is being taught in this way.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi atra na kaściddharmaḥ sūcyate na kaściddharmaḥ paridīpyate na kaściddharmaḥ prajñapyate
children.translated_text: Why is that? For here no dharma is pointed out, no dharma is illuminated, and no dharma is designated.

children.text: tadyathaivātra na kaściddharmaḥ sūcyate na kaściddharmaḥ paridīpyate na kaściddharmaḥ prajñapyate tathaivāsyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā evaṃ nirdiśyamānāyā na kaścitpratyeṣako bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Just as here no dharma is pointed out, no dharma is illuminated, and no dharma is designated, so too, when this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is taught in this way, there will be no one who seeks it out."

children.text: atha khalu śakrasya devānāmindrasyaitadabhūt asya dharmaparyāyasya āryeṇa subhūtinā bhāṣyamāṇasya pūjārthaṃ yannvahaṃ puṣpāṇyabhinirmāya āryaṃ subhūtimabhyavakireyamiti
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "While this dharma-teaching is being spoken by noble <s>Subhūti</s>, I should create flowers and scatter them over noble <s>Subhūti</s> for the sake of worship."

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindrastasyāṃ velāyāṃ puṣpāṇyabhinirmāya āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimabhyavākirat
children.translated_text: Then at that time <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, created flowers and scattered them over the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>.

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmataḥ subhūteḥ sthavirasya śakraṃ devānāmindramanuvyāharaṇāyaitadabhūt na khalu punarimāni puṣpāṇi mayā trāyastriṃśeṣu deveṣu pracaranti dṛṣṭapūrvāṇi yānīmāni śakreṇa devānāmindreṇa abhyavakīrṇāni
children.translated_text: Then, in order to respond to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, this thought occurred to the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s>: "I certainly have never before seen among the Trāyastriṃśa gods such flowers as these that have been scattered by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

children.text: nirmitānyetāni puṣpāṇi
children.translated_text: These flowers are magically created.

children.text: naitāni puṣpāṇi vṛkṣagulmalatānirjātāni yāni śakreṇa devānāmindreṇābhyavakīrṇāni manomayānyetāni puṣpāṇīti
children.translated_text: These flowers that have been scattered by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, have not arisen from trees, shrubs, or creepers; these flowers are mind-made."

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmataḥ subhūteścetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat anirjātānyetānyārya subhūte puṣpāṇi
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, knowing with his own mind the thought in the mind of the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, these flowers are unborn.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ na hi manonirjātāni kānicitpuṣpāṇi nāpi vṛkṣagulmalatānirjātāni
children.translated_text: Why is that? For there are no flowers produced from mind, nor any produced from trees, shrubs, or creepers."

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat yattvaṃ kauśika evaṃ vadasi anirjātānyetāni puṣpāṇi naitāni manonirjātāni nāpi vṛkṣagulmalatānirjātānīti
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "<s>Kauśika</s>, as you say, 'These flowers are unborn; they are not produced from mind, nor produced from trees, shrubs, or creepers,'

children.text: yatkauśika anirjātaṃ na tatpuṣpam
children.translated_text: what is unborn, <s>Kauśika</s>, is not a flower."

children.text: atha khalu śakrasya devānāmindrasyaitadabhūt gambhīraprajño batāyamāryaḥ subhūtiḥ
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "This noble <s>Subhūti</s> is indeed of profound wisdom.

children.text: tāṃ ca nāma padaprajñaptiṃ nirdiśati tāṃ ca na virodhayati tāṃ cottānīkaroti tāmeva copadiśati
children.translated_text: He teaches that very verbal designation, and he does not contradict it; he makes it clear, and he instructs in that very thing."

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmataṃ subhūtimetadavocat evametadārya subhūte evam etat
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "So it is, noble <s>Subhūti</s>; so it is.

children.text: evaṃ cātra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śikṣitavyaṃ yathā āryasubhūtirupadiśati
children.translated_text: A bodhisattva, a great being, should train here in just the way noble <s>Subhūti</s> instructs."

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtiḥ śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat evametatkauśika evam etat
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>; so it is.

children.text: evamatra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śikṣitavyam
children.translated_text: A bodhisattva, a great being, should train here in this way.

children.text: evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ kauśika bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na srotaāpattiphale śikṣate na sakṛdāgāmiphale na anāgāmiphale nārhattve śikṣate na pratyekabuddhatve śikṣate na buddhatve śikṣate
children.translated_text: Training in this way, <s>Kauśika</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, does not train in the fruit of stream-entry, nor in the fruit of once-returning, nor in the fruit of non-returning, nor in arhatship, nor in pratyekabuddhahood, nor in buddhahood.

children.text: yo nāsu bhūmiṣu śikṣate sa buddhatve sarvajñatve vā śikṣate
children.translated_text: One who does not train in these levels trains in buddhahood or in omniscience.

children.text: yo buddhatve sarvajñatve vā śikṣate so 'prameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu buddhadharmeṣu śikṣate
children.translated_text: One who trains in buddhahood or in omniscience trains in immeasurable, countless buddha-dharmas.

children.text: yo 'prameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu buddhadharmeṣu śikṣate sa na rūpasya vivṛddhaye śikṣate na parihāṇāya
children.translated_text: One who trains in immeasurable, countless buddha-dharmas does not train for the increase of form, nor for its decrease.

children.text: evaṃ sa na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārāṇām
children.translated_text: In the same way, he does not train for the increase or decrease of feeling, perception, or formations.

children.text: sa na vijñānasya vivṛddhaye śikṣate na parihāṇāya
children.translated_text: He does not train for the increase of consciousness, nor for its decrease.

children.text: yo na rūpasya vivṛddhaye śikṣate na parihāṇāya
children.translated_text: One who does not train for the increase of form, nor for its decrease,

children.text: evaṃ na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārāṇām
children.translated_text: likewise does not train for the increase or decrease of feeling, perception, or formations.

children.text: yo na vijñānasya vivṛddhaye śikṣate na parihāṇāya sa na rūpasya parigrahāya śikṣate notsargāya
children.translated_text: One who does not train for the increase of consciousness, nor for its diminution, does not train for the grasping of form, nor for its abandonment.

children.text: evaṃ sa na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārāṇām
children.translated_text: Thus he does not train for grasping or abandonment with regard to feeling, perception, or formations.

children.text: sa na vijñānasya parigrahāya śikṣate notsargāya nāpi kasyaciddharmasya parigrahāya śikṣate notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate
children.translated_text: He does not train for the grasping of consciousness, nor for its abandonment; nor does he train for the grasping of any <s>dharma</s>, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance.

children.text: yo na kasyaciddharmasya parigrahāya śikṣate notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate sa na sarvajñatāyā api parigrahāya śikṣate notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate
children.translated_text: One who does not train for the grasping of any <s>dharma</s>, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance, does not train even for the grasping of omniscience, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance.

children.text: evaṃ śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣate sarvajñatāyāṃ niryāsyati ||
children.translated_text: Training in this way, a bodhisattva, a great being, trains in omniscience and will go forth into omniscience.

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat ya āyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na kasyaciddharmasya parigrahāya śikṣate notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate sa na sarvajñatāyā api parigrahāya śikṣate notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the bodhisattva, the great being, who does not train for the grasping of any <s>dharma</s>, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance, does not train even for the grasping of omniscience, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance.

children.text: evaṃ śikṣamāṇa āyuṣmān subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣate sarvajñatāyāṃ niryāsyati ||
children.translated_text: Training in this way, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, trains in omniscience and will go forth into omniscience."

children.text: āyuṣmān subhūtirāha evametadāyuṣman śāriputra evam etat
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said: "So it is, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>; so it is.

children.text: ya āyuṣman śāriputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na kasyaciddharmasya parigrahāya śikṣate notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate sa na sarvajñatāyā api parigrahāya śikṣate notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate
children.translated_text: Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the bodhisattva, the great being, who does not train for the grasping of any <s>dharma</s>, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance, does not train even for the grasping of omniscience, nor for its arising, nor for its disappearance.

children.text: sarvabuddhadharmāṇām api na parigrahāya śikṣate notpādāya nāntardhānāya śikṣate
children.translated_text: He does not train even for the grasping of all the Buddha-dharmas, nor for their arising, nor for their disappearance.

children.text: evaṃ cāyuṣman śāriputra śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣate sarvajñatāyāṃ niryāsyati ||
children.translated_text: And training in this way, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, trains in omniscience and will go forth into omniscience."

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat prajñāpāramitā ārya śāriputra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena kuto gaveṣitavyāḥ śāriputra āha prajñāpāramitā kauśika bodhisattvena mahāsattvena āyuṣmataḥ subhūteḥ parivartād gaveṣitavyā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, where should <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (the perfection of wisdom) be sought by a bodhisattva, a great being?" <s>Śāriputra</s> said: "<s>Kauśika</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> should be sought by a bodhisattva, a great being, from the exposition of the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>."

children.text: evamukte śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat kasyaiṣa ārya śāriputra anubhāvo veditavyaḥ kasyaitadadhiṣṭhānaṃ veditavyaṃ yadāryasubhūtiḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣate āyuṣmān śāriputra āha tathāgatasyaiṣa kauśika anubhāvo veditavyaḥ
children.translated_text: When this had been said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, whose power should this be understood to be, whose sustaining force should this be understood to be, that the noble <s>Subhūti</s> speaks <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>?" The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said: "<s>Kauśika</s>, this should be understood as the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tathāgatasyaitadadhiṣṭhānaṃ veditavyaṃ yadāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣate
children.translated_text: It should be understood as the sustaining force of the <s>Tathāgata</s> that the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> speaks <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>."

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat yatkauśika evaṃ vadasi kasyaiṣo 'nubhāvo veditavyaḥ kasyaitadanuṣṭhānaṃ veditavyaṃ yadāryasubhūtiḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣate iti tathāgatasyaiṣa kauśika anubhāvo veditavyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "<s>Kauśika</s>, as to what you say, 'Whose power should this be understood to be, whose support should this be understood to be, that the noble <s>Subhūti</s> speaks <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>?', this should be understood as the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tathāgatasyaitadadhiṣṭhānaṃ veditavyaṃ yadahaṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣe
children.translated_text: It should be understood as the sustaining force of the <s>Tathāgata</s> that I speak <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: yad api kauśika evaṃ vadasi prajñāpāramitā bodhisattvena mahāsattvena kuto gaveṣitavyeti prajñāpāramitā kauśika bodhisattvena mahāsattvena na rūpādgaveṣitavyā nāpyanyatra rūpād gaveṣitavyā
children.translated_text: And as to what you say, <s>Kauśika</s>, 'Where should <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> be sought by a bodhisattva, a great being?', <s>Kauśika</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> should not be sought by a bodhisattva, a great being, from form, nor apart from form.

children.text: evaṃ na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārebhyaḥ na vijñānād gaveṣitavyāḥ nāpyanyatra vijñānād gaveṣitavyā
children.translated_text: Thus it should not be sought from feeling, from perception, from formations, or from consciousness, nor apart from consciousness.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi na rūpaṃ prajñāpāramitā nāpyanyatra rūpātprajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Why is that? For form is not <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, nor is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> apart from form.

children.text: evaṃ na vedanā na saṃjñā na saṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus feeling is not, perception is not, and formations are not <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na vijñānaṃ prajñāpāramitā nāpyanyatra vijñānātprajñāpāramitā ||
children.translated_text: Consciousness is not <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, nor is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> apart from consciousness."

children.text: evamukte śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat mahāpāramiteyamārya subhūte yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: When this had been said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is a great perfection.

children.text: apramāṇapāramiteyamārya subhūte yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is an immeasurable perfection.

children.text: aparimāṇapāramiteyamārya subhūte yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is an incalculable perfection.

children.text: anantapāramiteyamārya subhūte yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is an endless perfection."

children.text: sthaviraḥ subhūtirāha evametatkauśika evam etat
children.translated_text: The elder <s>Subhūti</s> said: "So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>; so it is.

children.text: mahāpāramiteyaṃ kauśika yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is a great perfection.

children.text: apramāṇapāramiteyaṃ kauśika yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is an immeasurable perfection.

children.text: aparimāṇapāramiteyaṃ kauśika yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is an incalculable perfection.

children.text: anantapāramiteyaṃ kauśika yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is an endless perfection.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ rūpamahattayā hi kauśika mahāpāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because of the greatness of form, <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is a great perfection.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
