children.translated_text: Thus because of the greatness of feeling, perception, and formations, it is a great perfection.

children.text: vijñānamahattayā hi kauśika mahāpāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Because of the greatness of consciousness, <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is a great perfection.

children.text: rūpāpramāṇatayā kauśika apramāṇapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Because of the immeasurability of form, <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is an immeasurable perfection.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus because of the immeasurability of feeling, perception, and formations, it is an immeasurable perfection.

children.text: vijñānāpramāṇatayā kauśika apramāṇapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Because of the immeasurability of consciousness, <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is an immeasurable perfection.

children.text: rūpāparimāṇatayā kauśika aparimāṇapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Because form is immeasurable, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an immeasurable perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: vijñānāparimāṇatayā kauśika aparimāṇapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Because consciousness is immeasurable, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an immeasurable perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: rūpānantatayā kauśika anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Because form is infinite, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: vijñānānantatayā kauśika anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Because consciousness is infinite, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ mahāpāramiteti kauśika nābhiniviśate
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Kauśika</s>, one does not settle upon it as a great perfection.

children.text: evamapramāṇapāramiteti evamaparimāṇapāramiteti evamanantapāramiteti nābhiniviśate
children.translated_text: Thus one does not settle upon it as a measureless perfection, thus as an immeasurable perfection, thus as an infinite perfection.

children.text: tasmātkauśika mahāpāramiteyam apramāṇapāramiteyam aparimāṇapāramiteyam anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is a great perfection, a measureless perfection, an immeasurable perfection, an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: ārambaṇānantatayā kauśika anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Because its objects are infinite, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: sattvānantatayā kauśika anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Because beings are infinite, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ kauśika ārambaṇānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā sarvadharmāṇāṃ hi kauśika yato nānto na madhyaṃ na paryavasānamupalabhyate tataḥ kauśika anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Kauśika</s>, is it an infinite perfection because its objects are infinite, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>? Since, <s>Kauśika</s>, no end, no middle, and no conclusion of all dharmas is found, therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: anena kauśika paryāyeṇa ārambaṇānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: In this way, <s>Kauśika</s>, because its objects are infinite, this is an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yasmātsarvadharmā anantā aparyantāḥ na teṣāmanto vā madhyaṃ vā paryavasānaṃ vā upalabhyate tasmātkauśika anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, because all dharmas are infinite and boundless, and because no end, middle, or conclusion of them is found, therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ rūpasya hi kauśika nānto na madhyaṃ na paryavasānamupalabhyate
children.translated_text: Why is that? For, <s>Kauśika</s>, no end, no middle, and no conclusion of form is found.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām
children.translated_text: So too of feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: vijñānasya hi kauśika nānto na madhyaṃ na paryavasānamupalabhyate
children.translated_text: For, <s>Kauśika</s>, no end, no middle, and no conclusion of consciousness is found.

children.text: anenāpi kauśika paryāyeṇa ārambaṇānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā ||
children.translated_text: By this method too, <s>Kauśika</s>, because its objects are infinite, this is an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika sattvo 'nanto 'paryantaḥ
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, a being is infinite and boundless.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ na hi sattvasyānto vā madhyaṃ vā paryavasānaṃ vopalabhyate
children.translated_text: Why is that? For no end, middle, or conclusion of a being is found.

children.text: tasmātkauśika sattvānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, because beings are infinite, this is an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat kathamāyuṣman subhūte sattvānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā sthaviraḥ subhūtirāha na hi kauśika gaṇanāyogena vā gaṇanābahutvena vā sattvānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "How, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, because beings are infinite, is this an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>?" The elder <s>Subhūti</s> said: "It is not, <s>Kauśika</s>, by the method of counting or by the great number counted that, because beings are infinite, this is an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>."

children.text: śakra āha kathaṃ tarhīdānīmārya subhūte sattvānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā sthaviraḥ subhūtirāha tatkaṃ manyase kauśika katamasyaitaddharmasyādhivacanaṃ yaduta sattvaḥ sattva iti śakra āha naitadārya subhūte dharmasyādhivacanaṃ na adharmādhivacanaṃ yaduta sattvaḥ sattva iti
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: "How then, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, because beings are infinite, is this an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>?" The elder <s>Subhūti</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Of what dharma is this a designation, namely 'being, being'?" <s>Śakra</s> said: "This, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, is not a designation of a dharma, nor a designation of a non-dharma, namely 'being, being.'"

children.text: āgantukametannāmadheyaṃ prakṣiptam
children.translated_text: This name has been introduced as something adventitious.

children.text: avastukametannāmadheyaṃ prakṣiptam
children.translated_text: This name has been introduced as without a real basis.

children.text: anātmīyam etannāmadheyaṃ prakṣiptam
children.translated_text: This name has been introduced as not belonging to a self.

children.text: anārambaṇametannāmadheyaṃ prakṣiptaṃ yaduta sattvaḥ sattva iti
children.translated_text: This name has been introduced as without an object, namely 'being, being.'

children.text: sthaviraḥ subhūtirāha tatkiṃ manyase kauśika kācidatra sattvaparidīpanā kṛtā śakra āha no hīdamārya subhūte
children.translated_text: The elder <s>Subhūti</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Has any indication of a being been made here?" <s>Śakra</s> said: "No indeed, noble <s>Subhūti</s>."

children.text: subhūtirāha yatra kauśika na kācitsattvaparidīpanā kṛtā tatra kā sattvānantatā sacetkauśika tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho 'nantavijñaptighoṣeṇa gambhīranirghoṣeṇa svareṇa gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpān api vitiṣṭhamānaḥ sattvaḥ sattva iti vācaṃ bhāṣeta api nu tatra kaścitsattva utpanno va utpatsyate vā utpadyate vā niruddho vā nirotsyate vā nirudhyate vā śakra āha no hīdamārya subhūte
children.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Where, <s>Kauśika</s>, no indication of any being has been made, what infinity of beings is there? If, <s>Kauśika</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one, standing firm even for kalpas like the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, were to utter the word 'being, being' with a voice of infinite proclamation and deep resonance, would any being there have arisen, or be going to arise, or be arising, or have ceased, or be going to cease, or be ceasing?" <s>Śakra</s> said: "No indeed, noble <s>Subhūti</s>."

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ ādiśuddhatvādādipariśuddhatvātsattvasya
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because a being is originally pure and pure from the beginning.

children.text: subhūtirāha anenāpi kauśika paryāyeṇa evaṃ sattvānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: "By this method too, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this way, because beings are infinite, this is an infinite perfection, namely <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ ca punaḥ kauśika sattvānantatayā prajñāpāramitānantatā veditavyā ||
children.translated_text: And again in this way, <s>Kauśika</s>, because beings are infinite, the infinity of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood."

children.text: atha khalu sendrakā devāḥ sabrahmakāḥ saprajāpatikāḥ sarṣinaranārīgaṇās trirudānam udānayanti sma aho dharmaḥ aho dharmaḥ aho dharmasya dharmatā
children.translated_text: Then the gods together with <s>Indra</s>, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, together with <s>Prajāpati</s>, and with assemblies of seers, men, and women, uttered a threefold exclamation: "Ah, the dharma! Ah, the dharma! Ah, the dharmatā of dharma!"

children.text: yastathāgatasya prādurbhāvaḥ sa āryeṇa subhūtinā sthavireṇa subhāṣiteneha sūcyate deśyate prakāśyate prabhāvyate
children.translated_text: The manifestation of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is indicated, taught, illuminated, disclosed, and made manifest here by the well-spoken words of the noble elder <s>Subhūti</s>.

children.text: tathāgataṃ taṃ vayaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamadyāgreṇa dhārayiṣyāmo yo 'nayā prajñāpāramitayā avirahito bhaviṣyati yo 'pi ca anena bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihāreṇa vihariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "From today onward, Blessed One, we will regard as that <s>Tathāgata</s> the bodhisattva, the great being, who will not be separated from this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, and also the bodhisattva, the great being, who will dwell in this dwelling of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>."

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstān sendrakān sabrahmakān saprajāpatikān sarṣinaranārīgaṇānāmantrayate sma evametaddevaputrāḥ evam etat
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed those assemblies together with <s>Indra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, the ṛṣis, men, and women: "So it is, devaputras; so it is.

children.text: yadāhaṃ devaputrā dīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntike dīpavatyāṃ rājadhānyām antarāyaṇamadhyagato 'nayā prajñāpāramitayā avirahito 'bhūvam tadāhaṃ dīpaṃkareṇa tathāgatenārhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhena vyākṛto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava anāgate 'dhvani asaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpaiḥ śākyamunirnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyānāṃ ca buddho bhagavāniti
children.translated_text: Devaputras, when in the royal city of <s>Dīpavatī</s>, having come into the presence of the <s>Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one, in the middle of the road, I was not separated from this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), then I was predicted by the <s>Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one, for unsurpassed perfect awakening: 'Young man, in a future time, after incalculable kalpas, you will be a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened one, endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, Blessed One.'

children.text: atha khalu te devaputrā bhagavantametadavocan āścaryaṃ bhagavan paramāścaryaṃ sugata
children.translated_text: Then those devaputras said this to the Blessed One: "Wonderful, Blessed One; most wonderful, Sugata!

children.text: yāvadiyaṃ prajñāpāramitā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ sarvajñatāyā āhārikā anuparigrāhikā ceti ||
children.translated_text: How much this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> nourishes and supports bodhisattvas, great beings, for omniscience!"

children.text: Chapter 3

atha khalu bhagavān ye tatra devaputrāḥ parṣadi saṃnipatitāḥ saṃniṣaṇṇāścābhūvan yāś ca bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ saṃnipatitāḥ saṃniṣaṇṇāścābhūvan tān devaputrān saṃnipatitān saṃniṣaṇṇāṃś ca viditvā tāś ca sarvāścatasraḥ parṣadaḥ saṃnipatitāḥ saṃniṣaṇṇāś ca viditvā kāmāvacarān rūpāvacarāṃś ca devaputrān brahmakāyikāṃś ca devaputrān ābhāsvarāṃś ca parīttaśubhāṃś ca akaniṣṭhāṃś ca devaputrān sākṣiṇaḥ sthāpayitvā śakradevendrapramukhān kāmāvacarān devaputrān mahābrahmapramukhāṃś ca brahmakāyikān devaputrānābhāsvarāṃś ca devaputrānāmantrayate sma yo hi kaściddevaputrāḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati na tasya māro vā mārakāyikā vā devatā avatāraprekṣiṇyo 'vatāragaveṣiṇyo 'vatāraṃ lapsyante
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing that the devaputras there in the assembly had gathered and sat down, and that the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen had gathered and sat down, and knowing that all four assemblies had gathered and sat down, appointed as witnesses the devaputras of the desire realm and form realm, the devaputras of <s>Brahmā</s>'s host, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, and the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> devaputras. He addressed the devaputras of the desire realm headed by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, the devaputras of <s>Brahmā</s>'s host headed by <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, and the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> devaputras: "Devaputras, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family takes up, retains, recites, masters, and sets forth this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, neither <s>Māra</s> nor deities of <s>Māra</s>'s retinue, watching for an opening and seeking an opening, will find an opening against him or her.

children.text: nāpi tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā manuṣyā vā amanuṣyā vā avatāraprekṣiṇo 'vatāragaveṣiṇo 'vatāraṃ lapsyante
children.translated_text: Nor will humans or nonhumans, watching for an opening and seeking an opening against that son of good family or daughter of good family, find an opening.

children.text: nāpi sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā viṣamāparihāreṇa kālaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Nor will that son of good family or daughter of good family die through an adverse misfortune.

children.text: punaraparaṃ devaputrāḥ ye devaputrā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samprasthitāḥ yaiś ca devaputrairiyaṃ prajñāpāramitā nodgṛhītā na dhāritā na vācitā na paryavāptā na pravartitā te devaputrāstaṃ kulaputraṃ vā kuladuhitaraṃ vā upasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyante tasya ca kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgṛhṇato dhārayato vācayataḥ paryavāpnuvataḥ pravartayamānasyāntikācchroṣyanti śrutvā codgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti pravartayiṣyanti
children.translated_text: Moreover, devaputras, those devaputras who have set out for unsurpassed perfect awakening and by whom this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> has not been taken up, retained, recited, mastered, or set forth will think that they should approach that son of good family or daughter of good family. From the presence of that son of good family or daughter of good family as he or she takes up, retains, recites, masters, and sets forth this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, they will listen; and having heard it, they will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, and set it forth.

children.text: na ca khalu punardevaputrāstasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgṛhṇato dhārayato vācayataḥ paryavāpnuvataḥ pravartayamānasya araṇyagatasya vā vṛkṣamūlagatasya vā śūnyāgāragatasya vā abhyavakāśagatasya vā pathi gatasya vā utpathagatasya vā aṭavīgatasya vā mahāsamudragatasya vā tatra tatropasaṃkrāmato vā caṅkramyamāṇasya vā sthitasya vā niṣaṇṇasya vā vipannasya vā bhayaṃ vā bhaviṣyati stambhitatvaṃ vā bhaviṣyati utpatsyate vā ||
children.translated_text: And, devaputras, for that son of good family or daughter of good family who takes up, retains, recites, masters, and sets forth this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, whether gone to the wilderness, to the foot of a tree, to an empty house, to the open air, on the road, off the road, in a forest, or on the great ocean, or while going here and there, walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, no fear or paralysis will occur there, nor will any arise.

children.text: atha khalu catvāro mahārājāno bhagavantametadavocan āścaryaṃ bhagavan yadimāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgṛhṇan dhārayan vācayan paryavāpnuvan pravartayan sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā yānatraye sattvān vinayati na ca sattvasaṃjñāmutpādayati
children.translated_text: Then the Four Great Kings said this to the Blessed One: "Wonderful, Blessed One, that this son of good family or daughter of good family, taking up, retaining, reciting, mastering, and setting forth this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, disciplines beings in the three vehicles and yet does not produce the notion of a being.

children.text: vayaṃ bhagavaṃstasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyāmaḥ ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Blessed One, we will arrange protection, defense, and guarding for that son of good family or daughter of good family who takes up, retains, recites, masters, and sets forth this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>."

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat aham api bhagavaṃstasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyāmi ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "I too, Blessed One, will arrange protection, defense, and guarding for that son of good family or daughter of good family who takes up, retains, recites, masters, and sets forth this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>."

children.text: brahmāpi sahāpatiḥ sārdhaṃ brahmakāyikair devaputrair bhagavantametadavocat aham api bhagavaṃstasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyāmi ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> too, together with the devaputras of the Brahmā host, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, I too will arrange protection, shelter, and guarding for that son of good family or daughter of good family who will take up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, and set it forth."

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat āścaryaṃ bhagavan yadimāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgṛhṇan dhārayan vācayan paryavāpnuvan pravartayan sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imān yato dṛṣṭadhārmikān guṇān pratilabhate parigṛhṇāti kiṃ punarbhagavan prajñāpāramitāyām udgṛhītāyāṃ sarvāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitā udgṛhītā bhavanti evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat evametatkauśika evam etat
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "It is wonderful, Blessed One, that a son of good family or daughter of good family, while taking up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retaining it, reciting it, mastering it, and setting it forth, obtains and gains these present-life qualities. Moreover, Blessed One, when the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is taken up, are all six <s>pāramitās</s> taken up?" When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>; so it is.

children.text: prajñāpāramitāyāṃ kauśika udgṛhītāyāṃ sarvāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitā udgṛhītā bhavanti
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s>, when the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is taken up, all six <s>pāramitās</s> are taken up.

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika prajñāpāramitāyām udgṛhītāyāṃ dhāritāyāṃ vācitāyāṃ paryavāptāyāṃ pravartitāyāṃ sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikān guṇān parigṛhṇāti
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, when the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> has been taken up, retained, recited, mastered, and set forth, that son of good family or daughter of good family gains present-life qualities.

children.text: tān kauśika sarvān śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te
children.translated_text: Hear all of them, <s>Kauśika</s>, and attend well and carefully; I will speak to you."

children.text: sādhu bhagavanniti śakro devānāmindro bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt
children.translated_text: "Good, Blessed One," <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, replied to the Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavānetadavocat tatra kauśika ye mama dharmaṃ vigrahītavyaṃ maṃsyante vivaditavyaṃ maṃsyante virodhayitavyaṃ maṃsyante teṣāṃ vigrahītukāmānāṃ vivaditukāmānāṃ virodhayitukāmānām utpannotpannā vigrahā vivādā virodhāḥ punarevāntardhāsyanti na sthāsyanti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this: "Here, <s>Kauśika</s>, those who will think that my Dharma should be attacked, who will think that it should be disputed, who will think that it should be opposed: for those who wish to attack, dispute, and oppose it, the attacks, disputes, and opposition that arise will disappear again and will not remain.

children.text: teṣāṃ vigrahītukāmānāṃ vivaditukāmānāṃ virodhayitukāmānāṃ na te 'bhiprāyāḥ paripūriṃ gamiṣyanti
children.translated_text: For those who wish to attack, dispute, and oppose it, those intentions of theirs will not come to fulfillment.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ evaṃ hyetatkauśika bhavati ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati tasyaivaṃ tānyutpannotpannānyadhikaraṇāni punarevāntardhāsyanti na sthāsyanti
children.translated_text: Why is that? For this is so, <s>Kauśika</s>: when a son of good family or daughter of good family will take up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, set it forth, teach it, instruct in it, recite it aloud, and study it, those very legal disputes that arise for that person will disappear again and will not remain.

children.text: teṣāṃ vigrahītukāmānāṃ vivaditukāmānāṃ virodhayitukāmānāṃ na te 'bhiprāyāḥ paripūriṃ gamiṣyanti
children.translated_text: For those who wish to attack, dispute, and oppose it, those intentions of theirs will not come to fulfillment.

children.text: imam api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ guṇaṃ parigṛhṇāti ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgṛhṇāti dhārayati vācayati paryavāpnoti pravartayati deśayati upadiśati uddiśati svādhyāyati
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s>, this too is a present-life quality gained by that son of good family or daughter of good family who takes up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retains it, recites it, masters it, sets it forth, teaches it, instructs in it, recites it aloud, and studies it.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma kauśika maghī nāmauṣadhī sarvaviṣapraśamanī
children.translated_text: It is, <s>Kauśika</s>, just like the herb called <s>Maghī</s>, which pacifies every poison.

children.text: tatra āśīviṣeṇa jantunā bubhukṣitena āhārārthinā āhāragaveṣiṇā kaścideva prāṇakajāto janturdṛṣṭo bhavet
children.translated_text: Suppose there were some living creature, some animal, seen by a poisonous serpent that was hungry, seeking food, looking for food.

children.text: sa āśīviṣastaṃ prāṇakajātaṃ gandhenānubadhnīyād anugacched āhārahetorbhakṣayitukāmaḥ
children.translated_text: That poisonous serpent, following the scent of that living creature, would pursue it for the sake of food, wanting to devour it.

children.text: atha sa prāṇakajāto yena sā maghī nāmauṣadhī tenopasaṃkramet tenopasaṃkramya tiṣṭhet
children.translated_text: Then that living creature would approach the place where that herb called <s>Maghī</s> was; having approached it, it would stand there.

children.text: atha sa āśīviṣastasyā oṣadhyā gandhenaiva pratyudāvarteta
children.translated_text: Then that poisonous serpent would turn back merely because of the scent of that herb.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi tasyā oṣadhyā bhaiṣajyaguṇaḥ sa tādṛśo yastasyāśīviṣasya tadviṣamabhibhavati
children.translated_text: Why is that? For the medicinal quality of that herb is such that it overpowers that poison of the poisonous serpent.

children.text: evaṃ balavatī hi sā oṣadhī
children.translated_text: For that herb is so powerful.

children.text: evameva kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā va imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati tasya kauśika yāni tānyutpannotpannānyadhikaraṇāni vigrahā vivādā virodhā bhaviṣyanti te prajñāpāramitāyāstejasā balena sthāmataḥ prajñāpāramitābalādhānena kṣipraṃ tata evoparaṃsyanti upaśamiṣyanti antardhāsyanti na vivardhiṣyante
children.translated_text: In just the same way, <s>Kauśika</s>, for a son of good family or daughter of good family who will take up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, set it forth, teach it, instruct in it, recite it aloud, and study it, whatever legal disputes, attacks, disputes, and opposition may arise, through the brilliance, power, and strength of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, by the empowerment of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, they will quickly cease right there, become pacified, and disappear; they will not increase.

children.text: yato yata evotpatsyante tatra tatraiva nirotsyante antardhāsyanti na vivardhiṣyante na sthāsyanti
children.translated_text: Wherever they arise, there and then they will cease and disappear; they will not increase and will not remain.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ prajñāpāramitā hi rāgādīnāṃ yāvannirvāṇagrāhasyopaśamayitrī na vivardhiketi
children.translated_text: Why is that? For the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> pacifies attachment and the rest, up to the grasping at nirvāṇa; it does not cause them to increase.

children.text: catvāraś ca tasya mahārājānaḥ śakraś ca devānāmindro brahmā ca sahāpatiḥ sarve ca buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvāś ca rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyanti ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati
children.translated_text: And the four great kings, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, all the blessed Buddhas, and the bodhisattvas will arrange protection, shelter, and guarding for the one who will take up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, set it forth, teach it, instruct in it, recite it aloud, and study it.

children.text: ayaṃ tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmiko guṇaḥ parigṛhīto bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: This present-life quality will have been gained by that son of good family or daughter of good family."

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati sa ādeyavacanaś ca bhaviṣyati mṛduvacanaś ca bhaviṣyati mitavacanaś ca bhaviṣyati aprakīrṇavacanaś ca bhaviṣyati na ca krodhābhibhūto bhaviṣyati na ca mānābhibhūto bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son of good family or daughter of good family who takes up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retains it, recites it, masters it, sets it forth, teaches it, explains it, rehearses it, and studies it will be one whose speech is acceptable, whose speech is gentle, whose speech is measured, and whose speech is not scattered; and he will not be overcome by anger, nor will he be overcome by pride.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi taṃ prajñāpāramitā paridamayati prajñāpāramitā pariṇamayati na krodhaṃ vardhayati na mānaṃ vardhayati
children.translated_text: Why is that? For this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> thoroughly tames him; the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> transforms him. It does not increase anger, and it does not increase pride.

children.text: sa nopanāhaṃ parigṛhṇāti na vyāpādaṃ parigṛhṇāti nānuśayaṃ dhārayati
children.translated_text: He does not take hold of resentment, does not take hold of malice, and does not maintain a latent tendency.

children.text: evaṃ carato 'sya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā smṛtirmaitrī cotpadyate
children.translated_text: For a son of good family or daughter of good family who practices in this way, mindfulness and loving-kindness arise.

children.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavati sacedahaṃ vyāpādamutpādayiṣyāmi tenendriyāṇi me paribhetsyante mukhavarṇaś ca me dhakṣyate
children.translated_text: It occurs to him: "If I give rise to malice, by that my faculties will be broken, and the color of my face will be scorched.

children.text: ayuktaṃ caitanmama yadahamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samprasthitaḥ tatra śikṣitukāmaḥ krodhasya vaśaṃ gaccheyam
children.translated_text: And it is not fitting for me, when I have set out toward unsurpassed perfect awakening and wish to train in it, to come under the power of anger."

children.text: ityevaṃ sa kṣiprameva smṛtiṃ pratilabhate
children.translated_text: Thinking in this way, he very quickly regains mindfulness.

children.text: imam api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ guṇaṃ parigṛhṇāti ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Kauśika</s>, is an immediate benefit obtained by a son of good family or daughter of good family who takes up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retains it, recites it, masters it, sets it forth, teaches it, explains it, rehearses it, and studies it.

children.text: evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat āścaryaṃ bhagavan yatheyaṃ prajñāpāramitā paridamanāya pratyupasthitā anunāmāya bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām ||
children.translated_text: When this had been said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "It is wonderful, Blessed One, how this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is present for the taming and humbling of bodhisattvas, great beings."

children.text: bhagavānāha punaraparaṃ kauśika ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati sacetkulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmevamudgṛhṇan dhārayan vācayan paryavāpnuvan pravartayan deśayan upadiśayan uddiśan svādhyāyan saṃgrāme vartamāne saṃgrāmaśirasi samārūḍhaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, if a son of good family or daughter of good family takes up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retains it, recites it, masters it, sets it forth, teaches it, explains it, rehearses it, and studies it, and if that son of good family or daughter of good family, while taking up, retaining, reciting, mastering, setting forth, teaching, explaining, rehearsing, and studying this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> in that way, should be in a battle and have mounted to the front of the battle,

children.text: tasya saṃgrāmamavatarato vā avatīrṇasya vā atikrāmato vā saṃgrāmamadhyagatasya vā tiṣṭhato vā niṣaṇṇasya vā asthānametatkauśika anavakāśo yattasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ manasi kurvato vā udgṛhṇato vā dhārayato vā vācayato vā paryavāpnuvato vā pravartayato vā deśayato vā upadiśato vā uddiśato vā svādhyāyato vā jīvitāntarāyo vā bhavet
children.translated_text: then, whether he is entering the battle, has entered it, is crossing through it, is in the midst of the battle, is standing, or is sitting, it is impossible, <s>Kauśika</s>, it cannot occur, that an obstacle to life should arise for that son of good family or daughter of good family while he brings this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> to mind, takes it up, retains it, recites it, masters it, sets it forth, teaches it, explains it, rehearses it, or studies it.

children.text: paropakrameṇa jīvitāntarāyaṃ so 'nuprāpnuyāt naitatsthānaṃ vidyate
children.translated_text: That he would meet with an obstacle to life through an attack by another: no such possibility is found.

children.text: sacetpunastasya kaścitkauśika tatra śastraṃ vā daṇḍaṃ vā loṣṭaṃ vā anyadvā kṣipet naitattasya śarīre nipatet
children.translated_text: And if, <s>Kauśika</s>, someone there should throw a weapon, a stick, a clod, or something else at him, it would not fall upon his body.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ mahāvidyeyaṃ kauśika yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Why is that? This, <s>Kauśika</s>, is a great <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge), namely the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: apramāṇeyaṃ kauśika vidyā yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: This, <s>Kauśika</s>, is an immeasurable <s>vidyā</s>, namely the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: aparimāṇeyaṃ kauśika vidyā yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: This, <s>Kauśika</s>, is a boundless <s>vidyā</s>, namely the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: anuttareyaṃ kauśika vidyā yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: This, <s>Kauśika</s>, is an unsurpassed <s>vidyā</s>, namely the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: asameyaṃ kauśika vidyā yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: This, <s>Kauśika</s>, is an unequalled <s>vidyā</s>, namely the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: asamasameyaṃ kauśika vidyā yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: This, <s>Kauśika</s>, is a <s>vidyā</s> equal to the unequalled, namely the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ atra hi kauśika vidyāyāṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā nātmavyābādhāya cetayate na paravyābādhāya cetayate nobhayavyābādhāya cetayate
children.translated_text: Why is that? For here, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son of good family or daughter of good family training in this <s>vidyā</s> does not intend harm to himself, does not intend harm to another, and does not intend harm to both.

children.text: atra hi kauśika vidyāyāṃ śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate sarvajñajñānaṃ ca pratilapsyate
children.translated_text: For here, <s>Kauśika</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, training in this <s>vidyā</s> will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening and will obtain omniscient knowledge.

children.text: tena so 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya sarvasattvānāṃ cittāni vyavalokayiṣyati
children.translated_text: By that, having fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, he will survey the minds of all beings.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ atra hi kauśika vidyāyāṃ śikṣamāṇasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya na tatkiṃcidasti yanna prāptaṃ vā na jñātaṃ vā na sākṣātkṛtaṃ vā syāt
children.translated_text: Why is that? For here, <s>Kauśika</s>, for a bodhisattva, a great being, training in this <s>vidyā</s>, there is nothing that would not have been attained, not known, or not directly realized.

children.text: tasmātsarvajñajñānamityucyate
children.translated_text: Therefore it is called omniscient knowledge.

children.text: ayam api kauśika tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā dṛṣṭadhārmiko guṇaḥ parigṛhīto bhaviṣyati ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Kauśika</s>, will be an immediate benefit obtained by that son of good family or daughter of good family who takes up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retains it, recites it, masters it, sets it forth, teaches it, explains it, rehearses it, and studies it.

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yatreyaṃ prajñāpāramitā antaśo likhitvā pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā pūjāpūrvaṃgamaṃ sthāpayitvā na satkariṣyate nodgrahīṣyate na dhārayiṣyate na vācayiṣyate na paryavāpsyate na pravartayiṣyate na deśayiṣyate nopadekṣyate noddekṣyate na svādhyāsyate na tatra kauśika sattvānāṃ manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vā avatārārthiko 'vatāragaveṣī avatāraṃ lapsyate sthāpayitvā pūrvakarmavipākam
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, wherever this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), even after it has been written down, made into a book, set up with worship going before it, is not honored, not taken up, not retained, not recited, not mastered, not set in motion, not taught, not explained, not rehearsed, and not studied, there, <s>Kauśika</s>, among beings, whether human or nonhuman, one who seeks an opening, who searches for an opening, will not obtain an opening, except through the ripening of former karma.

children.text: imam api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ guṇaṃ parigṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Kauśika</s>, is a benefit visible in this life that that son of good family or daughter of good family receives.

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika tadyathāpi nāma ye bodhimaṇḍagatā vā bodhimaṇḍaparisāmantagatā vā bodhimaṇḍābhyantaragatā vā bodhivṛkṣamūlagatā vā manuṣyā vā amanuṣyā vā tiryagyonigatānapyupādāya yāvanna te śakyā manuṣyairvā amanuṣyairvā viheṭhayituṃ vā vyāpādayituṃ vā āveśayituṃ vā sthāpayitvā pūrvakarmavipākam
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, just as, for example, those who have gone to the seat of awakening, or to the area surrounding the seat of awakening, or within the seat of awakening, or to the foot of the bodhi tree, whether humans, nonhumans, or even beings born in the animal realm, cannot be harassed, injured, or possessed by humans or nonhumans, except through the ripening of former karma,

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tatra hi atītānāgatapratyutpannāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbhotsyante abhisaṃbudhyante ca ye sarvasattvānām abhayam avairam anuttrāsaṃ prabhāvayanti prakāśayanti
children.translated_text: why is that? For there the past, future, and present <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones, have awakened, will awaken, and do awaken, and they bring forth and make manifest fearlessness, absence of hostility, and freedom from terror for all beings.

children.text: evameva kauśika yatra kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati deśayiṣyati upadekṣyati uddekṣyati svādhyāsyati tatra hi kauśika sattvā na śakyā manuṣyairvā amanuṣyairvā viheṭhayituṃ vā vyāpādayituṃ vā āveśayituṃ vā sthāpayitvā pūrvakarmavipākam
children.translated_text: So too, <s>Kauśika</s>, wherever a son of good family or daughter of good family will take up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, set it in motion, teach it, explain it, rehearse it, and study it, there, <s>Kauśika</s>, beings cannot be harassed, injured, or possessed by humans or nonhumans, except through the ripening of former karma.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ anayaiva hi kauśika prajñāpāramitayā pṛthivīpradeśaḥ sattvānāṃ caityabhūtaḥ kṛto vandanīyo mānanīyaḥ pūjanīyo 'rcanīyo 'pacāyanīyaḥ satkaraṇīyo gurukaraṇīyaḥ trāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ layanaṃ parāyaṇaṃ kṛto bhaviṣyati tatropagatānāṃ sattvānām
children.translated_text: Why is that? For by this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, that tract of earth has been made a shrine for beings, worthy of veneration, honor, worship, reverence, homage, respect, and esteem; it will have been made a protection, refuge, shelter, and final resort for the beings who come there.

children.text: imam api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ guṇaṃ parigṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Kauśika</s>, is a benefit visible in this life that that son of good family or daughter of good family receives.

children.text: evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat yo bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā sthāpayet enāṃ ca divyābhiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākābhiḥ samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ satkuryāt gurukuryāt mānayet pūjayet arcayet apacāyet yaś ca tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya śarīrāṇi stūpeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet parigṛhṇīyāt dhārayeddhā tāṃś ca tathaiva divyābhiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākābhiḥ samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ satkuryāt gurukuryāt mānayet pūjayet arcayet apacāyet katarastayoḥ kulaputrayoḥ kuladuhitrorvā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat tena hi kauśika tvāmevātra pratiprakṣyāmi
children.translated_text: When this had been said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, suppose a son of good family or daughter of good family writes down this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, makes it into a book, sets it up, and honors, reveres, respects, worships, venerates, and pays homage to it with divine flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, with rows of lamps all around, and with many kinds of worship. And suppose another were to place in stupas the bodily relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one, after his final nirvāṇa, were to take them up and preserve them, and were likewise to honor, revere, respect, worship, venerate, and pay homage to them with divine flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, with rows of lamps all around, and with many kinds of worship. Which of those two sons of good family, or daughters of good family, would produce the greater merit?" When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "Then, <s>Kauśika</s>, I shall question you yourself about this.

children.text: yathā te kṣamate tathā vyākuryāḥ
children.translated_text: Answer as it seems right to you."

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase kauśika yo 'yaṃ tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya sarvajñatātmabhāvo 'bhinirvartitaḥ sa katamasyāṃ pratipadi śikṣamāṇena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ sarvajñatā pratilabdhā abhisaṃbuddhā evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat ihaiva bhagavan bhagavatā prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ sarvajñatā pratilabdhā abhisaṃbuddhā
children.translated_text: "What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? This embodiment of omniscience belonging to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one, which has been brought forth: while training in what practice did the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one, attain and awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening, omniscience?" When this had been said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Here itself, Blessed One, while the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one, was training in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, unsurpassed perfect awakening, omniscience, was attained and awakened to."

children.text: bhagavānāha tasmāttarhi kauśika nānenātmabhāvaśarīrapratilambhena tathāgatastathāgata iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, it is not by the obtaining of this personal physical body that the <s>Tathāgata</s> is counted as a <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: sarvajñatāyāṃ tu pratilabdhāyāṃ tathāgatastathāgata iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati
children.translated_text: Rather, when omniscience has been attained, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is counted as a <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: yeyaṃ kauśika sarvajñatā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya prajñāpāramitānirjātaiṣā
children.translated_text: That omniscience of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one, <s>Kauśika</s>, is born from <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: eṣa ca kauśika tathāgatasyātmabhāvaśarīrapratilambhaḥ prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyanirjātaḥ san sarvajñajñānāśrayabhūto bhavati
children.translated_text: And this obtaining of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> personal physical body, <s>Kauśika</s>, being born from <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and skillful means, becomes the basis for the knowledge of omniscience.

children.text: enaṃ hyāśrayaṃ niśritya sarvajñajñānasya prabhāvanā bhavati buddhaśarīraprabhāvanā bhavati dharmaśarīraprabhāvanā bhavati saṃghaśarīraprabhāvanā bhavati
children.translated_text: For relying on this basis, the manifestation of the knowledge of omniscience takes place; the manifestation of the Buddha-body takes place; the manifestation of the Dharma-body takes place; the manifestation of the Saṅgha-body takes place.

children.text: ityevaṃ sarvajñajñānahetuko 'yamātmabhāvaśarīrapratilambhaḥ sarvajñajñānāśrayabhūtatvāt sarvasattvānāṃ caityabhūto vandanīyaḥ satkaraṇīyo gurukaraṇīyo mānanīyaḥ pūjanīyo 'rcanīyo 'pacāyanīyaḥ saṃvṛtto bhavati
children.translated_text: Thus this acquisition of a bodily existence, caused by omniscient knowledge, because it has become the support of omniscient knowledge and a shrine for all beings, becomes worthy of veneration, worthy of honor, worthy of respect as a teacher, worthy of esteem, worthy of worship, worthy of reverence, and worthy of homage.

children.text: evaṃ ca mama parinirvṛtasyāpi sataḥ eṣāṃ śarīrāṇāṃ pūjā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And in this way, even when I have passed into final nirvāṇa, worship of these bodily relics of mine will take place.

children.text: tasmāttarhi kauśika yaḥ kaścitkulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā pustakagatāṃ vā kṛtvā sthāpayet enāṃ ca divyābhiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākābhiḥ satkuryāt gurukuryāt mānayet pūjayet arcayet apacāyet ayameva kauśika tayoḥ kulaputrayoḥ kuladuhitrorvā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet
children.translated_text: Therefore then, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, having written this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> or made it into a book, should set it up, and should honor, respect, esteem, worship, revere, and pay homage to it with divine flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, that very one, <s>Kauśika</s>, whether a son of good family or daughter of good family, would produce more merit than those two.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ sarvajñajñānasya hi kauśika tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā pūjā kṛtā bhaviṣyati yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā iha prajñāpāramitāyāṃ likhyamānāyāṃ pustakagatāyāṃ vā satkāraṃ gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanām apacāyanāṃ pūjāṃ ca vividhāṃ kuryāt ayameva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet
children.translated_text: Why is that? For, <s>Kauśika</s>, by that son of good family or daughter of good family, worship of omniscient knowledge will have been performed. The son of good family or daughter of good family who, when this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being written or made into a book, should render honor, respect, esteem, worship, reverence, homage, and various forms of worship to it, would produce still more merit than that.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ sarvajñajñānasya hi kauśika tena pūjā kṛtā bhaviṣyati yaḥ prajñāpāramitāyai pūjāṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? For, <s>Kauśika</s>, worship of omniscient knowledge will have been performed by the one who will perform worship for the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat ya ime bhagavan jāmbūdvīpakā manuṣyā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ na likhiṣyanti nodgrahīṣyanti na dhārayiṣyanti na vācayiṣyanti na paryavāpsyanti na pravartayiṣyanti na deśayiṣyanti nopadekṣyanti noddekṣyanti na svādhyāsyanti tāṃ caināṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākābhiḥ samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhirna satkariṣyanti na gurukariṣyanti na mānayiṣyanti na pūjayiṣyanti nārcayiṣyanti nāpacāyiṣyanti kiṃ nu te bhagavan na jñāsyanti evaṃ mahārthikā bhagavatoktā prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pūjā kṛtā bhaviṣyatīti kiṃ nu te bhagavan na vetsyanti evaṃ mahānuśaṃsā evaṃ mahāphalā evaṃ mahāvipākā bhagavatoktā prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pūjā kṛtā bhaviṣyatīti na ca te vedayiṣyanti uta jñāsyanti vetsyanti vedayiṣyanti na ca punaḥ śraddhāsyanti evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat tatkiṃ manyase kauśika kiyantaste jāmbūdvīpakā manuṣyās te buddhe 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ ye dharme 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ ye saṃghe 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat alpakāste bhagavan jāmbūdvīpakā manuṣyā ye buddhe 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ ye dharme 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ ye saṃghe 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: When this had been said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, those people of <s>Jāmbūdvīpa</s> who will not write this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, not take it up, not retain it, not recite it, not master it, not set it forth, not teach it, not instruct in it, not recite it aloud, and not study it, and who will not honor, respect, esteem, worship, revere, or pay homage to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, flags, garlands of lamps all around, and many kinds of worship: Blessed One, will they not know that the Blessed One has said that worship performed for the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is of such great benefit? Blessed One, will they not understand that the Blessed One has said that worship performed for the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> has such great advantage, such great fruit, and such great result? Will they not perceive it; or will they know, understand, and perceive it, but still not have faith?" When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? How many of those people of <s>Jāmbūdvīpa</s> are endowed with confirmed confidence in the Buddha, with confirmed confidence in the Dharma, and with confirmed confidence in the Saṃgha?" When this had been said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Few, Blessed One, are those people of <s>Jāmbūdvīpa</s> who are endowed with confirmed confidence in the Buddha, confirmed confidence in the Dharma, and confirmed confidence in the Saṃgha."

children.text: evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat evametatkauśika evam etat
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>; so it is.

children.text: alpakāste jāmbūdvīpakā manuṣyā ye buddhe 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ ye dharme 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ ye saṃghe 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Few are those people of <s>Jāmbūdvīpa</s> who are endowed with confirmed confidence in the Buddha, confirmed confidence in the Dharma, and confirmed confidence in the Saṃgha.

children.text: tebhyaḥ kauśika alpebhyo 'lpatarakāste ye srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāpnuvanti tataḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalamanāgāmiphalam
children.translated_text: Fewer than those few, <s>Kauśika</s>, are those who attain the fruit of stream-entry; fewer still than those are those who attain the fruit of once-returning and the fruit of non-returning.

children.text: tebhyo 'pyalpebhyo 'lpatarakāste ye 'rhattvaṃ prāpnuvanti
children.translated_text: Fewer even than those few are those who attain arhatship.

children.text: tebhyo 'pyalpebhyo 'lpatarakāste ye pratyekabodhiṃ sākṣātkurvanti
children.translated_text: Fewer even than those few are those who directly realize solitary awakening.

children.text: tebhyo 'pyalpebhyo 'lpatarakāste ye 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādayanti
children.translated_text: Fewer even than those few are those who produce thoughts directed toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: tebhyo 'pyalpebhyo 'lpatarakāste ye 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādya taṃ cittotpādaṃ bṛṃhayanti
children.translated_text: Fewer even than those few are those who, having produced thoughts directed toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, strengthen that production of thought.

children.text: tebhyo 'pyalpebhyo 'lpatarakāste ye 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādya upabṛṃhayitvā ca ārabdhavīryā viharanti
children.translated_text: Fewer even than those few are those who, having produced thoughts directed toward unsurpassed perfect awakening and strengthened them, live with energy aroused.

children.text: tebhyo 'pyalpebhyo 'lpatarakāste ye prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yogamāpadyante
children.translated_text: Fewer even than those few are those who apply themselves to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tebhyo 'pyalpebhyo 'lpatarakāste ye prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caranti
children.translated_text: Fewer even than those few are those who practice in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tebhyo 'pyalpebhyo 'lpatarakāste ye prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caranto ghaṭamānā avinivartanīyāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmāvavatiṣṭhante
children.translated_text: Fewer even than those few are those who, while practicing in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and exerting themselves, stand on the irreversible bodhisattva stage.

children.text: tebhyo 'pyalpebhyo 'lpatarakāste ye prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caranto ghaṭamānā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante
children.translated_text: Fewer even than those few are those who, while practicing in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and exerting themselves, will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening."

children.text: tebhyo 'pyalpebhyo 'lpatarakāste ye prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caranto ghaṭamānā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante
children.translated_text: Fewer even than those few are those who, practicing in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and striving, fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: te te kauśika bodhisattvā mahāsattvā ye avinivartanīyāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya anyeṣāmadhyāśayasampannānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ ca prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇānāṃ ghaṭamānānāṃ prajñāpāramitāmupadiśanti ca uddiśanti
children.translated_text: Those, <s>Kauśika</s>, are the bodhisattvas, great beings, who, standing on the irreversible bodhisattva level and having fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, teach and proclaim the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> to other sons of good family and daughters of good family who are endowed with earnest intention, who train in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, and who strive.

children.text: te codgṛhṇanti dhārayanti vācayanti paryavāpnuvanti pravartayanti upadeśayanti upadiśanti uddiśanti svādhyāyanti
children.translated_text: And they take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, set it forth, teach it, instruct in it, proclaim it, and study it.

children.text: tāṃ caināṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ puṣpair dhūpair gandhair mālyair vilepanaiścūrṇair vastraiśchatrair dhvajairghaṇṭābhiḥ patākābhiḥ samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ satkurvanti gurukurvanti mānayanti pūjayanti arcayanti apacāyanti
children.translated_text: And they honor this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, revere it, respect it, worship it, venerate it, and pay homage to it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, garments, parasols, banners, bells, flags, rows of lamps all around, and many kinds of offerings.

children.text: santi khalu punaḥ kauśika aprameyā asaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvāḥ ye bodhicittamutpādayanti bodhicittamutpādya bodhicittamupabṛṃhayanti bodhicittamupabṛṃhayitvā bodhāya caranti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, there are immeasurable and innumerable beings who generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening); having generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, they strengthen <s>bodhicitta</s>; and having strengthened <s>bodhicitta</s>, they practice for awakening.

children.text: teṣāṃ khalu punaḥ kauśika aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhāya caratām api yadyeko vā dvau vā avinivartanīyāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmāvavatiṣṭheyātām
children.translated_text: Yet among those immeasurable and innumerable beings, <s>Kauśika</s>, who are practicing for awakening, perhaps only one or two would stand on the irreversible bodhisattva level.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ durabhisaṃbhavā hi kauśika anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirhīnavīryaiḥ kusīdairhīnasattvair hīnacittairhīnasaṃjñair hīnādhimuktikairhīnaprajñaiḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because, <s>Kauśika</s>, unsurpassed perfect awakening is difficult to attain for those of weak energy, the lazy, those of weak character, weak mind, weak perception, weak resolve, and weak wisdom.

children.text: tasmāttarhi kauśika kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃboddhukāmena iyameva prajñāpāramitā sukhaṃ abhīkṣṇaṃ śrotavyā udgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā pravartayitavyā deśayitavyā upadeṣṭavyā uddeṣṭavyā svādhyātavyā paripraṣṭavyā
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son of good family or daughter of good family who wishes quickly to fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening should listen to this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> gladly and repeatedly, take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, set it forth, teach it, instruct in it, proclaim it, study it, and ask questions about it.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi sa evaṃ jñāsyati atra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caran śikṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? For in this way he will know: 'Here, in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, formerly practicing the bodhisattva conduct, trained.

children.text: asmābhirapyatra śikṣitavyam
children.translated_text: We too should train here.

children.text: eṣo 'smākaṃ śāsteti
children.translated_text: This is our teacher.'

children.text: tiṣṭhato vā kauśika parinirvṛtasya vā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ prajñāpāramitaiva pratisartavyā
children.translated_text: Whether the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha is still present or has passed into complete nirvāṇa, bodhisattvas, great beings, should rely on the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> itself.

children.text: tasmāttarhi kauśika yaḥ kaścitkulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya pūjāyai koṭiśaḥ saptaratnamayāṃs tathāgatadhātugarbhān stūpān kārayet
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family, for the worship of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, Arhat, perfectly awakened Buddha who has passed into complete nirvāṇa, were to have many millions of stūpas made of the seven precious substances and containing relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> built;

children.text: kārayitvā ca tān yāvajjīvaṃ divyaiḥ puṣpair divyair dhūpair divyair gandhair divyair mālyair divyair vilepanair divyaiś cūrṇair divyair vastrair divyaiś chatrair divyair dhvajair divyābhir ghaṇṭābhiḥ divyābhiḥ patākābhiḥ samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ bahuvidhābhiś ca divyābhiḥ pūjābhiḥ satkuryāt gurukuryāt mānayet pūjayet arcayet apacāyet tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet śakra āha bahu bhagavan bahu sugata
children.translated_text: and, after having had them built, for as long as he lived he were to honor, revere, respect, worship, venerate, and pay homage to them with divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine ointments, divine powders, divine garments, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, divine flags, rows of lamps all around, and many kinds of divine offerings. What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account?' <s>Śakra</s> said, 'Much, Blessed One, much, <s>Sugata</s>.'

children.text: bhagavānāha ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām abhiśraddadhad avakalpayann adhimucya prasannacitto bodhāya cittamutpādya adhyāśayataḥ śṛṇuyādudgṛhṇīyād dhārayed vācayet paryavāpnuyāt pravartayed deśayedupadiśed uddiśet svādhyāyet parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayet arthamasyā vivṛṇuyāt manasānvavekṣeta yathādhikayā ca prajñayā atra parimīmāṃsām āpadyeta antaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā dhārayet sthāpayet saddharmacirasthitihetoḥ mā buddhanetrīsamucchedo bhūt mā saddharmāntardhānam
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, 'More merit than that, <s>Kauśika</s>, is produced by the son of good family or daughter of good family who, having faith in this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, accepting it, believing it, and being clear-minded, has generated the mind for awakening and listens to it with earnest intention, takes it up, retains it, recites it, masters it, sets it forth, teaches it, instructs in it, proclaims it, studies it, explains it in detail to others, makes its meaning clear, examines it mentally, enters into investigation of it with the highest wisdom available, and, even at least by putting it into a book, preserves it and establishes it for the long abiding of the true Dharma, thinking: May the Buddha-guide not be cut off; may the true Dharma not disappear.

children.text: bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ cānugrahopasaṃhāraḥ kṛto bhaviṣyati netryavaikalyeneti
children.translated_text: The favor and support of bodhisattvas, great beings, will have been accomplished, because the guide will not be impaired.'

children.text: tāṃ caināṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ satkuryāt gurukuryāt mānayet pūjayet arcayet apacāyet puṣpairdhūpairgandhairmālyair vilepanaiścūrṇairvastraiśchatrairdhvajairghaṇṭābhiḥ patākābhiḥ samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ pūjayet ayameva tataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati
children.translated_text: And if he were to honor this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, revere it, respect it, worship it, venerate it, and pay homage to it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, garments, parasols, banners, bells, flags, rows of lamps all around, and many kinds of offerings, then that very son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, would produce more merit than that.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika ayaṃ jambūdvīpaḥ saptaratnamayānāṃ tathāgatadhātugarbhāṇāṃ stūpānāṃ paripūrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Leave aside, moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> being filled with stūpas made of the seven precious substances and containing relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: sacetkauśika yāvantaś cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sarvasattvāḥ teṣāmekaikaḥ sattva ekaikaṃ saptaratnamayaṃ tathāgatadhātugarbhaṃ stūpaṃ kārayet taṃ ca yāvajjīvaṃ divyaiḥ puṣpair divyair dhūpair divyair gandhair divyairmālyairdivyaiścūrṇair divyairvastrairdivyaiśchatrair divyairdhvajair divyābhirghaṇṭābhir divyābhiḥ patākābhiḥ samantācca divyadīpamālābhiḥ bahuvidhābhiś ca divyābhiḥ pūjābhiḥ satkuryāt gurukuryāt mānayet pūjayet arcayet apacāyet tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu te sarvasattvāstatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasaveyuḥ śakra āha bahu bhagavan bahu sugata
children.translated_text: If, <s>Kauśika</s>, as many beings as there are in a four-continent world-system were each to have a <s>stūpa</s>, made of the seven precious substances and containing the relic-chamber of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, built, and were to honor it for as long as they lived with divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine powders, divine robes, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, divine flags, rows of divine lamps all around, and many kinds of divine worship, to revere it, esteem it, honor it, worship it, venerate it, and pay homage to it: what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would all those beings produce much merit from that cause? <s>Śakra</s> said: Much, Blessed One, much, <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: bhagavānāha ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām abhiśraddadhad avakalpayannadhimucya prasannacitto bodhāya cittamutpādya adhyāśayataḥ śṛṇuyādudgṛhṇīyāddhārayet vācayet paryavāpnuyāt pravartayet deśayet upadiśet uddiśet svādhyāyet parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayet arthamasyā vivṛṇuyāt manasānvavekṣeta yathādhikayā ca prajñayā atra parimīmāṃsām āpadyeta antaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā dhārayet sthāpayet saddharmacirasthitihetoḥ mā buddhanetrīsamucchedo bhūt mā saddharmāntardhānam

And if, <s>Kauśika</s>, all the beings there are in the trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra world-system, all of them, hypothetically, were to obtain a human personal existence without any first or last, and each single being were to have one stūpa made of the seven precious substances and containing a relic-deposit of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and each single being were to have all those stūpas made, and, after having had them made and established, were for an aeon or the remainder of an aeon to honor, revere, respect, worship, venerate, and pay homage to them with all instruments, all songs, all dances, all musical sounds and rhythms, with divine flowers of every kind, all incenses, all perfumes, all garlands, all ointments, all powders, all garments, with divine parasols, banners, bells, and flags, with rows of lamps everywhere around, and with many kinds of divine and human offerings of every sort: what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>?
