children.translated_text: Having looked at it, honored it, saluted it, taken it up, retained it, recited it, mastered it, set it forth, taught it, instructed in it, proclaimed it, and studied it, they will think that they should depart again.

children.text: tasya khalu punaḥ kauśika kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā gṛhaṃ vā layanaṃ vā prāsādo vā surakṣito bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, the house, dwelling, or mansion of that son of good family or daughter of good family will be well protected.

children.text: na ca tasya kaścidviheṭhako bhaviṣyati sthāpayitvā pūrvakarmavipākena
children.translated_text: And no one will harass that person, except through the ripening of former karma.

children.text: imam api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ guṇaṃ parigrahīṣyati yatra hi nāma evaṃ mahaujaskā devā nāgā yakṣā gandharvā asurā garuḍāḥ kinnarā mahoragā manuṣyā amanuṣyā vā āgantavyaṃ maṃsyante ||
children.translated_text: That son of good family or daughter of good family will also obtain this benefit visible in this very life, <s>Kauśika</s>: namely, that such powerful <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, or nonhumans will think that they should come there. ||

children.text: evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat kathaṃ punarbhagavan sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā evaṃ jānīyāt iha devā vā nāgā vā yakṣā vā gandharvā vā asurā vā garuḍā vā kinnarā vā mahoragā vā manuṣyā vā amanuṣyā vā āgacchanti imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ śrotuṃ draṣṭuṃ vandituṃ namaskartumudgrahītuṃ dhārayituṃ vācayituṃ paryavāptuṃ pravartayituṃ deśayitum upadeṣṭum uddeṣṭuṃ svādhyātumiti evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat sacetkauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatra udāramavabhāsaṃ saṃjānīte niṣṭhā tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā tatra gantavyā iha devo vā nāgo vā yakṣo vā gandharvo vā asuro vā garuḍo vā kinnaro vā mahorago vā manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vā āgata iti upasaṃkrānta iti
children.translated_text: When this had been said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "But how, Blessed One, should that son of good family or daughter of good family know, 'Here gods, or nāgas, or yakṣas, or gandharvas, or asuras, or garuḍas, or kinnaras, or mahoragas, or humans, or nonhumans are coming in order to hear, see, venerate, honor, take up, retain, recite, master, set forth, teach, instruct in, proclaim, and study this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>?'" When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "If, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son of good family or daughter of good family perceives a lofty radiance there, that son of good family or daughter of good family should come to the definite conclusion there: 'Here a god, or nāga, or yakṣa, or gandharva, or asura, or garuḍa, or kinnara, or mahoraga, or human, or nonhuman has come; has approached.'"

children.text: punaraparaṃ sacetkauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatra amānuṣaṃ gandhaṃ ghrāsyaty anāghrātapūrvam ghrātvā ca tadgandhaṃ niṣṭhā tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā tatra gantavyā iha devo vā nāgo vā yakṣo vā gandharvo vā asuro vā garuḍo vā kinnaro vā mahorago vā manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vā āgata iti upasaṃkrānta iti ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, if a son of good family or daughter of good family smells there a nonhuman fragrance, never smelled before, and after smelling that fragrance, that son of good family or daughter of good family should come to the definite conclusion there: 'Here a god, or nāga, or yakṣa, or gandharva, or asura, or garuḍa, or kinnara, or mahoraga, or human, or nonhuman has come; has approached.'

children.text: punaraparaṃ sacetkauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatra amānuṣaṃ gandhaṃ ghrāsyati anāghrātapūrvam ghrātvā ca tadgandhaṃ niṣṭhā tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā tatra gantavyāḥ iha devo vā nāgo vā yakṣo vā gandharvo vā asuro vā garuḍo vā kinnaro vā mahorago vā manuṣyo vāmanuṣyo vāgata iti upasaṃkrānta iti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, if a son of good family or daughter of good family smells there a nonhuman fragrance, never smelled before, and after smelling that fragrance, that son of good family or daughter of good family should come to the definite conclusion there: 'Here a god, or nāga, or yakṣa, or gandharva, or asura, or garuḍa, or kinnara, or mahoraga, or human, or nonhuman has come; has approached.'

children.text: punaraparaṃ sacetkauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā caukṣasamudācāro bhaviṣyati śucisamudācāro bhaviṣyati tasya tayā caukṣasamudācāratayā śucisamudācāratayā te devā nāgā yakṣā gandharvā asurā garuḍāḥ kinnarā mahoragā manuṣyā amanuṣyā vā āgantavyaṃ maṃsyante
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, if a son of good family or daughter of good family will be clean in conduct and pure in conduct, then because of that clean conduct and pure conduct, those gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, or nonhumans will think that they should come.

children.text: ye ca tatra devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā manuṣyā amanuṣyā vā āgatā bhaviṣyanti te tasya tayā caukṣasamudācāratayā śucisamudācāratayā āttamanaskāḥ pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātā bhaviṣyanti
children.translated_text: And whatever gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, or nonhumans will have come there, because of that clean conduct and pure conduct they will be pleased in mind, delighted, and filled with joy and gladness.

children.text: yāś ca tatra alpaujaskā alpaujaskā devatā adhyuṣitā bhaviṣyanti tāstato 'pakramitavyaṃ maṃsyante
children.translated_text: And whatever deities of little power, of little power, will have been dwelling there, they will think that they should depart from there.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ teṣāmeva hi mahaujaskānāṃ mahaujaskānāṃ devānāṃ nāgānāṃ yakṣāṇāṃ gandharvāṇāmasurāṇāṃ garuḍānāṃ kinnarāṇāṃ mahoragāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ amanuṣyāṇāṃ vā śriyaṃ ca tejaś ca gauravaṃ ca asahamānā eva tā alpaujaskā alpaujaskā devatā tato 'pakramitavyaṃ maṃsyante
children.translated_text: Why is that? Those very deities of little power, of little power, unable to bear the glory, brilliance, and dignity of those gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, or nonhumans of great power, of great power, will think that they should depart from there.

children.text: yathā yathā khalu punaḥ kauśika te mahaujaskā mahaujaskā devā nāgā yakṣā gandharvā asurā garuḍāḥ kinnarā mahoragā manuṣyā amanuṣyā vā abhīkṣṇamupasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyante tathā tathā sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā prasādabahulo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And, <s>Kauśika</s>, in whatever way those gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, or nonhumans of great power, of great power, will think that they should come near again and again, in that very way that son of good family or daughter of good family will become abundant in faith.

children.text: imam api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ guṇaṃ parigrahīṣyati
children.translated_text: That son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, will also acquire this benefit visible in this very life.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ kauśika kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā tasya dharmanetrīsthānasya parisāmantake 'śuciracaukṣasamudācāro na pracārayitavyaḥ tasyāṃ gurugauravatāparipūrimupādāya ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family should not carry on impure or unclean conduct in the neighborhood of that place of the guide to Dharma, out of regard for the fullness of heavy respect there.

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā na kāyaklamatho na cittaklamatha utpatsyate
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, neither bodily fatigue nor mental fatigue will arise for that son of good family or daughter of good family.

children.text: sa sukhameva śayyāṃ kalpayiṣyati sukhaṃ ca prakramiṣyati suptaś ca san na pāpakān svapnān drakṣyati paśyaṃś ca punastathāgatānevārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān drakṣyati stūpāneva drakṣyati bodhisattvāneva drakṣyati tathāgataśrāvakāneva drakṣyati
children.translated_text: He will prepare his bed comfortably, and he will set out comfortably; and while asleep he will not see bad dreams. And when he sees dreams, he will see only <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas; he will see only stūpas; he will see only bodhisattvas; he will see only disciples of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: śabdāṃś ca śṛṇvan pāramitāśabdāneva śroṣyati bodhipakṣāneva dharmān drakṣyati bodhivṛkṣāneva drakṣyati teṣu ca tathāgatānevārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhānabhisaṃbudhyamānān drakṣyati
children.translated_text: And when he hears sounds, he will hear only sounds of the perfections. He will see only dharmas belonging to awakening; he will see only trees of awakening; and at those he will see <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas in the act of awakening to full awakening.

children.text: tathā abhisaṃbuddhānāṃ ca dharmacakrapravartanaṃ drakṣyati bahūṃś ca bodhisattvāneva drakṣyati imāmeva prajñāpāramitāṃ saṃgāyamānān prajñāpāramitāsaṃgītiratān evaṃ sarvajñatā parigrahītavyā evaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ viśodhayitavyam ityupāyakauśalaṃ ca upadiśataḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, he will see the turning of the wheel of Dharma by those who have fully awakened; and he will see many bodhisattvas themselves, reciting this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, devoted to the recitation of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, and teaching skillful means in this way: 'Thus omniscience is to be acquired; thus the Buddha-field is to be purified.'

children.text: udāraṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatām abhisaṃbodhiśabdaṃ śroṣyati amuṣyāṃ diśi amuṣmin digbhāge amuṣmin lokadhātau amuko 'sau nāmnā tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakāṇāṃ śatairbahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakasahasrair bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakaśatasahasrair bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakakoṭībhir bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakakoṭīśatair bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakakoṭīsahasraiḥ bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakakoṭīśatasahasrair bahubhirbodhisattvaśrāvakakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto dharmaṃ deśayatīti
children.translated_text: And he will hear the noble sound of the awakening of the Blessed Buddhas: 'In that direction, in that quarter, in that world-system, that <s>Tathāgata</s>, arhat, perfectly awakened Buddha, named so-and-so, surrounded and attended by many hundreds of bodhisattvas and disciples, by many thousands of bodhisattvas and disciples, by many hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas and disciples, by many crores of bodhisattvas and disciples, by many hundreds of crores, many thousands of crores, many hundreds of thousands of crores, and many hundred-thousand niyutas of crores of bodhisattvas and disciples, is teaching the Dharma.'

children.text: yaś ca khalu punaḥ kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imānevaṃrūpān svapnān drakṣyati sa sukhameva svapsyati sukhaṃ ca pratibhotsyate ojaḥprakṣiptaṃ ca kāyaṃ sukhaṃ ca pratisaṃvedayiṣyati laghu laghveva ca pratisaṃvedayiṣyati
children.translated_text: And again, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family sees dreams of this sort will sleep happily and will wake happily; the body will be suffused with vigor, and he or she will experience comfort and will experience lightness, just lightness.

children.text: na cāsya adhimātrayā āhāragṛddhyā cittasaṃtatirutpatsyate
children.translated_text: And a continuum of thought marked by excessive greed for food will not arise in that person.

children.text: mṛdukā ca asya āhārasaṃjñā bhavati
children.translated_text: That person's perception of food will be gentle.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma kauśika bhikṣoryogācārasya samādhervyutthitasya manasikārapariṣyanditena cittena na balavatyāhāre gṛddhirbhavati mṛdukā cāsya āhārasaṃjñā bhavati evameva kauśika tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā na balavatyāhāre gṛddhirbhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Kauśika</s>, a monk practicing yoga, after rising from concentration, with a mind suffused by attention, does not have strong greed for food, and his perception of food is gentle, so too, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family will not have strong greed for food.

children.text: mṛdukā cāsya āhārasaṃjñā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And that person's perception of food will be gentle.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ evaṃ hyetatkauśika bhavati yathāpi nāma prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyogānuyuktatvāt tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā tathā hyasya amanuṣyāḥ kāye oja upasaṃhartavyaṃ maṃsyante
children.translated_text: Why is that? For this is how it is, <s>Kauśika</s>: because that son of good family or daughter of good family is devoted to the practice of cultivating the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the nonhumans will think that vigor should be supplied to that person's body.

children.text: imān api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikān guṇān parigṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: That son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, also takes hold of these benefits visible in this very life.

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā pūjāpūrvaṃgamaṃ sthāpayet pūjayennodgṛhṇīyānna dhārayenna vācayenna paryavāpnuyāt na pravartayenna deśayennopadiśennoddiśenna svādhyāyet ayameva tataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose a son of good family or daughter of good family, having written this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and made it into a book, should place it foremost for worship and should worship it, but should not take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, set it forth, teach it, instruct in it, proclaim it, or study it.

children.text: yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmabhiśraddadhadavakalpayannadhimucya prasannacitto bodhāya cittamutpādya adhyāśayataḥ śṛṇuyādudgṛhṇīyāddhārayedvācayet paryavāpnuyātpravartayeddeśayed upadiśeduddiśet svādhyāyet parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayet arthamasyā vivṛṇuyāt manasānvavekṣeta yathādhikayā ca prajñayā atra parimīmāṃsāmāpadyeta antaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā dhārayetsthāpayetsaddharmacirasthitihetoḥ mā buddhanetrīsamucchedo bhūt mā saddharmāntardhānam
children.translated_text: But suppose a son of good family or daughter of good family, believing in this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, accepting it, trusting it, with a clear mind and having generated the thought of awakening, should sincerely hear it, take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, set it forth, teach it, instruct in it, proclaim it, study it, explain it in detail to others, disclose its meaning, examine it mentally, and enter into investigation of it with whatever wisdom is available, and should at least make it into a book, keep it, and place it there for the sake of the long abiding of the true Dharma, thinking, 'Let there be no cutting off of the <s>Buddha-netrī</s>; let there be no disappearance of the true Dharma.

children.text: bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ cānugrahopasaṃhāraḥ kṛto bhaviṣyati netryavaikalyeneti
children.translated_text: Support and assistance will have been given to the bodhisattvas, the great beings, through the unimpaired condition of the guide.'

children.text: tāṃ caināṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ satkuryādgurukuryānmānayet pūjayedarcayedapacāyet puṣpairdhūpairgandhair mālyairvilepanaiścūrṇair vastraiśchatrairdhvajairghaṇṭābhiḥ patākābhiḥ samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ pūjayet ayameva tataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati
children.translated_text: And suppose that person should honor this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, treat it with respect, revere it, worship it, venerate it, and pay homage to it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, cloths, parasols, banners, bells, flags, rows of lamps all around, and many kinds of worship. This son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, produces much more merit on that account than the former.

children.text: tasmāttarhi kauśika imān dṛṣṭadhārmikān viśiṣṭān guṇān parigṛhītukāmena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā iyameva prajñāpāramitā abhiśraddhātavyā avakalpayitavyā adhibhoktavyā
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son of good family or daughter of good family who wishes to take hold of these distinguished benefits visible in this very life should believe in this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, accept it, and trust it.

children.text: prasannacittena bodhāya cittamutpādya satkṛtya adhyāśayena śrotavyā udgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā pravartayitavyā deśayitavyā upadeṣṭavyā uddeṣṭavyā svādhyātavyā parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyā arthato vivaritavyā manasānvavekṣitavyā yathādhikayā ca prajñayā atra parimīmāṃsāmāpadyeta
children.translated_text: With a clear mind, having generated the thought of awakening, it should be respectfully heard with sincere intention, taken up, retained, recited, mastered, set forth, taught, instructed in, proclaimed, studied, explained in detail to others, disclosed according to its meaning, examined mentally, and investigated with whatever wisdom is available.

children.text: antaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā sthāpayitavyā pūjayitavyā saddharmacirasthitihetoḥ mā buddhanetrīsamucchedo bhūt mā saddharmāntardhānam
children.translated_text: At the very least, it should be made into a book, placed, and worshiped for the sake of the long abiding of the true Dharma, thinking, 'Let there be no cutting off of the <s>Buddha-netrī</s>; let there be no disappearance of the true Dharma.

children.text: bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ cānugrahopasaṃhāraḥ kṛto bhaviṣyati netryavaikalyeneti
children.translated_text: Support and assistance will have been given to the bodhisattvas, the great beings, through the unimpaired condition of the guide.'

children.text: arthikānāṃ ca kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ ca saṃvibhāgaṃ kariṣyāmi mama ca pareṣāṃ ca kalyāṇasattvānāṃ buddhanetrīmahācakṣuravaikalyatā bhaviṣyatīti
children.translated_text: And I will share it with sons of good family and daughters of good family who seek it, and for me and for other good beings there will be the unimpaired condition of the <s>Buddha-netrī</s>, the great eye.'

children.text: sadā ca satkartavyā gurukartavyā mānayitavyā pūjayitavyā arcayitavyā apacāyitavyā puṣpairdhūpairgandhairmālyair vilepanaiścūrṇairvastraiśchatrair dhvajairghaṇṭābhiḥ patākābhiḥ samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ pūjayitavyeti ||
children.translated_text: And it should always be honored, treated as a teacher, revered, worshiped, venerated, and respected; it should be worshiped with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, cloths, parasols, banners, bells, flags, rows of lamps all around, and many kinds of offerings.

children.text: Chapter 4

punaraparaṃ bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindramāmantrayate sma sacetkauśika ayaṃ te jambūdvīpaḥ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhas tathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ dīyeta iyaṃ ca prajñāpāramitā likhitvopanāmyeta tata ekatareṇa bhāgena pravāryamāṇo 'nayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayoḥ katamaṃ tvaṃ kauśika bhāgaṃ gṛhṇīyāḥ śakra āha sacenme bhagavan ayaṃ jambūdvīpaḥ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhas tathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ dīyeta iyaṃ ca prajñāpāramitā likhitvopanāmyeta tata ekatareṇa bhāgena pravāryamāṇo 'nayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayorimāmevāhaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāṃ parigṛhṇīyām
children.translated_text: Moreover, the Blessed One addressed <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "If, <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, filled to the brim and heaped up with relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, were given to you, and this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, written down, were presented to you, then, being invited to choose one lot from these two lots set before you, which lot would you take, <s>Kauśika</s>?" <s>Śakra</s> said: "Blessed One, if this <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, filled to the brim and heaped up with relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, were given to me, and this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, written down, were presented to me, then, being invited to choose one lot from these two lots set before me, Blessed One, I would take this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>."

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ yathāpi nāma tathāgatanetrīcitrīkāreṇa
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because, as it were, it is distinguished as the guide of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.text: etaddhi tathāgatānāṃ bhūtārthikaṃ śarīram
children.translated_text: For this is the real body of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ uktaṃ hyetadbhagavatā dharmakāyā buddhā bhagavantaḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? For this has been said by the Blessed One: "The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are <s>dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-bodies).

children.text: mā khalu punarimaṃ bhikṣavaḥ satkāyaṃ kāyaṃ manyadhvam
children.translated_text: Monks, do not regard this individual physical body as the body.

children.text: dharmakāyapariniṣpattito māṃ bhikṣavo drakṣyatha
children.translated_text: Monks, you will see me through the complete realization of the <s>dharmakāya</s>.

children.text: eṣa ca tathāgatakāyo bhūtakoṭiprabhāvito draṣṭavyo yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: And this body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, made manifest from the limit of reality, is to be seen as precisely the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na khalu punarme bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣv agauravam
children.translated_text: Yet, Blessed One, it is not that I lack respect for those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: gauravameva me bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣu
children.translated_text: Blessed One, I do indeed have respect for those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: api tu khalu punarbhagavan itaḥ prajñāpāramitāto nirjātāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi pūjāṃ labhante
children.translated_text: But rather, Blessed One, the relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, born from this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, receive worship.

children.text: tasmāttarhi bhagavan anayaiva prajñāpāramitayā pūjitayā teṣām api tathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇā pūjā kṛtā bhavati
children.translated_text: Therefore, Blessed One, when this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is worshiped, full worship has also been performed for those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ prajñāpāramitānirjātatvāt tathāgataśarīrāṇām
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because the relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> are born from the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan sudharmāyāṃ devasabhāyāmahaṃ yasmin samaye divye svake āsane niṣaṇṇo bhavāmi tadā mama devaputrā upasthānāyāgacchanti
children.translated_text: For example, Blessed One, when I am seated on my own divine seat in the divine assembly hall <s>Sudharmā</s>, then my divine sons come to attend upon me.

children.text: yasmin samaye na niṣaṇṇo bhavāmi atha tasmin samaye yanmamāsanaṃ tatra devaputrā mama gauraveṇa tadāsanaṃ namaskṛtya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punareva prakrāmanti
children.translated_text: When I am not seated there, then at that time the divine sons, out of respect for me, bow to that seat of mine, circumambulate it, and then depart again.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ iha hi kila āsane niṣadya śakro devānāmindro devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayatīti
children.translated_text: Why is that? They think: "Here, seated on this seat, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, teaches Dharma to the gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>."

children.text: evameva bhagavan maheśākhyahetupratyayabhūtā prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: In just this way, Blessed One, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is a cause and condition of great power.

children.text: tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya sarvajñatāyā āhārikā
children.translated_text: It is what sustains the omniscience of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: sarvajñatāyāś ca tathāgataśarīrāṇyāśrayabhūtāni
children.translated_text: And the relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> are supports for omniscience.

children.text: na tu tāni pratyayabhūtāni na kāraṇabhūtāni jñānasyotpādāya
children.translated_text: But they are not conditions and not causes for the arising of knowledge.

children.text: evameva bhagavan sarvajñajñānahetukā tathāgataśarīreṣu pūjā kṛtā bhavati
children.translated_text: In this way, Blessed One, the worship performed toward the relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is grounded in the knowledge of omniscience.

children.text: tasmāttarhi bhagavan anayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayorimāmevāhaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāṃ parigṛhṇīyām
children.translated_text: Therefore, Blessed One, if these two lots were set before me, Blessed One, I would take this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na khalu punarme bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣv agauravam
children.translated_text: Yet, Blessed One, it is not that I lack respect for those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: gauravameva me bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣu
children.translated_text: Blessed One, I do indeed have respect for those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: api tu khalu punarbhagavaṃstāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi prajñāpāramitāparibhāvitatvāt pūjāṃ labhante
children.translated_text: But rather, Blessed One, those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> receive worship because they have been suffused by the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punarbhagavan ayaṃ jambūdvīpastathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhaḥ
children.translated_text: Let alone, Blessed One, this <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> filled to the brim and heaped up with relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu cāturmahādvīpako lokadhātustathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhaḥ
children.translated_text: Let alone a four-continent world-system filled to the brim and heaped up with relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu sāhasro lokadhātustathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhaḥ
children.translated_text: Let alone a thousandfold world-system filled to the brim and heaped up with relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu bhagavan dvisāhasro madhyamo lokadhātustathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhaḥ
children.translated_text: Let alone, Blessed One, a middle two-thousandfold world-system filled to the brim and heaped up with relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: ayameva bhagavaṃstrisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātustathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhaḥ eko bhāgaḥ kṛtvā sthāpyeta iyaṃ ca prajñāpāramitā likhitvā dvitīyo bhāgaḥ sthāpyeta
children.translated_text: If this very three-thousand great-thousand world-system, Blessed One, filled to the brim and heaped up with relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, were made into one lot and set aside, and this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, written down, were set aside as a second lot,

children.text: anayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayorekatareṇa bhāgena pravāryamāṇo 'nayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayoryaste bhāgo 'bhipretastamekaṃ bhāgaṃ gṛhāṇeti tatra imāmevāhaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāṃ parigṛhṇīyām
children.translated_text: and, when these two lots had been set before me, I were invited to choose one of them, saying, "Take whichever one lot of these two lots set before you is desired by you," then, Blessed One, I would take this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na khalu punarbhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣv agauravam
children.translated_text: Yet, Blessed One, it is not that I lack respect for those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: gauravameva me bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣu
children.translated_text: Blessed One, I do indeed have respect for those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: api tu khalu punarbhagavaṃstāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi prajñāpāramitāparibhāvitāni pūjāṃ labhante
children.translated_text: But rather, Blessed One, those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, suffused by the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, receive worship.

children.text: tathāgataśarīrāṇi hi sarvajñajñānāśrayabhūtāni
children.translated_text: For the relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> are supports for the knowledge of omniscience.

children.text: tad api sarvajñajñānaṃ prajñāpāramitānirjātam
children.translated_text: And that knowledge of omniscience too is born from the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tasmāttarhi bhagavan anayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayorimāmevāhaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāṃ parigṛhṇīyām
children.translated_text: Therefore then, Blessed One, if these two portions were set before me, Blessed One, I would take up this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na khalu punar me bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣv agauravam
children.translated_text: Yet, Blessed One, I certainly have no disrespect toward those bodies of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: gauravameva me bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣu
children.translated_text: Blessed One, I have only respect for those bodies of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: api tu khalu punarbhagavan itaḥ prajñāpāramitāto nirjātāni tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi pūjāṃ labhante yaduta prajñāpāramitāparibhāvitatvāt
children.translated_text: But rather, Blessed One, those bodies of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, born from this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, receive worship precisely because they have been pervaded by the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan anarghaṃ maṇiratnamebhirevaṃrūpairguṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ syāt
children.translated_text: It is, Blessed One, just as if there were a priceless jewel-gem endowed with such qualities.

children.text: tadyathā tadyatra yatra sthāpyeta tatra tatra manuṣyā vā amanuṣyā vā avatāraṃ na labheran
children.translated_text: Wherever and wherever it were placed, there and there humans or nonhumans would gain no opening against it.

children.text: yatra yatra vā amanuṣyagṛhītaḥ kaścidbhavet puruṣo vā strī vā tatra tatra tasmin maṇiratne praveśitamātre so 'manuṣyastato 'pakrāmet
children.translated_text: And wherever some man or woman had been seized by a nonhuman being, there, as soon as that jewel-gem was brought in, that nonhuman would withdraw from there.

children.text: vātenāpi bādhyamānasya dhamyamāne śarīre tanmaṇiratnaṃ sthāpyeta
children.translated_text: If that jewel-gem were placed on the body of one afflicted by wind, while the body was being blown about by wind,

children.text: tasya taṃ vātaṃ nigṛhṇīyāt na vivardhayet upaśamayet
children.translated_text: it would restrain that wind for him, would not increase it, and would pacify it.

children.text: pittenāpi dahyamāne śarīre sthāpyeta
children.translated_text: If it were placed on the body when it was burning with bile,

children.text: tasya tad api pittaṃ nigṛhṇīyāt na vivardhayet upaśamayet
children.translated_text: it would restrain that bile for him too, would not increase it, and would pacify it.

children.text: śleṣmaṇāpi parigṛddhe sarvato bādhyamāne śarīre sthāpyeta tasya tam api śleṣmāṇaṃ nigṛhṇīyāt na vivardhayet upaśamayet
children.translated_text: If it were placed on the body when it was obstructed by phlegm and afflicted on every side, it would restrain that phlegm for him too, would not increase it, and would pacify it.

children.text: sāṃnipātikenāpi vyādhinā duḥkhitasya śarīre sthāpyeta tasya tam api sāṃnipātikaṃ vyādhiṃ nigṛhṇīyāt na vivardhayet upaśamayet
children.translated_text: If it were placed on the body of one made miserable by a disease involving all three humors, it would restrain that disease involving all three humors for him too, would not increase it, and would pacify it.

children.text: andhakāratamisrāyāṃ ca rātrāvapyavabhāsaṃ kuryāt
children.translated_text: And even on a night of blind darkness it would give light.

children.text: uṣṇe cāpi vartamāne yasmin pṛthivīpradeśe sthāpyeta sa pṛthivīpradeśaḥ śītalo bhavet
children.translated_text: And when there was heat, whatever spot of earth it was placed on, that spot of earth would become cool.

children.text: śīte cāpi vartamāne yasmin pṛthivīpradeśe sthāpyeta sa pṛthivīpradeśa uṣṇo bhavet
children.translated_text: And when there was cold, whatever spot of earth it was placed on, that spot of earth would become warm.

children.text: yasmiṃś ca pṛthivīpradeśe āśīviṣā anuvicareyuḥ tathā anye 'pi kṣudrajantavaḥ tatrāpi pṛthivīpradeśe dhāryeta sthāpitaṃ vā bhavet te 'pyāśīviṣāste ca kṣudrajantavastato 'pakrāmeyuḥ
children.translated_text: And in whatever spot of earth poisonous snakes might be roaming, and other small creatures as well, if it were carried or placed in that spot of earth, those poisonous snakes and those small creatures too would withdraw from there.

children.text: sacedbhagavan strī vā puruṣo vā āśīviṣeṇa daṣṭo bhavet tasya tanmaṇiratnaṃ daśyeta tasya sahadaṃśanenaiva maṇiratnasya tadviṣaṃ pratihanyeta vigacchet
children.translated_text: If, Blessed One, a woman or man had been bitten by a poisonous snake and that jewel-gem were shown to that person, then, merely upon the showing of the jewel-gem, that poison would be checked and would disappear.

children.text: ebhiścānyaiś ca bhagavan evaṃrūpairguṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ tanmaṇiratnaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Blessed One, that jewel-gem would be endowed with these and other such qualities.

children.text: yeṣām api keṣāṃcidbhagavan akṣiṣvarbudaṃ vā timiraṃ vā akṣirogo vā paṭalaṃ vā bhavet teṣāṃ ca tanmaṇiratnamakṣiṣu sthāpyeta teṣāṃ sthāpitamātreṇaiva te 'kṣidoṣā nirghātaṃ praśamaṃ gaccheyuḥ
children.translated_text: And if any people had a swelling in the eyes, or dimness of sight, or eye disease, or a film over the eyes, and that jewel-gem were placed on their eyes, then as soon as it was placed there, those eye defects would go to destruction and pacification.

children.text: etaiś ca anyaiś ca bhagavan evaṃrūpairguṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ tanmaṇiratnaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Blessed One, that jewel-gem would be endowed with these and other such qualities.

children.text: yatra codake sthāpyeta tadapyudakamekavarṇaṃ kuryātsvakena varṇena
children.translated_text: And when it was placed in water, it would make that water of one color, with its own color.

children.text: sacetpāṇḍareṇa vastreṇa pariveṣṭya udake prakṣipyeta tadudakaṃ pāṇḍarīkuryāt
children.translated_text: If it were wrapped in a white cloth and thrown into water, it would make that water white.

children.text: evaṃ sacennīlena pītena lohitena māñjiṣṭhena eteṣāmanyeṣāṃ vā nānāprakārāṇāṃ vastrāṇāmanyatamena vastreṇa tanmaṇiratnaṃ veṣṭayitvā vā baddhvā vā udake prakṣipyeta tena tena vastrarāgeṇa tattatsvabhāvavarṇaṃ tadudakaṃ kuryāt
children.translated_text: So too, if that jewel-gem were wrapped or bound in a blue, yellow, red, madder-colored, or any other of these various kinds of cloths and thrown into water, it would make that water the natural color corresponding to each cloth-dye.

children.text: yo 'pi tasyodakasya kaluṣabhāvastam api prasādayet
children.translated_text: It would also clarify whatever muddy quality there was in that water.

children.text: ebhir api bhagavan evaṃrūpairguṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ tanmaṇiratnaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Blessed One, that jewel-gem would be endowed with these such qualities too. ||

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānandaḥ śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat kiṃ punaḥ kauśika devaloka eva tāni maṇiratnāni santi uta jāmbūdvīpakānām api manuṣyāṇāṃ tāni maṇiratnāni santi śakra āha deveṣvāryānanda tāni maṇiratnāni santi
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "But, <s>Kauśika</s>, do those jewel-gems exist only in the world of the gods, or do those jewel-gems also exist among the people of <s>Jāmbūdvīpa</s>?" <s>Śakra</s> said: "Noble <s>Ānanda</s>, those jewel-gems exist among the gods.

children.text: api tu khalu punarjāmbudvīpakānām api manuṣyāṇāṃ maṇiratnāni santi
children.translated_text: But, moreover, jewel-gems also exist among the people of <s>Jāmbūdvīpa</s>.

children.text: tāni tu gurukāṇi alpāni parīttāni guṇavikalāni na taistathārūpairguṇaiḥ samanvāgatāni
children.translated_text: Those, however, are heavy, few, limited, and deficient in qualities; they are not endowed with qualities of such a kind.

children.text: tatteṣāṃ divyānāṃ maṇiratnānāṃ śatatamīm api kalāṃ nopayānti sahasratamīmapi śatasahasratamīmapi koṭītamīmapi koṭīśatatamīmapi koṭīsahasratamīmapi koṭīśatasahasratamīmapi koṭīniyutaśatasahasratamīm api kalāṃ nopayānti saṃkhyām api kalām api gaṇanām api upamām api aupamyam api upanisām api upaniṣadam api na kṣamante nopayānti
children.translated_text: They do not approach even a hundredth part of those divine jewel-gems, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor a ten-millionth part, nor a hundred ten-millionth part, nor a thousand ten-millionth part, nor a hundred-thousand ten-millionth part, nor a hundred-thousand niyuta of ten-millions part; they do not bear comparison in number, fraction, reckoning, likeness, analogy, approximation, or even in the secret point; they do not approach them.

children.text: yāni khalu punardeveṣu tāni laghūni sarvākāraguṇaparipūrṇāni
children.translated_text: But those that are among the gods are light and complete in qualities in every respect.

children.text: yatra ca karaṇḍake tanmaṇiratnaṃ prakṣiptaṃ bhavati utkṣiptaṃ vā tata uddhṛte 'pi tasmin maṇiratne karaṇḍakāt spṛhaṇīya eva sa karaṇḍako bhavati
children.translated_text: And into whatever box that jewel-gem has been put or lifted, even when that jewel-gem has been taken out of the box, that box remains desirable.

children.text: tairmaṇiratnaguṇaiḥ parā tatra karaṇḍake spṛhotpadyate
children.translated_text: Because of those qualities of the jewel-gems, longing arises there for that box.

children.text: evameva bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyā ete guṇāḥ sarvajñajñānasya ca
children.translated_text: In just this way, Blessed One, these are the qualities of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and of the knowledge of omniscience.

children.text: yena parinirvṛtasyāpi tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi pūjāṃ labhante sarvajñajñānasyemāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi bhājanabhūtānyabhūvanniti
children.translated_text: Because through it, even when the <s>Tathāgata</s>, arhat, perfectly awakened Buddha has passed into parinirvāṇa, those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> receive worship, for these relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> had become vessels for the knowledge of omniscience.

children.text: yathā ca bhagavan sarvalokadhātuṣu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmadeśanā prajñāpāramitānirjātatvātpūjyā evaṃ dharmabhāṇakasya dharmadeśanā prajñāpāramitānirjātatvātpūjyā
children.translated_text: And just as, Blessed One, the Dharma teaching of the blessed Buddhas in all world-systems is worthy of worship because it has arisen from the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, so too the Dharma teaching of the Dharma-preacher is worthy of worship because it has arisen from the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: yathā ca bhagavan rājapuruṣo rājānubhāvānmahato janakāyasya akutobhayaḥ pūjyaḥ evaṃ sa dharmabhāṇako dharmakāyānubhāvānmahato janakāyasya akutobhayaḥ pūjyaḥ
children.translated_text: And just as, Blessed One, a royal officer, through the king's authority, is fearless before a great mass of people and is worthy of honor, so that Dharma-preacher, through the authority of the <s>dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body), is fearless before a great mass of people and is worthy of honor.

children.text: yathā ca dharmadeśanā dharmabhāṇakāś ca pūjāṃ labhante evaṃ tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi pūjāṃ labhante
children.translated_text: And just as Dharma teachings and Dharma-preachers receive worship, so too those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> receive worship.

children.text: tasmāttarhi bhagavan tiṣṭhatu trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātustathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇaścūlikābaddhaḥ ye 'pi bhagavan gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātavaḥ te 'pi sarve tathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ paripūrṇāścūlikābaddhā eko bhāgaḥ sthāpyeta iyaṃ ca prajñāpāramitā likhitvā dvitīyo bhāgaḥ sthāpyeta
children.translated_text: Therefore then, Blessed One, let the three-thousand great-thousand world-system stand aside, filled with relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and piled up like a crest; and even all the world-systems equal to the sands of the Ganges River, Blessed One, filled with relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and piled up like a crest, may be set aside as one portion, while this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, written out, may be set aside as a second portion.

children.text: tatra cenmāṃ bhagavan kaścideva pravārayedanyatareṇa bhāgena pravāryamāṇo 'nayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayoḥ yaste bhāgo 'bhipretaḥ tamekaṃ bhāgaṃ parigṛhṇīṣveti tatra imāmevāhaṃ bhagavaṃstayordvayorbhāgayoḥ sthāpitayorbhāgaṃ gṛhṇīyāṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitām
children.translated_text: If then, Blessed One, someone were to invite me to choose one or the other portion, saying, while these two portions were set before me, 'Take whichever one portion of these two portions set here is desired by you,' then, Blessed One, from those two portions set before me I would take precisely this portion, namely the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na khalu punarbhagavan mama teṣu tathāgataśarīreṣvagauravam
children.translated_text: Yet, Blessed One, I certainly do not lack reverence for those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: gauravameva bhagavaṃsteṣu tathāgataśarīreṣu
children.translated_text: Indeed, Blessed One, I have reverence for those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: api tu khalu punarbhagavan prajñāpāramitāparibhāvitā sarvajñatā sarvajñatānirjātā ca tathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ pūjā bhavati
children.translated_text: But rather, Blessed One, omniscience is cultivated by the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, and the worship of the relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is born from omniscience.

children.text: tasmāttarhi bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pūjitāyām atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūjā kṛtā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore then, Blessed One, when the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is worshiped, worship has been done to the blessed Buddhas of the past, future, and present. ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ bhagavan ye 'prameyeṣvasaṃkhyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavanta etarhi tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti tān dharmatayā draṣṭukāmena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caritavyam prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yogamāpattavyam
children.translated_text: Moreover, Blessed One, a son of good family or daughter of good family who wishes to see according to <s>dharmatā</s> (reality as it is) the blessed Buddhas who now stand, remain, and pass their lives in immeasurable, incalculable world-systems should practice in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and should enter into application in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: prajñāpāramitā bhāvayitavyā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> should be cultivated. ||

children.text: evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat evametatkauśika evam etat
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>; so it is.'

children.text: ye 'pi te kauśika abhūvannatīte 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ te 'pi kauśika imāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas who existed in the past time and fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, they too, <s>Kauśika</s>, fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening by relying on this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: ye 'pi te kauśika bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ te 'pi kauśika imāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante
children.translated_text: Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas who will exist in the future time, they too, <s>Kauśika</s>, will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening by relying on this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: ye 'pi te kauśika etarhi aprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti te 'pi kauśika buddhā bhagavantaḥ imāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: And those blessed Buddhas who now stand, remain, and pass their lives in immeasurable, incalculable world-systems, those blessed Buddhas too, <s>Kauśika</s>, have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening by relying on this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: aham api kauśika etarhi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ imāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I too, <s>Kauśika</s>, now a <s>Tathāgata</s>, arhat, perfectly awakened Buddha, have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening by relying on this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. ||

children.text: evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat mahāpāramiteyaṃ bhagavan yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: When this had been said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: 'Great is this perfection, Blessed One, namely the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

children.text: sarvasattvānāṃ hi bhagavaṃstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaścittacaritāni samyak prajānāti saṃpaśyati
children.translated_text: For, Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, arhat, perfectly awakened Buddha rightly knows and sees the movements of mind of all beings.

children.text: bhagavānāha evametatkauśika evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>; so it is.'

children.text: tathā hi kauśika bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dīrgharātraṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati tena sarvasattvānāṃ cittacaritāni prajñāpāramitāyāṃ samyak prajānāti saṃpaśyati ||
children.translated_text: For thus, <s>Kauśika</s>, the bodhisattva great being practices for a long time in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>; therefore, in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, he rightly knows and sees the movements of mind of all beings. ||

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat kiṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāmeva bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati nānyāsu pāramitāsu bhagavānāha sarvāsu kauśika ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu bodhisattvo mahāsattvaścarati
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: 'Does the bodhisattva great being practice only in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, Blessed One, and not in the other perfections?' The Blessed One said: 'The bodhisattva great being practices in all six perfections, <s>Kauśika</s>.'

children.text: api tu khalu punaḥ kauśika prajñāpāramitaiva atra pūrvaṃgamā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya dānaṃ vā dadataḥ śīlaṃ vā rakṣataḥ kṣāntyā vā saṃpādayamānasya vīryaṃ vā ārabhamāṇasya dhyānaṃ vā samāpadyamānasya dharmān vā vipaśyataḥ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitaivātra pūrvaṃgamā
children.translated_text: But nevertheless, <s>Kauśika</s>, here the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> alone goes before the bodhisattva great being: when the bodhisattva great being gives a gift, or guards morality, or brings patience to completion, or undertakes vigor, or enters meditation, or sees dharmas with insight, here the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> alone goes before him.

children.text: na ca kauśika āsāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānām upāyakauśalyaparigṛhītānāṃ prajñāpāramitāpariṇāmitānāṃ sarvajñatāpariṇāmitānāṃ viśeṣaḥ na ca nānākaraṇamupalabhyate
children.translated_text: And, <s>Kauśika</s>, among these six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), when they are embraced by <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skill in means), dedicated to <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, and dedicated to omniscience, no distinction and no difference is perceived.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma kauśika jambudvīpe nānāvṛkṣā nānāvarṇā nānāsaṃsthānā nānāpatrā nānāpuṣpā nānāphalā nānārohapariṇāhasampannāḥ na ca teṣāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ chāyāyā viśeṣo vā nānākaraṇaṃ vā prajñāyate api tu chāyā chāyetyevaṃ saṃkhyāṃ gacchati evameva kauśika āsāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānām upāyakauśalyaparigṛhītānāṃ prajñāpāramitāpariṇāmitānāṃ sarvajñatāpariṇāmitānāṃ na viśeṣaḥ na ca nānākaraṇamupalabhyate
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Kauśika</s>, in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> there are various trees, of various colors, various forms, various leaves, various flowers, various fruits, and endowed with various heights and girths; yet no distinction or difference is discerned in the shade of those trees. Rather, it is counted simply as shade. In just the same way, <s>Kauśika</s>, among these six <s>pāramitās</s>, when they are embraced by skill in means, dedicated to <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, and dedicated to omniscience, no distinction and no difference is perceived.

children.text: evamukte śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat mahāguṇasamanvāgateyaṃ bhagavan yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: When this had been said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is endowed with great qualities.

children.text: aprameyaguṇasamanvāgateyaṃ bhagavan yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Blessed One, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is endowed with immeasurable qualities.

children.text: aparyantaguṇasamanvāgateyaṃ bhagavan yaduta prajñāpāramiteti ||
children.translated_text: Blessed One, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is endowed with endless qualities." ||

children.text: Chapter 5

atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat yo bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmabhiśraddadhadavakalpayannadhimucya prasannacitto bodhāya cittamutpādya adhyāśayataḥ śṛṇuyādudgṛhṇīyāddhārayedvācayet paryavāpnuyāt pravartayeddeśayed upadiśeduddiśet svādhyāyet parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayet arthamasyā vivṛṇuyāt manasānvavekṣeta yathādhikayā ca prajñayā atra parimīmāṃsāmāpadyeta antaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā dhārayetsthāpayetsaddharmacirasthitihetoḥ mā buddhanetrīsamucchedo bhūt mā saddharmāntardhānam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, suppose a son of good family or daughter of good family, believing in this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, accepting it, trusting it, with a clear mind, and having generated the thought of awakening, should sincerely hear it, take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, set it forth, teach it, instruct in it, proclaim it, study it, and make it extensively known to others; should explain its meaning, examine it mentally, and enter into investigation of it with whatever wisdom is available; and should at least make it into a book, keep it, and place it there for the sake of the long abiding of the true Dharma, thinking, 'Let there be no cutting off of the <s>Buddha-netrī</s>; let there be no disappearance of the true Dharma.

children.text: bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ ca anugrahopasaṃhāraḥ kṛto bhaviṣyati netryavaikalyeneti
children.translated_text: Support and assistance will have been given to the bodhisattvas, the great beings, through the unimpaired condition of the guide.'

children.text: evamimaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvā evaṃ mahārthikā bateyaṃ prajñāpāramitā evaṃ mahānuśaṃsā evaṃ mahāphalā evaṃ mahāvipākā bateyaṃ prajñāpāramitā evaṃ bahuguṇasamanvāgateyaṃ prajñāpāramitā aparityajanīyā mayā prajñāpāramitā rakṣitavyā mama prajñāpāramitā gopāyitavyā mama prajñāpāramitā paramadurlabhā hīyaṃ prajñāpāramitetyadhimuñcet
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction, one should resolve: 'Indeed, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is of great benefit. Indeed, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> has great advantages, great fruit, and great result. This <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is endowed with many qualities. This <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> must not be abandoned by me. This <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> must be protected by me. This <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> must be guarded by me. For this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is exceedingly hard to find.'

children.text: svayameva caināṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ satkuryādgurukuryānmānayet pūjayedarcayedapacāyet puṣpairdhūpairgandhair mālyairvilepanaiścūrṇair vastraiśchatrairdhvajairghaṇṭābhiḥ patākābhiḥ samantācca dīpamālābhiḥ bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ yo vā anyaḥ sampūjya parasmai cārthikāya chandikāya kulaputrāya kuladuhitre vā yācamānāya dadyādupanāmayenniryātayetparityajet antaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā
children.translated_text: And that person should himself honor this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, treat it with respect, revere it, worship it, venerate it, and pay homage to it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, cloths, parasols, banners, bells, flags, rows of lamps all around, and many kinds of worship. Or else, after worshiping it, he should give, offer, hand over, and relinquish it to another son of good family or daughter of good family who wants it, desires it, and asks for it, even after making it into a book.

children.text: katarastayorbhagavan kulaputrayoḥ kuladuhitrorvā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet yo vā parityāgabuddhiryo vā na parityāgabuddhiḥ evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat tena hi kauśika tvāmevātra pratiprakṣyāmi
children.translated_text: Blessed One, which of those sons of good family or daughters of good family would produce greater merit: the one whose intention is to give it away, or the one whose intention is not to give it away?" When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "Then, <s>Kauśika</s>, I will question you yourself about this.

children.text: yathā te kṣamate vyākuryāḥ
children.translated_text: Answer as seems fitting to you.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya śarīraṃ satkṛtya paricareddhārayet satkuryādgurukuryānmānayet pūjayedarcayedapacāyet svayameva
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Suppose a son of good family or daughter of good family, after the <s>Tathāgata</s> has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, should respectfully attend to his bodily relic, keep it, honor it, treat it with respect, revere it, worship it, venerate it, and pay homage to it by himself.

children.text: yo vā anyaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tathāgataśarīraṃ svayaṃ ca satkuryādgurukuryānmānayet pūjayedarcayedapacāyet parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayet dadyāt saṃvibhajet vaistārikī pūjā bhaviṣyatīti sattvānāṃ cānukampāmupādāya
children.translated_text: Or suppose another son of good family or daughter of good family should himself honor the bodily relic of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, treat it with respect, revere it, worship it, venerate it, and pay homage to it, and should also make it extensively known to others, give it, and share it, thinking, 'There will be widespread worship,' out of compassion for beings.

children.text: katarastayordvayoḥ kulaputrayoḥ kuladuhitrorvā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet kiṃ yaḥ svayaṃ ca pūjayet parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayeddadyāt saṃvibhajet kiṃ vā yaḥ svayameva pratyātmaṃ pūjayet śakra āha yo bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā svayaṃ ca tathāgataśarīraṃ satkuryādgurukuryānmānayet pūjayedarcayedapacāyet parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayeddadyātsaṃvibhajet vaistārikī pūjā bhaviṣyatīti sattvānāṃ cānukampāmupādāya ayam evānayor dvayoḥ kulaputrayoḥ kuladuhitrorvā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati
children.translated_text: Which of those two sons of good family or daughters of good family would produce greater merit? Is it the one who both worships it himself and makes it extensively known to others, gives it, and shares it, or the one who worships it only by himself, privately?" <s>Śakra</s> said: "Blessed One, the son of good family or daughter of good family who both honors the bodily relic of the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, treats it with respect, reveres it, worships it, venerates it, and pays homage to it, and also makes it extensively known to others, gives it, and shares it, thinking, 'There will be widespread worship,' out of compassion for beings, that one alone, of these two sons of good family or daughters of good family, produces greater merit."

children.text: bhagavānāha evametatkauśika evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>; so it is."

children.text: evametatkauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā udgṛhṇīyāddhārayedvācayet paryavāpnuyāt pravartayeddeśayedupadiśed uddiśetsvādhyāyet parasmai cārthikāya chandikāya kulaputrāya kuladuhitre vā yācamānāya dadyādupanāmayenniryātayetparityajedantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā
children.translated_text: So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>. If a son of good family or daughter of good family, after writing this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and making it into a book, should take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, set it forth, teach it, instruct in it, proclaim it, and study it, and should give it, offer it, hand it over, and relinquish it to another son of good family or daughter of good family who is interested, desirous, and asking for it, even if only after making it into a book,

children.text: ayameva kauśika tayordvayoḥ kulaputrayoḥ kuladuhitrorvā parānugrahakaraḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā parityāgabuddhistannidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati ||
children.translated_text: then, <s>Kauśika</s>, of those two sons of good family or daughters of good family, this very son of good family or daughter of good family who benefits others and has the thought of giving produces much more merit on that account. ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā yatra yatra bhājanībhūtāḥ kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā syuḥ asyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ tatra tatra gatvā tebhyaḥ imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ dadyāt saṃvibhāgaṃ kuryāt ayameva kauśika tataḥ kulaputrātkuladuhiturvā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, if a son of good family or daughter of good family, wherever sons of good family or daughters of good family are worthy vessels for this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, should go there and there and give this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> to them and make a sharing of it, then, <s>Kauśika</s>, that person would produce much more merit than that son of good family or daughter of good family. ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā ye jambūdvīpe sattvāstān sarvān daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayet pratiṣṭhāpayet tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet śakra āha bahu bhagavan bahu sugata
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose a son of good family or daughter of good family were to cause all the beings in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> to undertake the ten wholesome paths of action and establish them in them. What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account? <s>Śakra</s> said, "Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>."

children.text: bhagavānāha ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet yaḥ imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhad abhiśraddadhate avakalpayannavakalpayate adhimuñcannadhimucyate prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya adhyāśayasampanno 'dhyāśayasampannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāya adhyāśayena dadyāt antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpyakilāsitayā sampādayet udyukto 'muṃ grāhayet saṃdarśayet samādāpayet samuttejayet saṃpraharṣayet vācā neṣyati vineṣyati arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminn eva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "More than that, <s>Kauśika</s>, would be the merit produced by a son of good family or daughter of good family who, even after merely making this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> into a book, believing in it, accepting it, trusting it, with a clear mind, with a noble intention, having generated the thought of awakening, should give it with sincere intention to a bodhisattva whose thought of awakening has been generated, or who should at least, without weariness, make it available for writing or recitation; who, exerting himself, should cause that person to grasp it, show it, cause him to undertake it, rouse him, gladden him, guide and train him by speech, explain its meaning to him, purify his mind in this way, make him free from doubt, and say this to him: 'Come, son of good family, train in this very bodhisattva path.

children.text: atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase
children.translated_text: For while you train here, practice, and exert yourself, you will very quickly fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti
children.translated_text: And after fully awakening, you will lead an immeasurable realm of beings to unsurpassed exhaustion of the supports, that is, to the realization of the limit of reality.'

children.text: ayaṃ kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā parityāgabuddhyā tataḥ paurvakātkulaputrātkuladuhiturvā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet
children.translated_text: This son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, through the thought of giving, would produce much more merit than the earlier son of good family or daughter of good family.

children.text: tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ kauśika jambūdvīpe sarvasattvāḥ etena kauśika paryāyeṇa ye 'pi te kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayet pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let alone, then, <s>Kauśika</s>, all the beings in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>. By this method, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to cause even all the beings in the four-continent world-system to undertake the ten wholesome paths of action and establish them in them.

children.text: tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sarvasattvāḥ etena paryāyeṇa ye 'pi te kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayet pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let alone, then, <s>Kauśika</s>, all the beings in the four-continent world-system. By this method, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to cause even all the beings in the small thousand world-system to undertake the ten wholesome paths of action and establish them in them.

children.text: tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sarvasattvāḥ etena paryāyeṇa ye 'pi te kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayet pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let alone, then, <s>Kauśika</s>, all the beings in the small thousand world-system. By this method, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to cause even all the beings in the middle two-thousand world-system to undertake the ten wholesome paths of action and establish them in them.

children.text: tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sarvasattvāḥ etena paryāyeṇa ye 'pi te kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayet pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let alone, then, <s>Kauśika</s>, all the beings in the middle two-thousand world-system. By this method, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to cause even all the beings in the three-thousand great-thousand world-system to undertake the ten wholesome paths of action and establish them in them.

children.text: tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvāḥ etena kauśika paryāyeṇa yāvanto gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayet pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let alone, then, <s>Kauśika</s>, all the beings in the three-thousand great-thousand world-system. By this method, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to cause all the beings, as many as there are in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems equal in number to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, to undertake the ten wholesome paths of action and establish them in them.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet śakra āha bahu bhagavan bahu sugata ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account? <s>Śakra</s> said, "Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>." ||

children.text: bhagavānāha ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate avakalpayannavakalpayate adhimuñcannadhimucyate prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya adhyāśayasampanno 'dhyāśayasampannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāya adhyāśayena dadyāt antaśaḥ likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā sampādayet udyukto 'muṃ grāhayet saṃdarśayet samādāpayet samuttejayet saṃpraharṣayet vācā neṣyati vineṣyati arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asmin eva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Therefore, moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family would produce much greater merit who, after making this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), even if only into a book, believing in it, accepting it, trusting it, with a clear mind and sincere intention, having generated the thought of awakening, should give it sincerely to a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has generated the thought of awakening; or who, even for writing it or reciting it, should tirelessly provide assistance, should energetically make him grasp it, show it, make him undertake it, encourage him, gladden him, lead and guide him by speech, explain its meaning to him, purify his mind in this way, make him free from doubt, and say to him in this way: 'Come, son of good family, train in this very path of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase
children.translated_text: For, training here, practicing, and striving, you will very quickly fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti
children.translated_text: And after fully awakening, you will guide the immeasurable realm of beings into the unsurpassed extinction of the substrata, that is, into the manifestation of the reality-limit.'

children.text: ayaṃ kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā parityāgabuddhyā tataḥ paurvakātkulaputrātkuladuhiturvā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ||
children.translated_text: This son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, because of the intention of relinquishing, would produce much greater merit than the former son of good family or daughter of good family. ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yāvanto jambūdvīpe sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā caturṣu dhyāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings there are in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions).

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet śakra āha bahu bhagavan bahu sugata ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account? <s>Śakra</s> said: "Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>." ||

children.text: bhagavānāha ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate avakalpayannavakalpayate adhimuñcannadhimucyate prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya adhyāśayasampanno 'dhyāśayasampannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāya adhyāśayena dadyāt antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā sampādayet udyukto 'muṃ grāhayet saṃdarśayet samādāpayet samuttejayet saṃpraharṣayet vācā neṣyati vineṣyati arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asmin eva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Therefore, moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family would produce much greater merit who, after making this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, even if only into a book, believing in it, accepting it, trusting it, with a clear mind and sincere intention, having generated the thought of awakening, should give it sincerely to a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has generated the thought of awakening; or who, even for writing it or reciting it, should tirelessly provide assistance, should energetically make him grasp it, show it, make him undertake it, encourage him, gladden him, lead and guide him by speech, explain its meaning to him, purify his mind in this way, make him free from doubt, and say to him in this way: 'Come, son of good family, train in this very path of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase
children.translated_text: For, training here, practicing, and striving, you will very quickly fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti
children.translated_text: And after fully awakening, you will guide the immeasurable realm of beings into the unsurpassed extinction of the substrata, that is, into the manifestation of the reality-limit.'

children.text: tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ kauśika jambudvīpe sarvasattvāḥ etena paryāyeṇa ye 'pi te kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā caturṣu dhyāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let all the beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> stand aside, <s>Kauśika</s>. By this same method, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings, too, who are in the world-system of the four great continents, in the four <s>dhyānas</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sarvasattvāḥ etena paryāyeṇa ye 'pi te kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā caturṣu dhyāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet

By this same method, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings, too, who are in the small thousandfold world-system, in the four <s>dhyānas</s>.

children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings there are in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in the four immeasurables; the formula should be expanded in this way.

children.text: yathā caturṣvapramāṇeṣu evaṃ catasṛṣvārūpyasamāpattiṣu pañcasvabhijñāsu yāvatsamastāsu dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: As with the four immeasurables, so too one should say that he would establish them in the four formless attainments, in the five superknowledges, and up to all the meditations, immeasurables, formless attainments, and superknowledges.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet śakra āha bahu bhagavan bahu sugata ||

children.translated_text: And after fully awakening, you will guide an immeasurable realm of beings into the unsurpassed exhaustion of basis, that is, into the manifestation of the reality-limit.'

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika jāmbūdvīpakān sarvasattvān dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ anena paryāyeṇa ye 'pi te kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Leave aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the accumulation of merit from establishing all beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, by this method, in the meditations, immeasurables, formless attainments, and superknowledges. Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings who are in a world-system of four great continents in the meditations, immeasurables, formless attainments, and superknowledges.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sarvasattvān dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ ye 'pi te kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Leave aside again, <s>Kauśika</s>, the accumulation of merit from establishing all beings in a world-system of four great continents in the meditations, immeasurables, formless attainments, and superknowledges. Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings who are in a small thousandfold world-system in the meditations, immeasurables, formless attainments, and superknowledges.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sarvasattvān dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ ye 'pi te kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Leave aside again, <s>Kauśika</s>, the accumulation of merit from establishing all beings in a small thousandfold world-system in the meditations, immeasurables, formless attainments, and superknowledges. Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings who are in a middle two-thousandfold world-system in the meditations, immeasurables, formless attainments, and superknowledges.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sarvasattvān dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ ye 'pi te kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet

Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings who are in a three-thousand great-thousand world-system in the meditations, immeasurables, formless attainments, and superknowledges.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvān dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ anena paryāyeṇa ye 'pi kecitkauśika gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let alone, moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, the production of merit from establishing all beings in a three-thousand great-thousand world-system in the meditations, immeasurable states, formless attainments, and higher knowledges. In this manner, <s>Kauśika</s>, if some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems equal in number to the sands of the Ganges River in the meditations, immeasurable states, formless attainments, and higher knowledges,

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet śakra āha bahu bhagavan bahu sugata ||
children.translated_text: what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account? <s>Śakra</s> said: "Much, Blessed One, much, <s>Sugata</s>." ||

children.text: bhagavānāha ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate avakalpayannavakalpayate adhimuñcannadhimucyate prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya adhyāśayasampanno 'dhyāśayasampannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāya adhyāśayena dadyāt antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā saṃpādayiṣyati udyukto 'muṃ grāhayiṣyati saṃdarśayiṣyati samādāpayiṣyati samuttejayiṣyati saṃpraharṣayiṣyati vācā neṣyati vineṣyati anuneṣyati arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminn eva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "But, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son of good family or daughter of good family would produce still more merit than that, if, having made even this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> into a book, and believing in it, accepting it, trusting it, with a clear mind and sincere intention, having generated the thought of awakening, he or she were to give it sincerely to a bodhisattva who has generated the thought of awakening; or if he or she would tirelessly make it available even for writing and recitation, and, being energetic, would make that person grasp it, show it, cause him to take it up, incite him, gladden him, lead him on by speech, guide him, encourage him, explain its meaning to him, purify his mind in this way, make him free from doubt, and say to him in this way: 'Come, son of good family, train in just this bodhisattva path.
