children.translated_text: For while training here, practicing, and exerting yourself, you will very quickly fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti ||
children.translated_text: And having fully awakened, you will lead the immeasurable realm of beings to unsurpassed extinction without remainder, that is, to the manifestation of the limit of reality.'" ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā svayaṃ ca vācayet parebhyaś ca likhitvā pūrvavaddadyāt ayatnataḥ kauśika pūrvakātkulaputrātkuladuhiturvā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son of good family or daughter of good family who, after writing this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, would recite it himself or herself and, after writing it, would give it to others as before, would effortlessly produce more merit than the previous son of good family or daughter of good family.

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmarthakuśalo vācayet parebhyaś ca likhitvā pūrvavaddadyāt sārthāṃ savyañjanāmupadiśet paridīpayet ayatnataḥ kauśika sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son of good family or daughter of good family who, skilled in its meaning, would recite this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, and after writing it would give it to others as before, and would teach and illuminate it together with its meaning and wording, that son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, would effortlessly produce still more merit. ||

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat iyam api bhagavan prajñāpāramitā upadeṣṭavyāḥ evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat iyam api kauśika prajñāpāramitā upadeṣṭavyā abudhyamānasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> too should be taught." When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "<s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> too should be taught to a son of good family or daughter of good family who does not understand.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ utpatsyate hi kauśika anāgate 'dhvani prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikā
children.translated_text: Why? For, <s>Kauśika</s>, in a future time there will arise a counterfeit of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tatra abudhyamānaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmo mā praṇaṃkṣīttāṃ prajñāpāramitā prativarṇikāṃ śrutvā ||
children.translated_text: There, a son of good family or daughter of good family who does not understand and desires to fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening should not be ruined after hearing that counterfeit <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. ||

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat kathaṃ bhagavan anāgate 'dhvani prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikā veditavyā iyaṃ sā prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikopadiśyata iti evamukte bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat bhaviṣyanti kauśika anāgate 'dhvani eke bhikṣavaḥ abhāvitakāyā abhāvitaśīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitaprajñā eḍamūkajātīyāḥ prajñāparihīṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, how should it be known in a future time, 'This is that counterfeit <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> being taught'?" When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "<s>Kauśika</s>, in a future time there will be certain monks whose bodies have not been cultivated, whose morality has not been cultivated, whose minds have not been cultivated, whose wisdom has not been cultivated, who are like blockheads and mutes, and who are bereft of wisdom.

children.text: te prajñāpāramitāmupadekṣyāma iti tasyāḥ prativarṇikāmupadekṣyanti
children.translated_text: Saying, 'We will teach the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>,' they will teach its counterfeit.

children.text: kathaṃ ca kauśika prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikām upadekṣyanti rūpavināśo rūpānityatetyupadekṣyanti
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Kauśika</s>, will they teach the counterfeit of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>? They will teach: 'The destruction of form is the impermanence of form.'

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: vijñānavināśo vijñānānityatetyupadekṣyanti
children.translated_text: They will teach: 'The destruction of consciousness is the impermanence of consciousness.'

children.text: evaṃ copadekṣyanti ya evaṃ gaveṣayiṣyati sa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ cariṣyatīti
children.translated_text: And they will teach in this way: 'Whoever investigates in this way will be practicing in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

children.text: iyaṃ sā kauśika prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikā veditavyā
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s>, this should be known as that counterfeit of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na khalu punaḥ kauśika rūpavināśo rūpānityatā draṣṭavyā
children.translated_text: But, <s>Kauśika</s>, the destruction of form is certainly not to be seen as the impermanence of form.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: na khalu punaḥ kauśika vijñānavināśo vijñānānityatā draṣṭavyā
children.translated_text: But, <s>Kauśika</s>, the destruction of consciousness is certainly not to be seen as the impermanence of consciousness.

children.text: sacedevaṃ paśyati prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikāyāṃ carati
children.translated_text: If one sees in this way, one practices in the counterfeit of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tasmāttarhi kauśika kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā prajñāpāramitāyā artha upadeṣṭavyaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore then, <s>Kauśika</s>, the meaning of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> should be taught by a son of good family or daughter of good family.

children.text: prajñāpāramitāyā arthamupadiśan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ||
children.translated_text: A son of good family or daughter of good family who teaches the meaning of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> would produce still more merit." ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yāvanto jambūdvīpe sattvāḥ tān sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings there are in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> in the fruit of stream-entry.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet śakra āha bahu bhagavan bahu sugata
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account? <s>Śakra</s> said, "Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>."

children.text: bhagavānāha ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhad abhiśraddadhate avakalpayannavakalpayate adhimuñcannadhimuñcate prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya adhyāśayasampanno 'dhyāśayasampannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāya adhyāśayena dadyāt antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā saṃpādayiṣyati udyukto 'muṃ grāhayiṣyati saṃdarśayiṣyati samādāpayiṣyati samuttejayiṣyati saṃpraharṣayiṣyati vācā neṣyati vineṣyati anuneṣyati arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminn eva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "More than that, <s>Kauśika</s>, would be the merit produced by a son of good family or daughter of good family who, even after merely making this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> into a book, believing in it, accepting it, trusting it, with a clear mind, endowed with noble intention, having generated the thought of awakening, should give it sincerely to a bodhisattva whose thought of awakening has been generated; or who should at least, without weariness, make it available for writing and recitation, and, exerting himself, cause him to grasp it, show it, cause him to undertake it, rouse him, gladden him, guide him by speech, train him, encourage him, explain its meaning to him, purify his mind in this way, make him free from doubt, and say this to him: 'Come, son of good family, train in this very bodhisattva path.

children.translated_text: For while you are training here, practicing, and exerting yourself, you will very quickly fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening; and after fully awakening, you will lead an immeasurable realm of beings to the unsurpassed exhaustion of the supports, that is, to the realization of the limit of reality.'

children.text: evaṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣeta eteṣāmeva tvaṃ kulaputra dharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhava yaduta prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktānāmiti
children.translated_text: And he would speak these words: 'Son of good family, become a recipient of precisely these dharmas, namely those connected with the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

children.text: ayameva kauśika tataḥ paurvakātkulaputrataḥ kuladuhitṛto vā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet
children.translated_text: This very person, <s>Kauśika</s>, would produce much more merit than that earlier son of good family or daughter of good family.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ ato hi kauśika srotaāpattiphalaṃ prabhāvyate ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? For from this, <s>Kauśika</s>, the fruit of stream-entry is brought about. ||

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika jāmbūdvīpakān sarvasattvān srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Let stand aside, then, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from establishing all the beings of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> in the fruit of stream-entry. Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings there are in the four-continent world-system in the fruit of stream-entry. ||

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sarvasattvān srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet ||

children.translated_text: Let stand aside, then, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from establishing all beings in the three-thousand great-thousand world-system in the fruit of stream-entry. Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings who are in a three-thousand great-thousand world-system in arhatship.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvānarhattve pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā arhattve pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let alone, moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, the accumulation of merit from establishing all beings in a three-thousand great-thousand world-system in arhatship. Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings who are in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems equal in number to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in arhatship.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase kauśike api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet śakra āha bahu bhagavan bahu sugata
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account? <s>Śakra</s> said: "Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>."

children.text: saṃkhyā api bhagavaṃstasya puṇyaskandhasya na sukarā kartum
children.translated_text: Blessed One, it is not easy even to make a reckoning of that mass of merit.

children.text: gaṇanāpi upamāpi aupamyam api upanisāpi upaniṣad api bhagavaṃstasya puṇyaskandhasya na sukarā kartum ||
children.translated_text: Blessed One, it is not easy to make a calculation, comparison, analogy, measure, or approximation of that mass of merit. ||

children.text: bhagavānāha ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate avakalpayannavakalpayate adhimuñcannadhimuñcate prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya adhyāśayasaṃpanno 'dhyāśayasaṃpannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāya adhyāśayena dadyāt antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā saṃpādayiṣyati udyukto 'muṃ grāhayiṣyati samādāpayiṣyati samuttejayiṣyati saṃpraharṣayiṣyati vācā neṣyati vineṣyati anuneṣyati arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminneva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Therefore again, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family would produce still more merit than this who, having made this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> even into a book, believes in it, accepts it, trusts it, with a clear mind, to one with a clear mind, endowed with sincere intention, to one endowed with sincere intention, having generated the thought for awakening, should give it sincerely to a bodhisattva whose thought of awakening has been generated; or who, at least for writing it out or reciting it, would tirelessly provide for it, and, being energetic, would make that person grasp it, make him undertake it, incite him, gladden him, lead him by speech, train him, encourage him, explain its meaning to him, purify his mind in this way, make him free from doubt, and say this to him: 'Come, son of good family, train in this very bodhisattva path.

children.text: atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase
children.translated_text: For while you train here, practice, and exert yourself, you will very quickly fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti
children.translated_text: And after fully awakening, you will lead the immeasurable realm of beings to unsurpassed exhaustion of the basis, that is, to the manifestation of the limit of reality.'

children.text: evaṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣeta eteṣāmeva tvaṃ kulaputra dharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhava yaduta prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktānāmiti
children.translated_text: And he would speak these words: "Son of good family, become a recipient of precisely these dharmas, namely those connected with the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>."

children.text: ayameva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet
children.translated_text: This very person would produce more merit than that.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ ato hi kauśika arhattvaṃ prabhāvyate
children.translated_text: Why is that? For from this, <s>Kauśika</s>, arhatship is brought about.

children.text: evaṃ ca asyotsāhaṃ vardhayiṣyati yathā yathā hi tvaṃ kulaputra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣiṣyase tathā tathā tvamanupūrveṇa buddhadharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyasi āsannaś ca bhaviṣyasyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ
children.translated_text: And in this way he will increase his enthusiasm: "For just as, son of good family, you train in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, so you will gradually become a recipient of the <s>buddhadharmas</s> (qualities of a Buddha), and you will be near to unsurpassed perfect awakening."

children.text: atra hi tvaṃ śikṣāyāṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ srotaāpattiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi anāgāmiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi arhattvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi pratyekabuddhatvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi samyaksaṃbuddhatvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi
children.translated_text: For here, while you are training in the training, practicing and exerting yourself, you will bring about the fruit of <s>srotaāpatti</s> (stream-entry), you will bring about the fruit of <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returning), you will bring about the fruit of <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returning), you will bring about arhatship, you will bring about <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s> (pratyekabuddhahood), and you will bring about perfect Buddhahood.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus. ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yāvanto jambūdvīpe sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings there are in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> also in <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s> (pratyekabuddhahood).

children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account? <s>Śakra</s> said, "Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>."

children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Therefore again, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family would produce still more merit who, having made this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> even merely into a book, believes in it, accepts it, trusts it, with a clear mind and endowed with sincere intention, having generated the thought of awakening, should give it with sincere intention to a <s>bodhisattva</s> whose thought of awakening has been generated; or who, at least for writing it out or reciting it, will tirelessly provide for it, and, being energetic, will cause that person to grasp it, show it, cause him to undertake it, incite him, gladden him, lead him by speech, guide him, encourage him, explain its meaning to him, purify his mind in this way, make him free from doubt, and say to him in this way: 'Come, son of good family, train in this very bodhisattva path.

children.text: atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase

children.translated_text: And having fully awakened, you will guide an immeasurable realm of beings to the unsurpassed exhaustion of the supports, that is, to the manifestation of the limit of reality.'"

children.translated_text: This very person would produce still more merit than that.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ ato hi kauśika pratyekabuddhatvaṃ prabhāvyate
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because from this, <s>Kauśika</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s> (pratyekabuddhahood) is brought about.

children.text: evaṃ cāsyotsāhaṃ vardhayiṣyati yathā yathā hi tvaṃ kulaputra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣiṣyase tathā tathā tvamanupūrveṇa buddhadharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyasi āsannaś ca bhaviṣyasyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ
children.translated_text: And he will increase that person's zeal in this way: 'As you train in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, son of good family, so, step by step, you will become a recipient of the dharmas of a Buddha, and you will be near to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.translated_text: For here, while you are training in the training, practicing and exerting yourself, you will quickly bring about the fruit of <s>srotaāpatti</s> (stream-entry), you will bring about the fruit of <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returning), you will bring about the fruit of <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returning), you will bring about arhatship, you will bring about <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s> (pratyekabuddhahood), and you will bring about perfect Buddhahood.'"

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika jambūdvīpakān sarvasattvān pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let stand aside then, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from establishing all the beings of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> in <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s> (pratyekabuddhahood). Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings there are in a four-continent world-system in <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake loakadhātau sarvasattvān pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let stand aside then, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from establishing all beings in a four-continent world-system in <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s> (pratyekabuddhahood). Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings there are in a small thousand world-system in <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sarvasattvān pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let stand aside then, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from establishing all beings in a small thousand world-system in <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s> (pratyekabuddhahood). Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings there are in a middle two-thousand world-system in <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sarvasattvān pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ ye 'pi kecitkauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let stand aside then, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from establishing all beings in a middle two-thousand world-system in <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s> (pratyekabuddhahood). Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings there are in a three-thousand great-thousand world-system in <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvān pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ tān api sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet
children.translated_text: Let stand aside then, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from establishing all beings in a three-thousand great-thousand world-system in <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s> (pratyekabuddhahood). Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings there are in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems equal in number to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in <s>pratyekabuddhatva</s>.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet śakra āha bahu bhagavan bahu sugata ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account? <s>Śakra</s> said: Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>. ||

children.text: bhagavānāha ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmantaśaḥ pustakagatām api kṛtvā abhiśraddadhadabhiśraddadhate avakalpayannavakalpayate adhimuñcannadhimuñcate prasannacittaḥ prasannacittāya adhyāśayasaṃpanno 'dhyāśayasaṃpannāya bodhāya cittamutpādya samutpāditabodhicittāya bodhisattvāyādhyāśayena dadyāt antaśo likhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi akilāsitayā saṃpādayiṣyati adyukto 'muṃ grāhayiṣyati saṃdarśayiṣyati samādāpayiṣyati samuttejayiṣyati saṃpraharṣayiṣyati vācā neṣyati vineṣyati anuneṣyati arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ viśodhayiṣyati nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati evaṃ cainaṃ vakṣyati ehi tvaṃ kulaputra asminneva bodhisattvamārge śikṣasva atra hi tvaṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ kṣipramevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Therefore again, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family would produce still greater merit who, having made this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> even merely into a book, believes in it, accepts it, and trusts it; who, with a clear mind and endowed with sincere intention, having generated the thought of awakening, should give it with sincere intention to a <s>bodhisattva</s> whose thought of awakening has arisen; or who, at least for writing it out or reciting it, will provide for it without weariness; who, being intent, will cause that person to grasp it, show it, cause him to undertake it, rouse him, gladden him, lead him by speech, train him, encourage him, explain its meaning to him, purify his mind in this way, make him free from doubt, and say this to him: 'Come, son of good family, train in this very <s>bodhisattva</s> path. For while you train here, practice, and exert yourself, you will very quickly fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: abhisaṃbudhya ca aparimitaṃ sattvadhātumanuttare upadhisaṃkṣaye 'bhivineṣyasi yaduta bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatāyāmiti
children.translated_text: And after fully awakening, you will lead an immeasurable realm of beings to the unsurpassed exhaustion of the supports, that is, to the manifestation of the limit of reality.'

children.text: evaṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣeta eteṣāmeva tvaṃ kulaputra dharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhava yaduta prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktānāmiti
children.translated_text: And he should speak in this way: 'May you, son of good family, become one who obtains these very dharmas, namely those connected with the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

children.text: ayameva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet
children.translated_text: This very person would produce still greater merit than that.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ ato hi kauśika pratyekabuddhatvaṃ prabhāvyate
children.translated_text: Why is that? For from this, <s>Kauśika</s>, the state of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> is brought about.

children.text: evaṃ cāsya utsāhaṃ vardhayiṣyasi yathā yathā hi tvaṃ kulaputra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣiṣyase tathā tathā tvamanupūrveṇa buddhadharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyasi āsannaś ca bhaviṣyasyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ
children.translated_text: And in this way you will increase his enthusiasm: 'For just as, son of good family, you train in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, so by degrees you will become one who obtains the dharmas of the Buddhas, and you will be near to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: atra hi tvaṃ śikṣāyāṃ śikṣamāṇaścaran vyāyacchamānaḥ srotaāpattiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi anāgāmiphalaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi arhattvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasi samyaksaṃbuddhatvaṃ prabhāvayiṣyasīti ||
children.translated_text: For while you train in this training, practice, and exert yourself, you will bring about the fruit of <s>srotaāpatti</s> (stream-entry), you will bring about the fruit of <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returning), you will bring about the fruit of <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returning), you will bring about arhatship, and you will bring about perfect Buddhahood.' ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yāvanto jambūdvīpe sattvāḥ teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ samutpādayet yaścānyaḥ kaścitkauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā teṣāṃ sarveṣāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya tebhya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā dadyāt
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to cause all the beings in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, however many there are, to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening; and suppose another son of good family or daughter of good family, after causing all of them to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening, were to write out this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and give it to them.

children.text: yo vā kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā avinivartanīyāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya enāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā upanāmayet atraiva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣiṣyate yogamāpatsyate
children.translated_text: Or, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose a son of good family or daughter of good family were to write out this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and present it to an irreversible <s>bodhisattva</s>, a great being: that person will train in this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and will apply himself to its practice.

children.text: atraiva prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayan vṛddhiṃ virūḍhiṃ vipulatāṃ gataḥ paripūrayiṣyati buddhadharmāniti
children.translated_text: Cultivating the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> here, having reached growth, increase, and expansion, he will fulfill the dharmas of the Buddhas.

children.text: ayaṃ tasmātpaurvakātkulaputrataḥ kuladuhitṛto vā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet
children.translated_text: This person would produce still greater merit than that former son of good family or daughter of good family.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ niyatameṣo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya sattvānāṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyatīti
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because this one, having certainly fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, will bring an end to the suffering of beings.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika jāmbūdvīpakānāṃ sarvasattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ teṣām api sarveṣāṃ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayet
children.translated_text: Let stand aside again, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from causing all beings in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening. Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to cause all the beings in a four-continent world-system, however many there are, to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening as well.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sarvasattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sattvāḥ teṣām api sarveṣāṃ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayet
children.translated_text: Let stand aside again, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from causing all beings in a four-continent world-system to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening. Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to cause all the beings in a small thousandfold world-system, however many there are, to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening as well.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sarvasattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sattvāḥ teṣām api sarveṣāṃ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayet
children.translated_text: Let stand aside again, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from causing all beings in a small thousandfold world-system to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening. Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to cause all the beings in a middle two-thousandfold world-system, however many there are, to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening as well.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sarvasattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ teṣām api sarveṣāṃ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayet
children.translated_text: Let stand aside again, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from causing all beings in a middle two-thousandfold world-system to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening. Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to cause all those beings who are in a three-thousand great-thousand world-system also to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ teṣām api sarveṣāṃ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayet
children.translated_text: Let stand aside again, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from causing all beings in a three-thousand great-thousand world-system to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening. Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to cause all those beings who are in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems equal in number to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> also to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: yaścānyaḥ kaścitkauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā teṣāṃ sarveṣāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya tebhya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā dadyāt
children.translated_text: And suppose another son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, after causing all of them to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening, were to write out this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and give it to them.

children.text: yo vā kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā avinivartanīyāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya enāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā dadyāt upanāmayet atraiva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣiṣyate yogamāpatsyate
children.translated_text: Or suppose a son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, were to write out this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and give it, present it, to an irreversible bodhisattva, a great being, thinking, 'He will train in this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>; he will devote himself to it.'

children.text: evamasyeyaṃ prajñāpāramitā bhūyasyā mātrayā bhāvanāṃ vṛddhiṃ virūḍhiṃ vipulatāṃ paripūriṃ gamiṣyatīti
children.translated_text: In this way this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> will come to cultivation, increase, growth, expansion, and fulfillment in a still greater measure.

children.text: ayaṃ kauśiaka tataḥ paurvakātkulaputrataḥ kuladuhitṛto vā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet
children.translated_text: This person, <s>Kauśika</s>, would produce much more merit than that earlier son of good family or daughter of good family.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ niyatameṣo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya sattvānāṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because, having certainly fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, this one will make an end of the suffering of beings. ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ kauśika yāvanto jambūdvīpe sattvāḥ te sarve avinivartanīyā bhaveyuranuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose all the beings there are in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> were irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: tebhyaḥ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃprasthitebhya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakalikhitāṃ kṛtvā dadyādupanāmayet
children.translated_text: Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to make this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> into a written book and give it, present it, to those who had set out for unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: yaś ca tebhyaḥ kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakalikhitāṃ kṛtvā dadyādupanāmayet sārthāṃ savyañjanāmupadiśet
children.translated_text: And suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to make this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> into a written book, give it and present it to them, and teach it with its meaning and its syllables.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase kauśika api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet śakra āha bahu bhagavan bahu sugata
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account? <s>Śakra</s> said, 'Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>.'

children.text: saṃkhyāpi bhagavaṃstasya puṇyaskandhasya na sukarā kartum
children.translated_text: Blessed One, it is not easy even to make a reckoning of that mass of merit.

children.text: gaṇanāpi upamāpi aupamyam api upanisāpi upaniṣad api bhagavaṃstasya puṇyaskandhasya na sukarā kartum ||
children.translated_text: Blessed One, it is not easy to make a calculation, a comparison, an analogy, a measure, or an approximation of that mass of merit. ||

children.text: bhagavānāha ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet yasteṣāmavinivartanīyānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ kṣiprataramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmebhya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakalikhitāṃ kṛtvā dadyāt upanāmayet sārthāṃ savyañjanāmupadiśet iha ca tān prajñāpāramitāyāmavavadedanuśiṣyāt tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika jāmbūdvīpakebhyaḥ sarvasattvebhyo 'vinivartanīyebhya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmupanāmya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ te 'pi sarve 'vinivartanīyā bhaveyuranuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Therefore again, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family would produce still greater merit who, for those irreversible bodhisattvas, great beings, who wish to fully awaken more quickly to unsurpassed perfect awakening, would make this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> into a written book, give it, present it, and teach it with its meaning and its syllables, and who would here advise and instruct them in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. Let stand aside again, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from presenting this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> to all the irreversible beings of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>. As many beings as there are in a world-system of four great continents, they too would all be irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: tebhyo 'pi kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakalikhitāṃ kṛtvā dadyādupanāmayet sārthāṃ savyañjanāmupadiśet
children.translated_text: Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to make this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> into a written book and give it, present it, and teach it with its meaning and its syllables to them also.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sarvasattvebhyo 'vinivartanīyebhya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmupanāmya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sattvāḥ te 'pi sarve 'vinivartanīyā bhaveyuranuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ
children.translated_text: Let stand aside again, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from presenting this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> to all the irreversible beings in a world-system of four great continents. As many beings as there are in a small thousandfold world-system, they too would all be irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: tebhyo 'pi kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakalikhitāṃ kṛtvā dadyādupanāmayet sārthāṃ savyañjanāmupadiśet
children.translated_text: Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to make this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> into a written book and give it, present it, and teach it with its meaning and its syllables to them also.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika sāhasre cūlike lokadhātau sarvasattvebhyo 'vinivartanīyebhya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmupanāmya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sattvāḥ te 'pi sarve 'vinivartanīyā bhaveyuranuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ
children.translated_text: Let stand aside again, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from presenting this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> to all the irreversible beings in a small thousandfold world-system. As many beings as there are in a middle two-thousandfold world-system, they too would all be irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.translated_text: Suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to make this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> into a written book and give it, present it, and teach it with its meaning and its syllables to them also.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre madhyame lokadhātau sarvasattvebhyo 'vinivartanīyebhya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmupanāmya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ te 'pi sarve 'vinivartanīyā bhaveyuranuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ
children.translated_text: Let alone again, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from presenting this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> to all the irreversible beings in a middle two-thousandfold world-system. Suppose that as many beings as there are in a three-thousand great-thousand world-system were also all irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: tebhyo 'pi kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakalikhitāṃ kṛtvā dadyādupanāmayet sārthāṃ savyañjanāmupadiśet
children.translated_text: If, to them too, some son of good family or daughter of good family, having made this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> into a written book, were to give it, present it, and teach it complete in meaning and syllables,

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sarvasattvebhyo 'vinivartanīyebhya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmupanāmya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te 'pi sarve 'vinivartanīyā bhaveyuranuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ
children.translated_text: let alone again, <s>Kauśika</s>, the formation of merit from presenting this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> to all the irreversible beings in a three-thousand great-thousand world-system. Suppose that as many beings as there are in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> were also all irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.translated_text: what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account? <s>Śakra</s> said, "Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>."

children.text: saṃkhyāpi bhagavaṃstasya puṇyaskandhasya na sukarā kartum

children.translated_text: Blessed One, it is not easy to make a calculation, comparison, analogy, measure, or approximation of that mass of merit. ||

children.text: bhagavānāha ataḥ khalu punaḥ sa kauśika kulaputro va kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet yasteṣāmavinivartanīyānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ kṣiprataramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmebhya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakalikhitāṃ kṛtvā dadyādupanāmayet sārthāṃ savyañjanāmupadiśet iha ca tān prajñāpāramitāyāmavavadedanuśiṣyāt
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Therefore again, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family would produce still greater merit who, for those irreversible bodhisattvas, great beings, who wish to awaken more quickly to unsurpassed perfect awakening, having made this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> into a written book, would give it, present it, and teach it complete in meaning and syllables, and here would advise and instruct them in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: athāparaḥ kauśika bodhisattvo mahāsattva utpadyeta sa evaṃ vadet ahameteṣāṃ kṣiprataramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsya iti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose another bodhisattva, a great being, were to arise and say, 'I will awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening more quickly than these.'

children.text: yastaṃ kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā kṣiprābhijñataraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāmavavadedanuśiṣyāt ayaṃ tataḥ paurvakātkulaputrātkuladuhiturvā sakāśādbahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ||
children.translated_text: Whoever, <s>Kauśika</s>, as a son of good family or daughter of good family, would advise and instruct that bodhisattva, great being, who is quicker in realization, in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, would produce still greater merit than that former son of good family or daughter of good family. ||

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro bhagavantametadavocat yathā yathā bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattva āsannībhavatyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ tathā tathā prajñāpāramitāyāmavavaditavyo 'nuśāsitavyaḥ tathā tathā prajñāpāramitāyāmavodyamāno 'nuśiṣyamāṇastathatāyā āsannībhavati
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, in whatever way a bodhisattva, a great being, draws near to unsurpassed perfect awakening, in just that way he should be advised and instructed in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>; and in just that way, while being advised and instructed in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, he draws near to suchness.

children.text: tathatāyā āsannībhavan yeṣāṃ paribhuṅke cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārān teṣāṃ tān kārān kṛtān mahāphalān karoti mahānuśaṃsān
children.translated_text: Drawing near to suchness, he makes the robes, alms food, bedding, seats, medicines for illness, and requisites that he uses, and that have been given by those people, of great fruit and great benefit for them.

children.text: ataḥ sa bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati
children.translated_text: Therefore he produces still greater merit.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ evaṃ hyetadbhagavan bhavati yadbodhisattvo mahāsattva āsannībhavatyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? For this is so, Blessed One: a bodhisattva, a great being, draws near to unsurpassed perfect awakening." ||

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat sādhu sādhu kauśika yastvaṃ bodhisattvayānikānāṃ pudgalānāmutsāhaṃ dadāsi anugṛhṇīṣe anuparivārayasi
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "Good, good, <s>Kauśika</s>, that you give encouragement to persons who belong to the bodhisattva vehicle, support them, and attend upon them.

children.text: evaṃ ca kauśika tvayā karaṇīyam ya āryaśrāvakaḥ sarvasattvānāmanugrahaṃ kartukāmaḥ sa bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāvutsāhaṃ vardhayati anugṛhṇīte 'nuparivārayati evametatkaraṇīyam
children.translated_text: And this, <s>Kauśika</s>, is what you should do. A noble disciple who wishes to bring benefit to all beings increases the enthusiasm of bodhisattvas, great beings, for unsurpassed perfect awakening, supports them, and attends upon them. This is what should be done.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ ataḥprasūtā hi bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? For from this the unsurpassed perfect awakening of bodhisattvas, great beings, is produced.

children.text: yadi hi bodhisattvā mahāsattvā etadbodhicittaṃ notpādayeran na caite bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau śikṣeran na ṣaṭpāramitāsu śikṣeran aśikṣamāṇā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ nābhisaṃbudhyeran
children.translated_text: For if bodhisattvas, great beings, did not generate this thought of awakening, and if these bodhisattvas, great beings, did not train in unsurpassed perfect awakening and did not train in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), then, not training, they would not fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: yasmāttarhi bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bodhisattvaśikṣāyāmāsu ṣaṭpāramitāsu śikṣante tasmādetadbodhicittamutpādayante tasmādanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyanta iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, because bodhisattvas, great beings, train in the bodhisattva training, in these six <s>pāramitās</s>, therefore they generate this thought of awakening, and therefore they fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening." ||

children.text: Chapter 6

atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattva āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃ sthaviramāmantrayate sma yacca khalu punaḥ ārya subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya anumodanāpariṇāmanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu yacca sarvasattvānāṃ dānamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu śīlamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu bhāvanāmayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu idameva tato bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya anumodanāpariṇāmanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu agramākhyāyate śreṣṭhamākhyāyate jyeṣṭhamākhyāyate varamākhyāyate pravaramākhyāyate praṇītamākhyāyate uttamamākhyāyate anuttamamākhyāyate niruttamamākhyāyate asamamākhyāyate asamasamamākhyāyate ||
children.translated_text: Then indeed the bodhisattva mahāsattva <s>Maitreya</s> addressed the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s>: "And again, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, there is the bodhisattva mahāsattva's basis for meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing and dedication, and there is the basis for meritorious action, made of giving, made of morality, and made of cultivation, of all beings. Of these, precisely this basis for meritorious action of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, accompanied by rejoicing and dedication, is declared foremost, is declared best, is declared eldest, is declared excellent, is declared most excellent, is declared sublime, is declared highest, is declared unsurpassed, is declared without superior, is declared unequalled, is declared equal to the unequalled." ||

children.text: evamukte āyupyān subhūtiḥ sthaviraṃ maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat yatpunarayaṃ maitreya bodhisattvo mahāsattvo daśadiśi loke sarvataḥ sarvatra gatayā aprameyāprameyeṣu asaṃkhyeyāsaṃkhyeṣu aparimāṇāparimāṇeṣu acintyācintyeṣu anantāparyanteṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu atīte 'dhvani ekaikasyāṃ diśi ekaikasmiṃstrisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau aprameyāprameyāṇām asaṃkhyeyāsaṃkhyeyānām aparimāṇāparimāṇānām acintyācintyānām anantāparyantānām anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ chinnavartmanāṃ chinnavartmanīnāṃ chinnaprapañcabhavanetrīkāṇāṃ paryāttabāṣpāṇāṃ marditakaṇṭakānāṃ svapahṛtabhārāṇām anuprāptasvakārthānāṃ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanānāṃ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittānāṃ sarvacetovaśiparamapāramiprāptānāṃ yāvatprathamacittotpādamupādāya yāvacca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhānāṃ yāvacca anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtānāṃ yāvacca saddharmo nāntarhitaḥ etasmin antare yasteṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śīlaskandhaḥ samādhiskandhaḥ prajñāskandho vimuktiskandho vimuktijñānadarśanaskandhaśca yāni ca ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni kuśalamūlāni buddhaguṇasaṃpatpratisaṃyuktāni kuśalamūlāni balavaiśāradyapāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni kuśalamūlāni evamabhijñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni parijñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni praṇidhānapāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni sarvajñajñānasaṃpatpratisaṃyuktāni kuśalamūlāni yā ca hitaiṣitā yā ca mahāmaitrī yā ca mahākaruṇā ye ca aprameyāsaṃkhyeyā buddhaguṇāḥ yā ca anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ yacca anuttaraṃ samyaksaṃbodhisukham yā ca sarvadharmaiśvaryapāramitā yaś ca aparimeyo 'nabhibhūtaḥ sarvābhibhūtaḥ paramaṛddhyabhisaṃskāraḥ yacca anāvaraṇam asaṅgam apratihatam asamamasamasamam anupamam aparimeyaṃ tathāgatayathābhūtajñānabalam yadbuddhajñānabalam balānāṃ yadbuddhajñānadarśanam yā ca daśabalapāramitā yaś ca caturvaiśāradyaparamasukhaparipūrṇo 'dhigamaḥ yaś ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ paramārthābhinirhāreṇa dharmādhigamaḥ yacca dharmacakrapravartanam dharmolkāpragrahaṇam dharmabherīsaṃpratāḍanam dharmaśaṅkhaprapūraṇam dharmaśaṅkhapravyāharaṇam dharmakhaḍgapraharaṇam dharmavṛṣṭipravarṣaṇam dharmayajñayajanam dharmadānena sarvasattvasaṃtarpaṇam dharmadānasaṃpravāraṇam ye ca tatra dharmadeśanāsu buddhadharmeṣu pratyekabuddhadharmeṣu śrāvakadharmeṣu vā vinītāḥ śikṣitā adhimuktā niyatāḥ saṃbodhiparāyaṇāḥ teṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yāni kuśalamūlāni ye ca tairbuddhairbhagavadbhirbodhisattvā mahāsattvā vyākṛtā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau teṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yāni kuśalamūlāni ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni ye ca pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pudgalā vyākṛtāḥ pratyekabodhau teṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yāni kuśalamūlāni yacca śrāvakayānikānāṃ pudgalānāṃ dānamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu śīlamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu bhāvanāmayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu yāni ca śaikṣāṇyanāsravāṇi kuśalamūlāni yāni ca aśaikṣāṇyanāsravāṇi kuśalamūlāni yaiś ca pṛthagjanaistatra dharmakuśalamūlānyavaropitāni teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīnāṃ upāsakānāmupāsikānām yacca dānamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu śīlamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu bhāvanāmayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu yaiś ca tatra teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmaṃ deśayatāṃ devairnāgairyakṣairgandharvairasurairgaruḍaiḥ kinnarairmahoragair manuṣyāmanuṣyairvā yaiś ca tiryagyonigatair api sattvaiḥ kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni yaiś ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ parinirvāpayatām api kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni yaiś ca tatra teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ parinirvṛtānām api kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni buddhaṃ ca bhagavantamāgamya dharmaṃ cāgamya saṃghaṃ cāgamya manobhāvanīyāṃś ca pudgalānāgamya teṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yāni kuśalamūlāni tatsarvaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ niravaśeṣāniravaśeṣam anavaśeṣam aikadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya piṇḍayitvā tulayitvā agrayā anumodanayā anumodeta śreṣṭhayā jyeṣṭhayā varayā pravarayā praṇītayā uttamayā anuttamayā niruttarayā asamayā asamasamayā anumodanayā anumodeta
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> spoke thus to the elder <s>Maitreya</s>, the bodhisattva mahāsattva: "But, <s>Maitreya</s>, as for this bodhisattva mahāsattva: in the worlds of the ten directions, everywhere and in every place, in immeasurable upon immeasurable, innumerable upon innumerable, limitless upon limitless, inconceivable upon inconceivable, infinite and boundless three-thousand great-thousand world-systems, in the past time, in each direction and in each three-thousand great-thousand world-system, there have been immeasurable upon immeasurable, innumerable upon innumerable, limitless upon limitless, inconceivable upon inconceivable, infinite and boundless Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas, who have passed completely into the nirvāṇa-element without remainder, whose road has been cut off, whose pathways have been cut off, whose net of conceptual existence has been cut off, whose tears are dried, whose thorns are crushed, whose burden has been laid down, whose own purpose has been attained, whose fetters to existence are wholly exhausted, whose minds are well liberated through right knowledge, and who have reached the highest perfection in mastery over every state of mind. From their first production of the thought of awakening up to their full awakening to unsurpassed perfect awakening, up to their passing completely into the nirvāṇa-element without remainder, and up to the time before the true Dharma disappeared, whatever there was in the interval as the aggregate of morality, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, and the aggregate of knowledge and vision of liberation of those blessed Buddhas; whatever wholesome roots were connected with the six perfections, wholesome roots connected with the accomplishment of the qualities of a Buddha, wholesome roots connected with the perfection of the powers and confidences, and likewise wholesome roots connected with the perfection of superknowledges, the perfection of complete understanding, the perfection of vows, and the accomplishment of omniscient knowledge; whatever wish for welfare, great loving-kindness, and great compassion there was; whatever immeasurable and innumerable qualities of a Buddha there were; whatever unsurpassed perfect awakening, unsurpassed happiness of perfect awakening, and perfection in sovereignty over all dharmas there was; whatever immeasurable, unconquered, all-conquering supreme formation of miraculous power there was; whatever unobstructed, unattached, unhindered, unequalled, equal to the unequalled, incomparable, and immeasurable Tathāgata power of knowledge of things as they really are there was; whatever power of Buddha-knowledge, whatever knowledge and vision of a Buddha, whatever perfection of the ten powers, whatever attainment filled with the supreme happiness of the four confidences, whatever realization of dharmas through the ultimate disclosure of all dharmas, whatever turning of the Dharma-wheel, raising of the Dharma-torch, beating of the Dharma-drum, filling of the Dharma-conch, proclamation of the Dharma-conch, striking with the Dharma-sword, raining down of the Dharma-rain, performance of the Dharma-sacrifice, satisfaction of all beings with the gift of Dharma, and invitation through the gift of Dharma there was; and all those who, in those Dharma teachings, were disciplined, trained, resolved, fixed, and bound for awakening in the dharmas of Buddhas, the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas, or the dharmas of disciples, and whatever wholesome roots all of them had; and whatever wholesome roots connected with the six perfections were possessed by all those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who had been predicted by those blessed Buddhas to unsurpassed perfect awakening; and whatever wholesome roots were possessed by all those persons belonging to the vehicle of pratyekabuddhas who had been predicted to pratyekabodhi; and whatever basis for meritorious action made of giving, made of morality, and made of cultivation belonged to persons of the disciple vehicle, and whatever outflow-free wholesome roots belonged to learners and whatever outflow-free wholesome roots belonged to those beyond training; and whatever wholesome roots in the Dharma had been planted there by ordinary people; and whatever basis for meritorious action made of giving, made of morality, and made of cultivation belonged to the four assemblies of those blessed Buddhas, namely monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen; and whatever wholesome roots had been planted there, while those blessed Buddhas were teaching the Dharma, by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans or nonhumans, and even by beings gone into animal birth; and whatever wholesome roots had been planted while those blessed Buddhas were passing into nirvāṇa; and whatever wholesome roots had been planted there after those blessed Buddhas had passed into nirvāṇa, on account of the blessed Buddha, on account of the Dharma, on account of the Saṃgha, and on account of persons worthy of mental reverence: having gathered, collected, weighed, and combined all that wholesome root, wholly and without remainder, he would rejoice in it with the foremost rejoicing, the best, the eldest, the excellent, the most excellent, the refined, the highest, the unsurpassed, the supreme, the unequalled, the equal to the unequalled rejoicing."

children.text: evamanumodya anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayāmīti vācaṃ bhāṣeta anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherāhārakaṃ bhavatviti
children.translated_text: Having rejoiced in this way, he should utter the words, "I dedicate the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing to unsurpassed perfect awakening. May it become a support for unsurpassed perfect awakening."

children.text: tatra bodhisattvayānikaḥ pudgalo yairvastubhiranumodeta yairārambaṇairyairākāraistaccittamutpādayet api nu tāni vastūni tāni vā ārambaṇāni te vā ākārāstathopalabhyeran yathā nimittīkaroti evamukte maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattva āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃ sthavirametadavocat na tāni bhadanta subhūte vastūni tāni vā ārambaṇāni te vā ākārāstathopalabhyante yathā nimittīkaroti
children.translated_text: There, with whatever objects a person belonging to the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle rejoices, and with whatever objective supports and whatever aspects he gives rise to that thought, are those objects, those objective supports, or those aspects apprehended in the very way in which he makes them into signs? When this had been said, the bodhisattva mahāsattva <s>Maitreya</s> said this to the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s>: "Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, those objects, those objective supports, or those aspects are not apprehended in the way in which he makes them into signs."

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtiḥ sthaviro maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat yadi so 'saṃvidyamānaṃ vastu asaṃvidyamānam ārambaṇam ārambaṇīkuryāt nimittīkuryāt tatkathamasya saṃjñāviparyāsaścittaviparyāso dṛṣṭiviparyāso na bhavet tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi rāgo 'pyasaṃvidyamānaṃ vastu anitye nityamiti duḥkhe sukhamiti anātmanyātmeti aśubhe śubhamiti vikalpya saṃkalpya utpadyate saṃjñāviparyāsaścittaviparyāso dṛṣṭiviparyāsaḥ
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the bodhisattva mahāsattva <s>Maitreya</s>: "If he should take as an objective support and make into a sign a non-existent object, a non-existent objective support, how would there not be for him a perversion of perception, a perversion of thought, and a perversion of view? Why is that? For desire too arises with respect to a non-existent object after imagining and constructing what is impermanent as permanent, what is suffering as happiness, what is not self as self, and what is impure as pure; and that is a perversion of perception, a perversion of thought, and a perversion of view.

children.text: athāpi yathā vastu yathā ārambaṇaṃ yathā ākārastathā bodhistathā cittam evaṃ sarvadharmāḥ sarvadhātavaḥ
children.translated_text: But if awakening is just as the object is, just as the objective support is, just as the aspect is, and thought is just so, then so also are all dharmas and all elements.

children.text: yadi ca yathā vastu yathā ārambaṇaṃ yathā ākārastathā bodhistathā cittam tatkatamairvastubhiḥkatamairārambaṇaiḥ katamairākāraiḥ katamaṃ cittamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati katamadvā anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu kva anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattva āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃ sthavirametadavocat nedamārya subhūte navayānasamprasthitasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya purato bhāṣitavyaṃ nopadeṣṭavyam
children.translated_text: And if awakening is just as the object is, just as the objective support is, just as the aspect is, and thought is just so, then with what objects, with what objective supports, and with what aspects does he dedicate what thought to unsurpassed perfect awakening? Or what is the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing, and where does he dedicate it to unsurpassed perfect awakening?" Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva <s>Maitreya</s> said this to the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s>: "Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, this is not to be spoken or taught in the presence of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has newly set out in the vehicle.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ yad api hi syāttasya śraddhāmātrakaṃ premamātrakaṃ prasādamātrakaṃ gauravamātrakam tad api tasya sarvamantardhīyeta
children.translated_text: Why is that? Whatever mere faith, mere affection, mere confidence, or mere respect he might have, all of that would disappear for him.

children.text: avinivartanīyasyedam ārya subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya purato bhāṣitavyamupadeṣṭavyam
children.translated_text: Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, this should be spoken and taught in the presence of an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.

children.text: yo vā kalyāṇamitropastabdho sattvo mahāsattvo bhavet so 'tra nāvaleṣyate na saṃleṣyate na vipatsyati na viṣādamāpatsyate na vipṛṣṭhīkariṣyati mānasam na bhagnapṛṣṭhīkariṣyati nottrasiṣyati na saṃtrasiṣyati na saṃtrāsamāpatsyate
children.translated_text: Or if a being, a great being, is supported by a good friend, then he will not be depressed here, will not sink down, will not come to ruin, will not fall into despondency, will not turn his mind away, will not become broken-backed in spirit, will not be frightened, will not be terrified, and will not fall into terror.

children.text: evaṃ ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu sarvajñatāyāṃ pariṇāmayitavyam ||
children.translated_text: And in this way the bodhisattva mahāsattva should dedicate the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing to omniscience." ||

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ sthaviro maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat yena maitreya cittenānumodya yatpariṇāmayati taccittaṃ kṣīṇaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇatam
children.translated_text: Then the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the bodhisattva mahāsattva <s>Maitreya</s>: "<s>Maitreya</s>, the thought by which one rejoices and dedicates something is exhausted, ceased, gone, and changed.

children.text: tatkatamattaccittaṃ yena pariṇāmayati anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye katamadvā taccittamanumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu yatpariṇāmayatyanuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye kathaṃ vā śakyaṃ cittena cittaṃ pariṇāmayituṃ yadā dvayościttayoḥ samavadhānaṃ nāsti na ca taccittasvabhāvatā śakyā pariṇāmayitum ||
children.translated_text: Which is that thought by which he dedicates it to unsurpassed perfect awakening? Or which is that thought accompanied by rejoicing that is the basis of meritorious action, which he dedicates to unsurpassed perfect awakening? And how can thought be dedicated by thought, when there is no conjunction of two thoughts, and when the own-being of that thought cannot be dedicated?" ||

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃ sthavirametadavocat mā khalvārya subhūte navayānasamprasthitā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā imaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvā uttrasiṣuḥ saṃtrasiṣuḥ saṃtrāsamāpatsyante kathaṃ cārya subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena tadanumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye pariṇāmayitavyam kathaṃ ca anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu parigṛhṇatā anumodanāsahagataṃ cittaṃ pariṇāmayatā tadanumodanāsahagataṃ cittaṃ suparigṛhītaṃ supariṇāmitaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s>: "Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, let not bodhisattva mahāsattvas newly set out in the vehicle, having heard this instruction, be frightened, terrified, or fall into terror. And how, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, should a bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicate that basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing to unsurpassed perfect awakening? And how, when he grasps the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing and dedicates the thought accompanied by rejoicing, does that thought accompanied by rejoicing become well grasped and well dedicated?" ||

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ sthaviro maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamārabhya maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamadhiṣṭhānaṃ kṛtvā maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayate sma iha maitreya bodhisattvo mahāsattvas teṣāmatītānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ chinnavartmanāṃ chinnavartmanīnāṃ chinnaprapañcabhavanetrīkāṇāṃ paryāttabāṣpāṇāṃ marditakaṇṭakānām apahṛtabhārāṇām anuprāptasvakārthānāṃ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanānāṃ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittānāṃ sarvacetovaśiparamapāramitāprāptānāṃ daśasu dikṣu aprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu ekaikasyāṃ diśi ekaikasmiṃś ca trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau aprameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ parinirvṛtānāṃ yāvatprathamacittotpādamupādāya yāvacca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhānāṃ yāvacca anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtānāṃ yāvacca saddharmo nāntarhitaḥ etasmin antare yāni teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ kuśalamūlāni pāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni yaś ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ kuśalamūlābhisaṃskāraḥ yaś ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śīlaskandhaḥ samādhiskandhaḥ prajñāskandho vimuktiskandho vimuktijñānadarśanaskandhaḥ yā ca hitaiṣitā yā ca mahāmaitrī yā ca mahākaruṇā ye ca aprameyāsaṃkhyeyā buddhaguṇāḥ yaś ca tairbuddhairbhagavadbhirdharmo deśitaḥ ye ca tasmin dharme śikṣitā adhimuktāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ teṣāṃ ca yāni kuśalamūlāni ye ca tairbuddhairbhagavadbhirbodhisattvā mahāsattvā vyākṛtā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau teṣāṃ ca yāni kuśalamūlāni ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni ye ca pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pudgalā vyākṛtāḥ pratyekabodhau teṣāṃ ca yāni kuśalamūlāni yāni ca śrāvakayānikānāṃ pudgalānāṃ dānamayāni kuśalamūlāni śīlamayāni kuśalamūlāni bhāvanāmayāni kuśalamūlāni yāni ca śaikṣāṇyanāsravāṇi kuśalamūlāni yāni ca aśaikṣāṇyanāsravāṇi kuśalamūlāni yaiś ca tasmin dharme pṛthagjanaiḥ kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni yaiś ca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyairvā sa dharmaḥ śrutaḥ śrutvā ca kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni yaiś ca tiryagyonigatair api sattvaiḥ sa dharmaḥ śrutaḥ śrutvā ca kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni yaiś ca teṣu buddheṣu bhagavatsu parinirvāpayatsu parinirvṛteṣu ca kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni teṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yāni kuśalamūlāni tāni sarvāṇyekato 'bhisaṃkṣipya piṇḍayitvā tulayitvā niravaśeṣya niravaśeṣamanumodeta ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s>, taking up the bodhisattva, the great being <s>Maitreya</s>, and making the bodhisattva, the great being <s>Maitreya</s>, the basis of his sustaining power, addressed the bodhisattva, the great being <s>Maitreya</s>: "Here, <s>Maitreya</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, gathers into one, collects, weighs, leaves nothing out, and rejoices in all the roots of good of those past Buddhas, Blessed Ones: whose path has been cut off, whose course has been cut off, whose net of proliferated becoming has been cut off, whose tears are dried up, whose thorns are crushed, whose burden has been removed, who have attained their own goal, whose fetters of becoming are completely exhausted, whose minds are well liberated through right knowledge, and who have attained the supreme perfection of mastery over every mental state. In the ten directions, in immeasurable and incalculable three-thousand great-thousand world-systems, in each direction and in each three-thousand great-thousand world-system, there are immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who have passed into final <s>nirvāṇa</s>; from their first arising of the thought up to their full awakening to unsurpassed perfect awakening, up to their passing into final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the element of <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder, and up to the time when the true <s>dharma</s> has not disappeared. In that interval, whatever roots of good connected with the <s>pāramitās</s> belonged to those Buddhas, Blessed Ones; whatever formation of merit and formation of roots of good belonged to them; whatever aggregate of morality, aggregate of concentration, aggregate of wisdom, aggregate of liberation, and aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation belonged to them; whatever wish for welfare, great friendliness, great compassion, and immeasurable, incalculable qualities of a Buddha there were; whatever <s>dharma</s> was taught by those Buddhas, Blessed Ones; and whatever roots of good belonged to those who trained in, were devoted to, and were established in that <s>dharma</s>; whatever roots of good connected with the six <s>pāramitās</s> belonged to the bodhisattvas, great beings, whom those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, predicted for unsurpassed perfect awakening; whatever roots of good belonged to persons of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle who were predicted for <s>pratyekabodhi</s>; whatever roots of good made of giving, made of morality, and made of cultivation belonged to persons of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle; whatever undefiled roots of good belonged to trainees and to those beyond training; whatever roots of good were planted in that <s>dharma</s> by ordinary people; whatever roots of good were planted by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, or nonhumans who heard that <s>dharma</s>; whatever roots of good were planted by animals too, after they heard that <s>dharma</s>; and whatever roots of good were planted when those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, were passing into final <s>nirvāṇa</s> and after they had passed into final <s>nirvāṇa</s>: all those roots of good of all of them he gathers into one, collects, weighs, leaves nothing out, and rejoices in them without remainder."

children.text: anumodya anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayate pariṇāmayato bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kathaṃ na saṃjñāviparyāso na cittaviparyāso na dṛṣṭiviparyāso bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Having rejoiced, he dedicates the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing to unsurpassed perfect awakening. For the bodhisattva, the great being, as he dedicates it, how is there no distortion of perception, no distortion of mind, and no distortion of view?"

children.text: evamukte maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattva āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃ sthavirametadavocat sacedārya subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yena cittena yatpariṇāmayati tasmiṃścitte na cittasaṃjñī bhavati
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the bodhisattva, the great being <s>Maitreya</s>, said this to the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s>: "If, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, with regard to the mind by which a bodhisattva, a great being, dedicates whatever he dedicates, he does not conceive that mind as a mind,

children.text: evaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye pariṇāmitaṃ bhavati yathā taccittaṃ na saṃjānīte idaṃ taccittamiti
children.translated_text: then in this way the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing has been dedicated by the bodhisattva, the great being, to unsurpassed perfect awakening, insofar as he does not perceive that mind, thinking, 'This is that mind.'

children.text: evaṃ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya na saṃjñāviparyāso na cittaviparyāso na dṛṣṭiviparyāso bhavati
children.translated_text: In this way, for the bodhisattva, the great being, there is no distortion of perception, no distortion of mind, and no distortion of view.

children.text: atha yena cittena yatpariṇāmayati taccittaṃ saṃjānīte idaṃ taccittamiti cittasaṃjñī bhavati
children.translated_text: But if, with regard to the mind by which he dedicates whatever he dedicates, he perceives that mind, thinking, 'This is that mind,' and conceives it as a mind,

children.text: evaṃ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya saṃjñāviparyāsaścittaviparyāso dṛṣṭiviparyāso bhavati
children.translated_text: then in this way, for the bodhisattva, the great being, there is distortion of perception, distortion of mind, and distortion of view.

children.text: sacetpunarbodhisattvo mahāsattvo yaccittaṃ pariṇāmayati taccittamevaṃ saṃjānīte evaṃ samanvāharati
children.translated_text: If again the bodhisattva, the great being, perceives that very mind which he dedicates and attends to it in this way,

children.text: taccittaṃ samanvāhriyamāṇam eva kṣīṇaṃ kṣīṇamityevaṃ saṃjānīte niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇatamityevaṃ saṃjānīte
children.translated_text: he perceives that very mind, precisely as it is being attended to, as exhausted, thinking, 'It is exhausted'; he perceives it as ceased, gone, and altered.

children.text: yacca kṣīṇaṃ na tacchakyaṃ pariṇāmayitum
children.translated_text: And what is exhausted cannot be dedicated.

children.text: yenāpi cittena pariṇāmyate tasyāpi cittasya saiva dharmatā
children.translated_text: The mind by which it is dedicated also has that same nature of things.

children.text: yair api dharmaiḥ pariṇāmyate teṣām api dharmāṇāṃ saiva dharmatā
children.translated_text: The dharmas by means of which it is dedicated also have that same nature of things.

children.text: yeṣv api dharmeṣu pariṇāmyate teṣām api dharmāṇāṃ saiva dharmateti
children.translated_text: The dharmas to which it is dedicated also have that same nature of things."

children.text: sacedevaṃ pariṇāmayati samyakpariṇāmayati na mithyā pariṇāmayati
children.translated_text: If he dedicates it in this way, he dedicates it correctly; he does not dedicate it falsely.

children.text: evaṃ ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena pariṇāmayitavyam ||
children.translated_text: And in this way a <s>bodhisattva</s>, a great being, should dedicate it. ||

children.text: punaraparam ārya subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena yathā atītānām evamanāgatānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ chinnavartmanāṃ chinnavartmanīnāṃ chinnaprapañcabhavanetrīkāṇām aprameyāṇām asaṃkhyeyānāṃ yāvatprathamacittotpādamupādāya yāvacca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante yāvacca anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāsyanti yāvacca saddharmo nāntardhāsyati etasmin antare yāni teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni kuśalamūlāni yaś ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śīlaskandhaḥ samādhiskandhaḥ prajñāskandho vimuktiskandho vimuktijñānadarśanaskandhaḥ yā ca hitaiṣitā yā ca mahāmaitrī yā ca mahākaruṇā ye ca aprameyāsaṃkhyeyā buddhaguṇāḥ ye ca te buddhā bhagavanto dharmaṃ deśayiṣyanti ye ca tasmin dharme śikṣiṣyante 'dhimokṣayiṣyanti pratiṣṭhāsyanti teṣāṃ ca yāni kuśalamūlāni yāṃś ca te buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvān mahāsattvān vyākariṣyanti anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau teṣāṃ ca yāni ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni kuśalamūlāni yāṃś ca te buddhā bhagavantaḥ pratyekabuddhayānikān pudgalān vyākariṣyanti pratyekabodhau teṣāṃ ca yāni kuśalamūlāni yāni ca śrāvakayānikānāṃ pudgalānāṃ dānamayāni kuśalamūlāni śīlamayāni kuśalamūlāni bhāvanāmayāni kuśalamūlāni yāni ca śaikṣāṇyanāsravāṇi kuśalamūlāni yāni ca aśaikṣāṇyanāsravāṇi kuśalamūlāni ye ca tasmin dharme pṛthagjanāḥ kuśalamūlānyavaropayiṣyanti ye ca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ kuśalamūlānyavaropayiṣyanti ye ca tiryagyonigatā api sattvāstaṃ dharmaṃ śroṣyanti śrutvā ca kuśalamūlānyavaropayiṣyanti ye ca sattvāsteṣu buddheṣu bhagavatsu parinirvāyatsu parinirvṛteṣu ca kuśalamūlānyavaropayiṣyanti teṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yāni kuśalamūlāni tāni sarvāṇyekato 'bhisaṃkṣipya piṇḍayitvā tulayitvā niravaśeṣya niravaśeṣam anumoditavyāni
children.translated_text: Moreover, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, a great being, should do just as with the past Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and so too with the future Buddhas, Blessed Ones, whose path is cut off, whose course is cut off, whose net of conceptual existence is cut off, immeasurable and innumerable: from their first production of the thought of awakening up to the time when they will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening, up to the time when they will pass completely into the nirvāṇa-element without remainder, and up to the time when the true Dharma will not yet have disappeared, whatever wholesome roots connected with the perfections those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, have in the interval; and whatever aggregate of morality, aggregate of concentration, aggregate of wisdom, aggregate of liberation, and aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, have; and whatever wish for welfare, great loving-kindness, great compassion, and immeasurable and innumerable qualities of a Buddha there are; and whatever Dharma those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, will teach; and those who will train in, resolve upon, and become established in that Dharma, together with whatever wholesome roots they have; and those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, whom those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, will predict to unsurpassed perfect awakening, together with whatever wholesome roots connected with the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) they have; and those persons belonging to the vehicle of the <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> whom those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, will predict to solitary awakening, together with whatever wholesome roots they have; and whatever wholesome roots made of giving, made of morality, and made of cultivation belong to persons belonging to the vehicle of disciples; and whatever outflow-free wholesome roots belong to learners, and whatever outflow-free wholesome roots belong to those beyond training; and those ordinary people who will plant wholesome roots in that Dharma; and those gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and nonhumans who will plant wholesome roots; and even those beings gone into animal birth who will hear that Dharma and, having heard it, will plant wholesome roots;
