and those beings who will plant wholesome roots while those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, are passing into nirvāṇa and after they have passed into nirvāṇa: all the wholesome roots of all of them should be gathered into one, collected, weighed, and, wholly and without remainder, rejoiced in without remainder.

children.text: anumodya anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye pariṇāmayato bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kathaṃ na saṃjñāviparyāso na cittaviparyāso na dṛṣṭiviparyāso bhavati sacedbodhisattvo mahāsattvo yena cittena yatpariṇāmayati tasmiṃścitte na cittasaṃjñī bhavati
children.translated_text: When a <s>bodhisattva</s>, a great being, after rejoicing, dedicates the basis for meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing to unsurpassed perfect awakening, how does he avoid distortion of perception, distortion of mind, and distortion of view? If the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the great being, does not conceive as mind that mind by which he dedicates whatever he dedicates,

children.text: evaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye pariṇāmitaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: then in this way the basis for meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing has been dedicated by the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the great being, to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: sa yathā taccittaṃ na saṃjānīte idaṃ cittamiti evaṃ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya na saṃjñāviparyāso na cittaviparyāso na dṛṣṭiviparyāso bhavati
children.translated_text: Just as he does not perceive that mind as, 'This is mind,' so there is no distortion of perception, no distortion of mind, and no distortion of view for the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the great being.

children.text: atha yena cittena yatpariṇāmayati taccittaṃ saṃjānīte idaṃ taccittamiti cittasaṃjñī bhavati
children.translated_text: But if he perceives as, 'This is that mind,' the mind by which he dedicates whatever he dedicates, and conceives it as mind,

children.text: evaṃ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya saṃjñāviparyāsaścittaviparyāso dṛṣṭiviparyāso bhavati
children.translated_text: then for the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the great being, there is distortion of perception, distortion of mind, and distortion of view.

children.text: sacetpunarbodhisattvo mahāsattvo yaccittaṃ pariṇāmayati taccittamevaṃ saṃjānīte evaṃ samanvāharati taccittaṃ samanvāhriyamāṇameva kṣīṇaṃ kṣīṇamityevaṃ saṃjānīte niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇatamityevaṃ saṃjānīte
children.translated_text: But again, if the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the great being, perceives that very mind which he dedicates in this way and attends to it in this way: that very mind, while being attended to, is exhausted; he perceives it in this way, 'It is exhausted'; he perceives it in this way, 'It has ceased, vanished, and changed,'

children.text: yacca kṣīṇaṃ na tacchakyaṃ pariṇāmayitum
children.translated_text: and what is exhausted cannot be dedicated.

children.text: yenāpi cittena pariṇāmyate tasyāpi cittasya saiva dharmatā
children.translated_text: The mind by which dedication is made also has that very same <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of dharmas).

children.text: yair api dharmaiḥ pariṇāmyate teṣām api dharmāṇāṃ saiva dharmatā
children.translated_text: The dharmas by means of which dedication is made also have that very same <s>dharmatā</s>.

children.text: yeṣv api dharmeṣu pariṇāmyate teṣām api dharmāṇāṃ saiva dharmateti
children.translated_text: The dharmas to which dedication is made also have that very same <s>dharmatā</s>.

children.text: sacedevaṃ pariṇāmayati samyakpariṇāmayati na mithyā pariṇāmayati
children.translated_text: If he dedicates it in this way, he dedicates it correctly; he does not dedicate it falsely.

children.text: evaṃ ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena pariṇāmayitavyam ||
children.translated_text: And in this way a <s>bodhisattva</s>, a great being, should dedicate it. ||

children.text: punaraparamārya subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena pratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ chinnavartmanāṃ chinnavartmanīnāṃ chinnaprapañcabhavanetrīkāṇām aprameyāṇām asaṃkhyeyānāmaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu tiṣṭhatāṃ dhriyamāṇānāṃ yāpayatāṃ yāvatprathamacittotpādamupādāya yāvacca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante yāvacca nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvānti yāvacca saddharmo nāntardadhāti etasmin antare yāni teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni kuśalamūlāni yaś ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śīlaskandhaḥ samādhiskandhaḥ prajñāskandho vimuktiskandho vimuktijñānadarśanaskandhaḥ yā ca hitaiṣitā yā ca mahāmaitrī yā ca mahākaruṇā ye ca aprameyāsaṃkhyeyā buddhaguṇāḥ yaṃ ca te buddhā bhagavanto dharmaṃ deśayanti ye ca tasmin dharme śikṣante 'dhimokṣayanti pratitiṣṭhanti teṣāṃ ca yāni kuśalamūlāni yāṃś ca te buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvān mahāsattvān vyākurvanti anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau teṣāṃ ca yāni ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni kuśalamūlāni yāṃś ca te buddhā bhagavantaḥ pratyekabuddhayānikān pudgalān vyākurvanti pratyekabodhau teṣāṃ ca yāni kuśalamūlāni yāni ca śrāvakayānikānāṃ pudgalānāṃ dānamayāni kuśalamūlāni śīlamayāni kuśalamūlāni bhāvanāmayāni kuśalamūlāni yāni ca śaikṣāṇyanāsravāṇi kuśalamūlāni yāni ca aśaikṣāṇyanāsravāṇi kuśalamūlāni ye ca tasmin dharme pṛthagjanāḥ kuśalamūlānyavaropayanti ye ca devānāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā manuṣyāmanuṣyā vā taṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti śrutvā ca kuśalamūlānyavaropayanti ye ca tiryagyonigatā api sattvāstaṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti śrutvā ca kuśalamūlānyavaropayanti ye ca teṣu buddheṣu bhagavatsu parinirvāyatsu parinirvṛteṣu ca kuśalamūlānyavaropayanti teṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yāni kuśalamūlāni tāni sarvāṇyekato 'bhisaṃkṣipya piṇḍayitvā tulayitvā niravaśeṣya niravaśeṣamanumoditavyāni
children.translated_text: Moreover, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, should bring together into one, collect, weigh, leave nothing out, and rejoice in without remainder all the wholesome roots of the blessed Buddhas who are present now: those whose course is cut off, whose pathways are cut off, whose net of conceptual proliferation and becoming is cut off, who are immeasurable and incalculable, who abide, remain, and pass their time in immeasurable and incalculable three-thousand great-thousand world-systems, from their first production of the thought of awakening up to their full awakening to unsurpassed perfect awakening, up to their final passing away in the nirvāṇa-element without remainder, and up to the time before the true Dharma disappears. In that interval, whatever wholesome roots connected with the perfections belong to those blessed Buddhas; whatever aggregate of morality, aggregate of concentration, aggregate of wisdom, aggregate of liberation, and aggregate of knowledge and vision of liberation belongs to them; whatever wish for welfare, great loving-kindness, great compassion, immeasurable and incalculable Buddha-qualities they have; whatever Dharma those blessed Buddhas teach; whatever wholesome roots belong to those who train in that Dharma, become resolved upon it, and stand firm in it; whatever wholesome roots connected with the six perfections belong to the bodhisattvas, great beings, whom those blessed Buddhas predict to unsurpassed perfect awakening; whatever wholesome roots belong to the persons of the pratyekabuddha vehicle whom those blessed Buddhas predict to pratyekabodhi; whatever wholesome roots made of giving, made of morality, and made of cultivation belong to persons of the disciple vehicle; whatever outflow-free wholesome roots belong to learners and to those beyond training; whatever wholesome roots ordinary people plant in that Dharma; whatever wholesome roots are planted by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans or nonhumans who hear that Dharma and, having heard it, plant wholesome roots; whatever wholesome roots are planted even by beings gone into animal birth who hear that Dharma and, having heard it, plant wholesome roots; and whatever wholesome roots are planted while those blessed Buddhas are passing into nirvāṇa and after they have passed into nirvāṇa: all those wholesome roots of all of them should be gathered into one, collected, weighed, left without remainder, and rejoiced in completely and without remainder.

children.text: anumodya anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye pariṇāmayato bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kathaṃ na saṃjñāviparyāso na cittaviparyāso na dṛṣṭiviparyāso bhavati sacedbodhisattvo mahāsattvo yena cittena yatpariṇāmayati tasmiṃścitte na cittasaṃjñī bhavati
children.translated_text: Having rejoiced, when a bodhisattva, a great being, dedicates the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing to unsurpassed perfect awakening, how does there come to be no perversion of perception, no perversion of thought, and no perversion of view for him? If, with regard to the thought by which he dedicates whatever he dedicates, the bodhisattva, the great being, does not form a notion of thought in that thought,

children.text: evaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye pariṇāmitaṃ bhavati yathā taccittaṃ na saṃjānīte idaṃ taccittamiti
children.translated_text: then in this way the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing has been dedicated by the bodhisattva, the great being, to unsurpassed perfect awakening, since he does not perceive that thought as, 'This is that thought.'

children.text: evaṃ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya na saṃjñāviparyāso na cittaviparyāso na dṛṣṭiviparyāso bhavati
children.translated_text: In this way there is no perversion of perception, no perversion of thought, and no perversion of view for the bodhisattva, the great being.

children.text: atha yena cittena yatpariṇāmayati taccittaṃ saṃjānīte idaṃ taccittamiti cittasaṃjñī bhavati
children.translated_text: But if, with regard to the thought by which he dedicates whatever he dedicates, he perceives that thought as, 'This is that thought,' and forms a notion of thought,

children.text: evaṃ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya saṃjñāviparyāsaścittaviparyāso dṛṣṭiviparyāso bhavati
children.translated_text: then in this way there is perversion of perception, perversion of thought, and perversion of view for the bodhisattva, the great being.

children.text: sacetpunarbodhisattvo mahāsattvo yaccittaṃ pariṇāmayati taccittamevaṃ saṃjānīte evaṃ samanvāharati taccittaṃ samanvāhriyamāṇameva kṣīṇaṃ kṣīṇamityevaṃ saṃjānīte niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇatamityevaṃ saṃjānīte
children.translated_text: But if, again, the bodhisattva, the great being, perceives the thought that he dedicates and attends to it in this way: that very thought, as it is being attended to, is exhausted; he perceives it precisely as exhausted, and he perceives it as ceased, gone, and changed,

children.text: yacca kṣīṇaṃ na tacchakyaṃ pariṇāmayitum
children.translated_text: then what is exhausted cannot be dedicated.

children.text: yenāpi cittena pariṇāmyate tasyāpi cittasya saiva dharmatā
children.translated_text: The thought by which it is dedicated also has just that same nature.

children.text: yair api dharmaiḥ pariṇāmyate teṣām api dharmāṇāṃ saiva dharmatā
children.translated_text: The dharmas by means of which it is dedicated also have just that same nature.

children.text: yeṣv api dharmeṣu pariṇāmyate teṣām api dharmāṇāṃ saiva dharmateti
children.translated_text: The dharmas with respect to which it is dedicated also have just that same nature.

children.text: sacedevaṃ pariṇāmayati samyakpariṇāmayati na mithyā pariṇāmayati
children.translated_text: If he dedicates in this way, he dedicates rightly; he does not dedicate wrongly.

children.text: evaṃ ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena pariṇāmayitavyam ||
children.translated_text: And in this way the bodhisattva, the great being, should dedicate it. ||

children.text: punaraparamārya subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ chinnavartmanāṃ chinnavartmanīnāṃ chinnaprapañcabhavanetrīkāṇām aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ yāvatprathamacittotpādamupādāya yāvacca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbhotsyante abhisaṃbudhyante ca yāvacca nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtāḥ parinirvāsyanti parinirvānti ca yāvacca saddharmo nāntarhito nāntardhāsyati nāntardadhāti ca etasmin antare yāni teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni kuśalamūlāni yaś ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śīlaskandhaḥ samādhiskandhaḥ prajñāskandho vimuktiskandho vimuktijñānadarśanaskandhaḥ yā ca hitaiṣitā yā ca mahāmaitrī yā ca mahākaruṇā ye ca aprameyāsaṃkhyeyā buddhaguṇāḥ yaiś ca tairbuddhairbhagavadbhirdharmo deśito deśayiṣyate deśyate ca ye ca tasmin dharme śikṣitāḥ śikṣiṣyante śikṣante ca adhimuktā adhimokṣayiṣyanti adhimokṣayanti ca sthitāḥ sthāsyanti tiṣṭhanti ca teṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yāni kuśalamūlāni ye ca tairbuddhairbhagavadbhirbodhisattvā mahāsattvā vyākṛtā vyākariṣyante vyākriyante ca anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau teṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yāni kuśalamūlāni ye ca pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pudgalā vyākṛtā vyākariṣyante vyākriyante ca pratyekabodhau teṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yāni kuśalamūlāni yāni ca śrāvakayānikānāṃ pudgalānāṃ dānamayāni kuśalamūlāni śīlamayāni kuśalamūlāni bhāvanāmayāni kuśalamūlāni yāni ca śaikṣāṇyanāsravāṇi kuśalamūlāni yāni ca aśaikṣāṇyanāsravāṇi kuśalamūlāni yaiś ca tasmin dharme pṛthagjanaiḥ kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni avaropayiṣyante 'varopyante ca yaiś ca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragair manuṣyāmanuṣyairvā sa dharmaḥ śrutaḥ śroṣyate śrūyate ca śrutvā ca kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni avaropayiṣyante 'varopyante ca yaiś ca tiryagyonigatair api sattvaiḥ sa dharmaḥ śrutaḥ śroṣyate śrūyate ca śrutvā ca kuśalamūlāni avaropitānyavaropayiṣyante 'varopyante ca yaiś ca sattvaisteṣu buddheṣu bhagavatsu parinirvṛteṣu parinirvāsyatsu parinirvāyatsu ca kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni avaropayiṣyante 'varopyante ca teṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yāni kuśalamūlāni tāni sarvāṇyekato 'bhisaṃkṣipya piṇḍayitvā tulayitvā niravaśeṣya niravaśeṣamagrayā anumodanayā anumodeta śreṣṭhayā jyeṣṭhayā varayā pravarayā praṇītayā uttamayā anuttamayā niruttamayā asamayā asamasamayā anumodanayā anumodeta
children.translated_text: Moreover, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, with regard to the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones of the past, future, and present, whose path has been cut off, whose course has been cut off, and whose guiding net of proliferated becoming has been cut off, immeasurable and incalculable, from their first arising of the thought up to when they have fully awakened, will fully awaken, and are fully awakening to unsurpassed perfect awakening, and up to when they have passed, will pass, and are passing into final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the element of <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder, and up to when the true <s>dharma</s> had not disappeared, will not disappear, and is not disappearing: in that interval, whatever wholesome roots of those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, were, will be, and are connected with the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections); and whatever aggregate of morality, aggregate of concentration, aggregate of wisdom, aggregate of liberation, and aggregate of knowledge and vision of liberation belonged, will belong, and belongs to those Buddhas, Blessed Ones; whatever wish for welfare, whatever great friendliness, whatever great compassion, and whatever immeasurable and incalculable qualities of a Buddha there were; whatever <s>dharma</s> was taught, will be taught, and is taught by those Buddhas, Blessed Ones; and whatever wholesome roots belonged, will belong, and belong to those who were trained, will be trained, and are being trained in that <s>dharma</s>, who were resolved, will be resolved, and are resolved upon it, and who were established, will be established, and are established in it; and whatever wholesome roots belonged, will belong, and belong to all those bodhisattvas, great beings, who were predicted, will be predicted, and are predicted by those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, for unsurpassed perfect awakening; and whatever wholesome roots belonged, will belong, and belong to persons of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle who were predicted, will be predicted, and are predicted for <s>pratyekabodhi</s>; and whatever wholesome roots made of giving, wholesome roots made of morality, and wholesome roots made of cultivation belonged, will belong, and belong to persons of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle; and whatever undefiled wholesome roots belonged to learners, and whatever undefiled wholesome roots belonged to those beyond training; and whatever wholesome roots were planted, will be planted, and are planted in that <s>dharma</s> by ordinary people; and whatever wholesome roots were planted, will be planted, and are planted by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, or nonhumans who heard, will hear, and are hearing that <s>dharma</s>, and, having heard it, planted, will plant, and are planting wholesome roots; and whatever wholesome roots were planted, will be planted, and are planted even by beings gone into animal birth who heard, will hear, and are hearing that <s>dharma</s>, and, having heard it, planted, will plant, and are planting wholesome roots; and whatever wholesome roots were planted, will be planted, and are planted by beings when those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, have passed, will pass, and are passing into final <s>nirvāṇa</s>: gathering all those wholesome roots of all of them into one, collecting them, weighing them, leaving nothing out, completely and without remainder, he would rejoice in them with the foremost rejoicing, with the best, the eldest, the excellent, the most excellent, the sublime, the highest, the unsurpassed, the supreme, the unequalled, and the equal-to-the-unequalled rejoicing.

children.text: evamanumodya anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye pariṇāmayāmīti vācaṃ bhāṣeta anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherāhārakaṃ bhavatviti
children.translated_text: Having rejoiced in this way, he would utter the words, "I dedicate this basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing to unsurpassed perfect awakening. May it become a support for unsurpassed perfect awakening."

children.text: tasya kathaṃ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya na saṃjñāviparyāso na cittaviparyāso na dṛṣṭiviparyāso bhavati sacetpariṇāmayan evaṃ samanvāharati te dharmāḥ kṣīṇā niruddhā vigatā vipariṇatāḥ sa ca dharmo 'kṣayo yatra pariṇāmyate ityevaṃ pariṇāmitaṃ bhavatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: How, for that bodhisattva, great being, is there no perversion of perception, no perversion of mind, and no perversion of view? If, while dedicating, he attends in this way: "Those dharmas are exhausted, ceased, gone, and changed, and that <s>dharma</s> to which the dedication is made is inexhaustible," then in this way it has been dedicated to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: sacetpunarevamupaparīkṣate na dharmo dharmaṃ pariṇāmayati ity api pariṇāmitaṃ bhavatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: If again he examines it in this way: "No <s>dharma</s> dedicates a <s>dharma</s>," then in this way too it has been dedicated to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: evaṃ bhadantaṃ subhūte pariṇāmayato bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya na saṃjñāviparyāso na cittaviparyāso na dṛṣṭiviparyāso bhavati
children.translated_text: When a bodhisattva, great being, dedicates in this way, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, there is no perversion of perception, no perversion of mind, and no perversion of view.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi sa tāṃ pariṇāmanāṃ nābhiniviśate
children.translated_text: Why is that? For in this way he does not settle upon that dedication.

children.text: sacetpunarevaṃ saṃjānīte na cittaṃ cittaṃ jānāti na dharmo dharmaṃ jānāti ity api pariṇāmitaṃ bhavatyanuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye
children.translated_text: If again he recognizes it in this way: "Mind does not know mind; a <s>dharma</s> does not know a <s>dharma</s>," then in this way too it has been dedicated to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: ayaṃ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyānuttaraḥ pariṇāmaḥ
children.translated_text: This is the unsurpassed dedication of a bodhisattva, a great being.

children.text: sacetpunarbodhisattvastaṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraṃ saṃjānīte na pariṇāmayatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: But if a bodhisattva recognizes that formation of merit, he does not dedicate it to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi sa tāṃ pariṇāmanāmabhiniviśate
children.translated_text: Why is that? For in this way he settles upon that dedication.

children.text: sacetpunarasyaivaṃ bhavati so 'pi puṇyābhisaṃskāro viviktaḥ śāntaḥ yadapyanumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu tad api viviktaṃ śāntamiti pariṇāmayatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: But if this occurs to him: "That formation of merit too is isolated and peaceful, and the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing is also isolated and peaceful," then he dedicates it to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: sacedevam api na saṃjānīte sarvasaṃskārāḥ śāntā viviktā iti evamiyaṃ tasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitā yad api tatteṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ parinirvṛtānāṃ kuśalamūlam
children.translated_text: If, even in this way, he does not recognize, "All conditioned things are calm and secluded," this is the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> of that bodhisattva, great being. Whatever root of good there is of those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who have passed into final <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: yādṛśa eva sa pariṇāmastādṛśameva tatkuśalamūlam yenāpi tatpariṇāmitaṃ tad api tajjātikaṃ tallakṣaṇaṃ tannikāyaṃ tatsvabhāvam
children.translated_text: the dedication is just as that root of good is; and that by which it has been dedicated is also of that same kind, with that same mark, that same class, and that same nature.

children.text: sacedevaṃ saṃjānīte na pariṇāmayatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: If he understands it in just this way, he does not dedicate it to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ na hi buddhā bhagavanto nimittayogena pariṇāmanāmabhyanujānanti
children.translated_text: Why is that? For the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, do not approve dedication through attachment to signs.

children.text: yaccātītaṃ tatkṣīṇaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇatam yadapyanāgataṃ tadapyasaṃprāptam pratyutpannasya sthitirnopalabhyate yacca nopalabhyate tannaiva nimittaṃ na viṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: What is past is exhausted, ceased, gone, and changed. What is future has not yet been reached. No abiding of the present is apprehended. And what is not apprehended is neither a sign nor an object.

children.text: sacedevaṃ nimittīkaroti na samanvāharati na pariṇāmayatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: If he thus makes it into a sign, he does not attend to it rightly and does not dedicate it to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: atha smṛtivaikalyena na nimittīkaroti na samanvāharati na manasi karoti smṛtivaikalyādanavabodhādvā evam api na pariṇāmayatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: Or if, through failure of mindfulness, he does not make it into a sign, does not attend to it, and does not bring it to mind, because of failure of mindfulness or because of not understanding, then in this way too he does not dedicate it to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: atha tannimittaṃ samanvāharati na ca nimittīkaroti evaṃ pariṇāmitaṃ bhavati tatkuśalamūlaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: But if he attends to that sign and yet does not make it into a sign, then that root of good has been dedicated by the bodhisattva, the great being, to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: evamatra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena śikṣitavyam idaṃ tadbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyopāyakauśalaṃ veditavyam
children.translated_text: In this matter the bodhisattva, the great being, should train in this way. This should be understood as the skill in means of that bodhisattva, great being.

children.text: yenopāyakauśalena kuśalamūlaṃ pariṇāmayati sa āsannaḥ sarvajñatāyāḥ
children.translated_text: By that skill in means with which he dedicates a root of good, he is near to omniscience.

children.text: atra copāyakauśalaṃ śikṣitukāmena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena iyameva prajñāpāramitā abhīkṣṇaṃ śrotavyā udgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā pravartayitavyā deśayitavyā upadeṣṭavyā uddeṣṭavyā svādhyātavyā paripraśnīkartavyā
children.translated_text: And the bodhisattva, the great being, who wishes to train in skill in means here should repeatedly hear this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, set it forth, teach it, explain it, proclaim it, study it, and ask questions about it.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ na hi prajñāpāramitām anāgamya śakyeyam aśrutavatā prajñāpāramitāpariṇāmanākriyā praveṣṭum
children.translated_text: Why is that? For without coming to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, one who has not heard cannot enter this act of dedicating through the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tatra ya evaṃ vadet śakyam anāgamya prajñāpāramitāṃ tatpuṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayitumiti sa maivaṃ vocaditi syādvacanīyaḥ
children.translated_text: There, if someone were to say, "It is possible to dedicate that basis of meritorious action to unsurpassed perfect awakening without coming to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>," he should be told, "Do not say that."

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ niruddhā hi te ātmabhāvāḥ niruddhā hi te saṃskārāḥ śāntā viviktā virahitā upalabdhinaḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? For those individual existences are ceased; those conditioned things are ceased, calm, secluded, devoid, and without apprehension.

children.text: api tu khalu punaḥ sa pudgalo nimittīkṛtya vikalpya ca yathābhūtam ayathābhūte yathābhūtasaṃjñī upalambhamanupalambhe pariṇāmayet tasya kuśalamūlaṃ buddhā bhagavanta evaṃ pariṇāmitamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau nābhyanujānanti
children.translated_text: Moreover, if that person, having made a sign and conceptualized, taking what is not as it really is to be as it really is, perceiving it as it really is, should dedicate his root of good with apprehension where there is no apprehension, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, do not approve that as dedicated to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ eṣa eva hi tasya mahānupalambho bhavati yatsa parinirvāṇam api buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ nimittīkaroti vikalpayati ca
children.translated_text: Why is that? For this is precisely his great apprehension: that he makes even the final <s>nirvāṇa</s> of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, into a sign and conceptualizes it.

children.text: ākārataś ca nirvāṇamupalabhate
children.translated_text: And he apprehends <s>nirvāṇa</s> by way of its aspects.

children.text: na copalambhasaṃjñinastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ pariṇāmanāṃ mahārthakarīṃ vadanti
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas, do not say that dedication by one who perceives apprehension is greatly meaningful.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ saviṣaḥ saśalyo hyeṣaḥ pariṇāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? For this dedication is poisonous and barbed.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma praṇītaṃ bhojanaṃ saviṣaṃ bhavet kiṃcāpi tadvarṇataś ca gandhataś ca rasataś ca sparśataś ca abhilaṣaṇīyaṃ bhavati api tu khalu punaḥ saviṣatvātparivarjanīyaṃ bhavati paṇḍitānām na paribhogāya
children.translated_text: For example, suppose excellent food were mixed with poison. Although it would be desirable in color, smell, taste, and touch, nevertheless, because it is poisonous, it should be avoided by the wise and not consumed.

children.text: tadeva bālajātīyo duṣprajñajātīyaḥ puruṣaḥ paribhoktavyaṃ manyeta
children.translated_text: Yet a foolish and unintelligent man would think that very food should be eaten.

children.text: tasya tadbhojanaṃ paribhuñjānasya varṇataśca gandhataś ca rasataś ca sparśataś ca svādeṣu sukhakaraṃ pariṇāme cāsya duḥkhavipākaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: For him, as he eats that food, it would be pleasant in the pleasures of its color, smell, taste, and touch, but in its outcome it would have painful ripening.

children.text: sa tatonidānaṃ maraṇaṃ vā nigacchet maraṇamātrakaṃ vā duḥkham
children.translated_text: Because of that, he would meet with death or with suffering like death.

children.text: evameva ārya subhūte ihaike durgṛhītena durupalakṣitena duḥsvādhyātena subhāṣitasyārtham ajānānā yathābhūtamartham anavabudhyamānā evamavavadiṣyanti evamanuśāsiṣyanti ehi tvaṃ kulaputra atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śīlaskandhaṃ samādhiskandhaṃ prajñāskandhaṃ vimuktiskandhaṃ vimuktijñānadarśanaskandham
children.translated_text: In just the same way, noble <s>Subhūti</s>, here some people, through something badly grasped, badly characterized, and badly studied, not knowing the meaning of what has been well spoken and not understanding the meaning as it really is, will advise and instruct in this way: "Come, son of good family, the aggregate of morality, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of the past, future, and present Buddhas, the Blessed Ones..."

children.text: teṣāṃ ca śrāvakāṇāṃ yaistatra teṣvatītānāgatapratyutpanneṣu buddheṣu bhagavatsu kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni avaropayiṣyante 'varopyante ca yāvacca saddharmo nāntarhito nāntardhāsyati nāntardadhāti ca etasmin antare teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ yāvatprathamacittotpādamupādāya yāvacca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ yāvacca anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtānām ye ca tairbuddhairbhagavadbhirbodhisattvā mahāsattvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtā vyākariṣyante vyākriyante ca teṣāṃ ca yāni kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni avaropayiṣyante 'varopyante ca ye ca pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pudgalā vyākṛtā vyākariṣyante vyākriyante ca pratyekabodhau teṣāṃ ca yāni kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni avaropayiṣyante 'varopyante ca ye ca śrāvakayānikāḥ pudgalā vyākṛtā vyākariṣyante vyākriyante ca śrāvakabodhau teṣāṃ ca yāni kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni avaropayiṣyante 'varopyante ca yāni ca pṛthagjanānāmaprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sarvalokadhātuṣu tatsarvaṃ kuśalamūlamekato 'bhisaṃkṣipya piṇḍayitvā tulayitvā niravaśeṣya niravaśeṣamanumodya anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati
children.translated_text: And whatever roots of good have been planted, will be planted, and are being planted by those <s>śrāvakas</s> among those past, future, and present Buddhas, Blessed Ones, for as long as the true <s>dharma</s> has not disappeared, will not disappear, and is not disappearing; and, in the interval of those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, from their first production of the thought up to their awakening to unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>, and up to their complete passing into the element of <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder; and whatever roots of good have been planted, will be planted, and are being planted by the bodhisattvas, great beings, whom those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, have predicted, will predict, and are predicting to unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>; and whatever roots of good have been planted, will be planted, and are being planted by persons of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle who have been predicted, will be predicted, and are being predicted to <s>pratyekabodhi</s>; and whatever roots of good have been planted, will be planted, and are being planted by persons of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle who have been predicted, will be predicted, and are being predicted to the awakening of a disciple; and whatever roots of good belong to ordinary people in immeasurable and incalculable world-systems, in all the world-systems of past, future, and present Buddhas, Blessed Ones: having gathered all that root of good into one, collected it, weighed it, leaving nothing out, and rejoiced in it completely and without remainder, he dedicates the basis for meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing to unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>.

children.text: evaṃ sa pariṇāmo nimittayogena pariṇāmyamāno viṣatvāya sampravartate tadyathāpi nāma tatsaviṣaṃ bhojanameva
children.translated_text: Such a dedication, when it is being dedicated in connection with signs, proceeds as something poisonous, just like food that contains poison.

children.text: nāstyupalambhasaṃjñinaḥ pariṇāmanā
children.translated_text: There is no dedication for one who has the notion of apprehending something.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ saviṣatvādupalambhasya
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because apprehension is poisonous.

children.text: tasmādbodhisattvayānikena pudgalena naivaṃ śikṣitavyam
children.translated_text: Therefore a person belonging to the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle should not train in this way.

children.text: kathaṃ punaranena śikṣitavyam kathamatītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ kuśalamūlaṃ parigrahītavyam kathaṃ ca parigṛhītaṃ suparigṛhītaṃ bhavati kathaṃ ca pariṇāmayitavyam kathaṃ ca pariṇāmitaṃ supariṇāmitaṃ bhavatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau ihānena bodhisattvayānikena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā tathāgatam anabhyākhyātukāmena evaṃ tatsarvaṃ kuśalamūlamanumoditavyamevaṃ pariṇāmayitavyaṃ yathā te tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā buddhajñānena buddhacakṣuṣā jānanti paśyanti tatkuśalamūlaṃ yajjātikaṃ yannikāyaṃ yādṛśaṃ yatsvabhāvaṃ yallakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: How, then, should he train? How should he grasp the root of good of past, future, and present Buddhas, Blessed Ones? How, when grasped, does it become well grasped? How should he dedicate it? And how, when dedicated, does it become well dedicated to unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>? Here a son of good family or daughter of good family belonging to the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, wishing not to misrepresent the <s>Tathāgata</s>, should rejoice in all that root of good in this way and should dedicate it in this way: just as those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas know and see with Buddha-knowledge and with the Buddha-eye that root of good, of whatever kind it is, whatever class it is, whatever nature it has, whatever own-being it has, and whatever mark it has,

children.text: yayā dharmatayā saṃvidyate tathā anumode tatkuśalamūlam yathā ca te tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā abhyanujānanti pariṇāmyamānaṃ tatkuśalamūlamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau tathāhaṃ pariṇāmayāmīti
children.translated_text: in accordance with the nature of things by which it exists, so I rejoice in that root of good; and just as those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas approve that root of good when it is being dedicated to unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>, so I dedicate it.

children.text: evamanumodamāna evaṃ pariṇāmayan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'naparāddho bhavati
children.translated_text: A bodhisattva, a great being, who rejoices in this way and dedicates in this way is without fault.

children.text: buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ samyaktvānumoditaṃ pariṇāmitaṃ ca bhavati tatkuśalamūlamanuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye na ca tāṃstathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhānabhyākhyāti
children.translated_text: That root of good has been rightly rejoiced in and dedicated to unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s> for the Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and he does not misrepresent those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas.

children.text: evaṃ cāsya pariṇāmo nirviṣaḥ pariṇāmo mahāpariṇāmo dharmadhātupariṇāmaḥ paripūrṇaḥ suparipūrṇo bhavati adhyāśayena adhimuktyā pariṇāmayataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in this way, for him who dedicates with intention and conviction, the dedication becomes a non-poisonous dedication, a great dedication, a dedication in accordance with the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, complete and well complete. ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ bodhisattvayānikena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā evaṃ pariṇāmayitavyam yacchīlaṃ yaḥ samādhiryā prajñā yā vimuktiryadvimuktijñānadarśanaṃ tadyathā aparyāpannaṃ kāmadhātau aparyāpannaṃ rūpadhātau aparyāpannam ārūpyadhātau nāpyatītaṃ na anāgataṃ na pratyutpannam
children.translated_text: Moreover, a son of good family or daughter of good family belonging to the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle should dedicate in this way: whatever morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and knowledge and vision of liberation there is, it is not included in the desire realm, not included in the form realm, not included in the formless realm, and it is not past, not future, and not present.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tryadhvatraidhātukāparyāpannatvāt
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because it is not included in the three times or the three realms.

children.text: tathaiva pariṇāmo 'pyaparyāpannaḥ
children.translated_text: In just the same way, the dedication too is not included.

children.text: yatrāpi dharme sa pariṇāmaḥ pariṇāmyate so 'pi dharmo 'paryāpannaḥ
children.translated_text: The dharma to which that dedication is dedicated is also not included.

children.text: sacedevamadhimuñcati evaṃ pariṇāmayatastasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya avinaṣṭaḥ pariṇāmo bhavatyaparyāpanno nirviṣaḥ pariṇāmo mahāpariṇāmo dharmadhātupariṇāmaḥ paripūrṇaḥ suparipūrṇo bhavati
children.translated_text: If he has conviction in this way, then for that bodhisattva, great being, as he dedicates, the dedication is not destroyed; it is not included, and it becomes a non-poisonous dedication, a great dedication, a dedication in accordance with the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, complete and well complete.

children.text: atha taṃ pariṇāmayati niviśate nimittīkaroti mithyā pariṇāmayati
children.translated_text: But if he dedicates it, settles upon it, and makes a sign of it, he dedicates wrongly.

children.text: tatra yo 'yaṃ pariṇāmo bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya anayā dharmadhātupariṇāmanayā yathā buddhā bhagavanto jānanti yathā cābhyanujānanti tatkuśalamūlamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmitamevaṃ supariṇāmitaṃ bhavatīti tathāhaṃ pariṇāmayāmi ityayaṃ samyakpariṇāmaḥ
children.translated_text: There, this dedication of the bodhisattva, the great being, by means of this dedication in accordance with the <s>dharmadhātu</s>--namely, 'Just as the Buddhas, Blessed Ones, know it, and just as they approve it, so that root of good, dedicated to unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>, becomes well dedicated; in that way I dedicate it'--this is right dedication.

children.text: evaṃ ca pariṇāmitaṃ supariṇāmitaṃ bhavatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau ||
children.translated_text: And when it has been dedicated in this way, it is well dedicated to unsurpassed perfect awakening. ||

children.text: atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmate subhūtaye sādhukāramadāt sādhu sādhu subhūte
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One applauded the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Good, good, <s>Subhūti</s>.

children.text: śāstṛkṛtyaṃ tvaṃ subhūte karoṣi yastvaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayasi
children.translated_text: You are doing the teacher's work, <s>Subhūti</s>, since you teach the <s>dharma</s> to bodhisattvas, great beings.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ yo hyayaṃ subhūte pariṇāmaḥ dharmadhātupariṇāmo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya
children.translated_text: Why is that? For this dedication, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the bodhisattva, the great being's, dedication in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>.

children.text: asyāmeva dharmatāyāṃ yathā buddhā bhagavanto jānanti paśyanti tatkuśalamūlaṃ yajjātikaṃ yannikāyaṃ yādṛśaṃ yatsvabhāvaṃ yallakṣaṇaṃ yayā dharmatayā saṃvidyate tathā anumode
children.translated_text: In this very <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of dharmas), just as the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, know and see that root of good, of whatever birth, class, kind, own-nature, and mark, and by whatever nature of dharmas it exists, so do I rejoice in it.

children.text: yathā ca abhyanujānanti tathāhaṃ pariṇāmayāmīti
children.translated_text: And just as they approve it, so do I dedicate it."

children.text: atra yaḥ puṇyaskandho yaś ca gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu ye sattvāḥ tān sarvān kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayetpratiṣṭhāpayet tasya yaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ tato 'yameva bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya dharmadhātupariṇāmajaḥ puṇyaskandho 'gra ākhyāyate śreṣṭha ākhyāyate jyeṣṭha ākhyāyate vara ākhyāyate pravara ākhyāyate praṇīta ākhyāyate uttama ākhyāyate anuttama ākhyāyate niruttama ākhyāyate asama ākhyāyate asamasama ākhyāyate
children.translated_text: In this matter, there is the aggregate of merit, and there is the formation of merit of some son of good family or daughter of good family who would lead and establish all those beings, in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, in the ten wholesome paths of action; yet compared with that, this very aggregate of merit of the bodhisattva, the great being, born from dedication in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, is declared foremost, declared best, declared highest, declared choice, declared excellent, declared exalted, declared supreme, declared unsurpassed, declared without superior, declared unequalled, and declared equal to the unequalled.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvān daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te sarve caturṇāṃ dhyānānāṃ lābhino bhaveyuḥ teṣāṃ ca yaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ tato 'yameva bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya pariṇāmanāsahagataḥ puṇyaskandho 'gra ākhyāyate śreṣṭha ākhyāyate jyeṣṭha ākhyāyate vara ākhyāyate pravara ākhyāyate praṇīta ākhyāyate uttama ākhyāyate anuttama ākhyāyate niruttama ākhyāyate asama ākhyāyate asamasama ākhyāyate
children.translated_text: Let alone, <s>Subhūti</s>, the formation of merit from establishing all beings in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s> in the ten wholesome paths of action: as many beings as there are, <s>Subhūti</s>, in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, suppose all of them were attainors of the four <s>dhyānas</s>; compared with their formation of merit, this very aggregate of merit of the bodhisattva, the great being, accompanied by dedication, is declared foremost, declared best, declared highest, declared choice, declared excellent, declared exalted, declared supreme, declared unsurpassed, declared without superior, declared unequalled, and declared equal to the unequalled.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvānāṃ caturdhyānaniṣpādanasambhūtaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ ye subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te sarve caturṇāmapramāṇānāṃ lābhino bhaveyuḥ
children.translated_text: Again, let alone, <s>Subhūti</s>, the formation of merit arisen from the accomplishment of the four <s>dhyānas</s> by all beings in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>: suppose those beings, <s>Subhūti</s>, in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, were all attainors of the four immeasurables.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu caturapramāṇalābhināṃ sarvasattvānāṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ ye subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te sarve catasṛṇāmārūpyasamāpattīnāṃ lābhino bhaveyuḥ
children.translated_text: Again, let alone, <s>Subhūti</s>, the formation of merit of all beings in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s> who have attained the four immeasurables: suppose those beings, <s>Subhūti</s>, in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, were all attainors of the four formless attainments.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu caturārūpyasamāpattilābhināṃ sarvasattvānāṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ ye subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te sarve pañcānāmabhijñānāṃ lābhino bhaveyuḥ
children.translated_text: Again, let alone, <s>Subhūti</s>, the formation of merit of all beings in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s> who have attained the four formless attainments: suppose those beings, <s>Subhūti</s>, in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, were all attainors of the five superknowledges.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu pañcābhijñānāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ ye subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu srotaāpannā bhaveyuḥ
children.translated_text: Again, let alone, <s>Subhūti</s>, the formation of merit of all beings in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s> who possess the five superknowledges: suppose those beings in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, were stream-enterers.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvānāṃ srotaāpannānāṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ ye subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te sarve sakṛdāgāmino bhaveyuḥ
children.translated_text: Again, let alone, <s>Subhūti</s>, the formation of merit of all beings in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s> who are stream-enterers: suppose those beings, <s>Subhūti</s>, in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, were all once-returners.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvānāṃ sakṛdāgāmināṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te sarve anāgāmino bhaveyuḥ
children.translated_text: Again, let alone, <s>Subhūti</s>, the formation of merit of all beings in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s> who are once-returners: as many beings as there are, <s>Subhūti</s>, in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, suppose all of them were non-returners.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvānām anāgāmināṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ yāvantaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te sarve arhanto bhaveyuḥ
children.translated_text: Again, let alone, <s>Subhūti</s>, the formation of merit of all beings in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s> who are non-returners: as many beings as there are, <s>Subhūti</s>, in three-thousand great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Ganges</s>, suppose all of them were arhats.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvānāmarhatāṃ puṇyaskandhaḥ
children.translated_text: But let alone, <s>Subhūti</s>, the aggregate of merit of all beings as <s>arhats</s> in three-thousand-great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges river.

children.text: ye subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te sarve pratyekabuddhā bhaveyuḥ
children.translated_text: Suppose, <s>Subhūti</s>, that all the beings in three-thousand-great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges river were to become <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhatu khalu punaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvānāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ puṇyaskandhaḥ ye subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te sarve anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samprasthitā bhaveyuḥ
children.translated_text: But let alone, <s>Subhūti</s>, the aggregate of merit of all beings as <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> in three-thousand-great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges river. Suppose, <s>Subhūti</s>, that all the beings in three-thousand-great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges river were to be set out toward unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>.

children.text: ye sarve anyeṣvanyeṣu gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu ye sattvāḥ tān sarvānekaiko bodhisattvaś cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpānupatiṣṭhet sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ sarvaiḥ sukhasparśavihāraiḥ tacca dānamupalambhasaṃjñino dadyuḥ
children.translated_text: Suppose that, among all those beings in still other three-thousand-great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges river, each <s>bodhisattva</s> were to serve them all for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges river with robes, almsfood, beds and seats, medicines and requisites for the sick, with all provisions of happiness and with every pleasant mode of dwelling, and that they were to give that gift while having the notion of apprehension.

children.text: etena paryāyeṇa tān sarvasattvānekaikaṃ parikalpya tāṃś ca sarvabodhisattvānekaiko bodhisattvo gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpān upatiṣṭheccīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ sarvaiḥ sukhasparśavihāraiḥ satkuryādgurukuryānmānayet pūjayedarcayedapacāyet
children.translated_text: In this way, having imagined each one of all those beings individually, if each <s>bodhisattva</s> were to serve all those <s>bodhisattvas</s> for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges river with robes, almsfood, beds and seats, medicines and requisites for the sick, with all provisions of happiness and with every pleasant mode of dwelling, and were to honor, revere, respect, worship, venerate, and attend upon them,

children.text: evamekaikasteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ bodhisattvānāmanena paryāyeṇa dānaṃ dadyāt evaṃ sarve 'pi te dānaṃ dadyuḥ
children.translated_text: and if each one of them were to give gifts to all those <s>bodhisattvas</s> in this manner, all of them too would give gifts in this way.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu te bodhisattvāstatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasaveyuḥ subhūtirāha bahu bhagavan bahu sugata
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Would those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, on that account, produce much merit? <s>Subhūti</s> said, "Much, Blessed One, much, <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: aprameyaṃ bhagavan aprameyaṃ sugata
children.translated_text: Immeasurable, Blessed One, immeasurable, <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: saṃkhyāpi bhagavaṃstasya puṇyaskandhasya na sukarā kartum gaṇanāpi upamāpi aupamyam api upanisāpi upaniṣad api bhagavaṃstasya puṇyaskandhasya na sukarā kartum
children.translated_text: Blessed One, it would not be easy to make even a number of that aggregate of merit, nor a calculation, nor a comparison, nor a likeness, nor an approximation, nor even an ultimate measure of that aggregate of merit."

children.text: sacedbhagavan rūpī bhavet sa puṇyaskandho gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣv api trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu na māyet ||
children.translated_text: "Blessed One, if that aggregate of merit had form, it would not fit even in three-thousand-great-thousand world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges river." ||

children.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmataṃ subhūtiṃ sthavirametadavocat evametatsubhūte evam etat
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s>: "So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>; so it is.

children.text: yatra khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvayānikaḥ pudgalaḥ prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyaparigṛhīto 'nena dharmadhātupariṇāmena tatkuśalamūlamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayet puṇyaṃ prasavati
children.translated_text: But, <s>Subhūti</s>, where a person belonging to the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, embraced by <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skill in means), dedicates that root of good to unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s> by this dedication in accordance with the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (sphere of reality), he produces merit.

children.text: asya subhūte puṇyaskandhasya dharmadhātupariṇāmajasya asau pūrvaka upalambhasaṃjñināṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dānamayaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ śatatamīm api kalāṃ nopaiti sahasratamīm api śatasahasratamīm api koṭītamīm api koṭīśatatamīm api koṭīsahasratamīm api koṭīśatasahasratamīm api koṭīniyutaśatasahasratamīm api kalāṃ nopaiti saṃkhyām api kalām api gaṇanām api upamām api aupamyam api upanisām api upaniṣadam api na kṣamate
children.translated_text: Compared with this aggregate of merit, born from dedication in accordance with the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, that former formation of merit made of giving by <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have the notion of apprehension does not approach even a hundredth part, nor a thousandth, nor a hundred-thousandth, nor a ten-millionth, nor a hundred ten-millionth, nor a thousand ten-millionth, nor a hundred-thousand ten-millionth, nor a hundred-thousand ten-million niyuta-th part; it cannot bear numbering, a fraction, calculation, comparison, likeness, approximation, or ultimate measure.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi teṣāṃ paurvakāṇāmupalambhasaṃjñināṃ bodhisattvānāṃ subahv api dānaṃ dattaṃ subahvity api parisaṃkhyātaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because, although those earlier <s>bodhisattvas</s> with the notion of apprehension gave very much, it is still counted as 'very much.'" ||

children.text: atha khalu cāturmahārājakāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ viṃśatisahasrāṇi prāñjalīni namasyanti bhagavantametadavocan mahāpariṇāmo 'yaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyaparigṛhītānāṃ kuśalamūlapariṇāmaḥ sarvajñatāyai yatra hi nāma teṣām aupalambhikānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ tāvantaṃ dānamayaṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāramabhibhavati
children.translated_text: Then twenty thousand sons of gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> class, with joined palms, bowed to the Blessed One and said this: "Blessed One, this is a great dedication of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, namely the dedication of roots of good, embraced by <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and <s>upāyakauśalya</s>, toward <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), since it overcomes so great a formation of merit made of giving by those apprehending <s>bodhisattvas</s>."

children.text: atha khalu trāyastriṃśakāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ śatasahasrāṇi divyapuṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇavarṣair divyai ratnavarṣairdivyaiś ca vastravarṣairbhagavantam abhyavākirannabhiprākiran
children.translated_text: Then hundreds of thousands of sons of gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> class scattered and showered down upon the Blessed One divine showers of flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, and powders, divine showers of jewels, and divine showers of garments.

children.text: divyaiśchatrairdivyairdhvajair divyābhirghaṇṭābhirdivyābhiḥ patākābhiḥ samantācca divyadīpamālābhirbahuvidhābhiś ca divyābhiḥ pūjābhirbhagavantaṃ satkurvanti sma gurukurvanti sma mānayanti sma pūjayanti sma arcayanti sma apacāyanti sma divyāni ca vādyānyabhipravādayāmāsuḥ
children.translated_text: With divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, divine standards, with garlands of divine lamps all around, and with many kinds of divine worship, they honored, revered, respected, worshiped, venerated, and attended upon the Blessed One, and they caused divine musical instruments to resound.

children.text: evaṃ ca vācamabhāṣanta mahāpariṇāmo batāyaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya yo 'yaṃ dharmadhātupariṇāmaḥ yatra hi nāma tatteṣām aupalambhikānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ dānamayaṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraskandhamabhibhavati yathāpi nāma prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyaparigṛhītatvād asya mahāpariṇāmasya
children.translated_text: And they spoke these words: "Indeed, Lord, this is a great dedication of the bodhisattva, the great being, namely this dedication in accordance with the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena). For by it his aggregate of meritorious formation consisting in giving surpasses that of those bodhisattvas, great beings, who apprehend, since this great dedication is embraced by <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) and skill in means."

children.text: evamanyebhyo 'pi devanikāyebhyo devaputrā āgatya bhagavantaṃ parameṇa satkāreṇa parameṇa gurukāreṇa paramayā mānanayā paramayā pūjanayā paramayā arcanayā paramayā apacāyanayā satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvā arcayitvā apacāyya evameva śabdamudīrayanti sma ghoṣamanuśrāvayanti sma
children.translated_text: So too, divine sons from other classes of gods came to the Lord, honored, revered, respected, worshiped, venerated, and paid homage to him with supreme honor, supreme reverence, supreme respect, supreme worship, supreme veneration, and supreme homage, and they uttered just this sound and made this proclamation heard.

children.text: evaṃ peyālena kartavyam
children.translated_text: The abbreviation should be supplied in this way.

children.text: yāmāstuṣitā nirmāṇaratayaḥ paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikā brahmapurohitā brahmapārṣadyā mahābrahmāṇaḥ parīttābhā apramāṇābhā ābhāsvarāḥ parīttaśubhā apramāṇaśubhāḥ śubhakṛtsnā anabhrakāḥ puṇyaprasavā bṛhatphalā asaṃjñisattvā abṛhā atapāḥ sudṛśāḥ sudarśanā akaniṣṭhāś ca devāḥ te 'pyevamevāñjaliṃ kṛtvā bhagavantaṃ namasyanta etadavocan āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvadayaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyaparigṛhītānāṃ kuśalamūlapariṇāmaḥ yasteṣāmupalambhasaṃjñināṃ bodhisattvānāṃ tāvaccirarātrasaṃcitamam api tathā mahāvistarasamudānītam api puṇyaskandhamabhibhavati ||
children.translated_text: The gods who are <s>Yāmas</s>, <s>Tuṣitas</s>, <s>Nirmāṇaratis</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartins</s>, <s>Brahmakāyikas</s>, <s>Brahmapurohitas</s>, <s>Brahmapārṣadyas</s>, <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, <s>Parīttābhas</s>, <s>Apramāṇābhas</s>, <s>Ābhāsvaras</s>, <s>Parīttaśubhas</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubhas</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsnas</s>, <s>Anabhrakas</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasavas</s>, <s>Bṛhatphalas</s>, <s>Asaṃjñisattvas</s>, <s>Abṛhas</s>, <s>Atapas</s>, <s>Sudṛśas</s>, <s>Sudarśanas</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭhas</s> likewise joined their palms, bowed to the Lord, and said this: "Wonderful, Lord, to such an extent is this dedication of the roots of good of bodhisattvas, great beings, embraced by <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means, that it surpasses even the aggregate of merit accumulated by those bodhisattvas who have the notion of apprehension, amassed over so long a time and gathered in such great extent."

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstān śuddhāvāsakāyikān devaputrānādīn kṛtvā sarvāṃstān devaputrānāmantrayate sma tiṣṭhatu khalu punardevaputrā gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvānāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃprasthitānāmanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ pratilambhāya dānaṃ dadatāṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ anena paryāyeṇa ye 'pi te devaputrā anyeṣvanyeṣu gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te 'pi sarve anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānaṃ kṛtvā bodhāya cittamutpādya anyeṣvanyeṣu gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvānāṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ sarvaiḥ sukhasparśavihārairekaiko bodhisattvo gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpāṃstiṣṭhan dānaṃ dadyāt evaṃ sarve 'pi yāvatte copalambhasaṃjñino dānaṃ dadyuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Lord addressed all those divine sons, beginning with the divine sons of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> class: "Let alone, divine sons, the formation of merit of all beings in three-thousand-great-thousand world systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, beings who have set out for unsurpassed perfect awakening and who give gifts for the attainment of unsurpassed perfect awakening. By this method, those beings in each of the other three-thousand-great-thousand world systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> also, having all made a vow for unsurpassed perfect awakening and produced the thought for awakening, would each as a bodhisattva remain for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> and give gifts to all beings in each of the other three-thousand-great-thousand world systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with robes, alms food, beds and seats, medicines for sickness, requisites, all provisions of happiness, and every comfortable mode of dwelling; thus all of them, as long as they gave gifts with the notion of apprehension, would give gifts."

children.text: etena paryāyeṇa tān sarvasattvānekaikaṃ parikalpya tāṃś ca sarvabodhisattvānekaiko bodhisattvo yāvatsarve te bodhisattvā gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpāṃstiṣṭhantastān sarvasattvāṃścīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ sarvaiḥ sukhasparśavihārairupatiṣṭheyuḥ tacca dānamupalambhasaṃjñino dadyuḥ
children.translated_text: By this method, having imagined each one of all those beings and all those bodhisattvas, each single bodhisattva, until all those bodhisattvas, remaining for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, would attend upon all those beings with robes, alms food, beds and seats, medicines for sickness, requisites, all provisions of happiness, and every comfortable mode of dwelling, and they would give that gift with the notion of apprehension.

children.text: yaś ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyaparigṛhīto 'tītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śīlaskandhaṃ samādhiskandhaṃ prajñāskandhaṃ vimuktiskandhaṃ vimuktijñānadarśanaskandhaṃ teṣāṃ ca bodhisattvapratyekabuddhaśrāvakayānikānāṃ pudgalānāṃ yaiś ca tatra anyair api sattvaiḥ kuśalamūlānyavaropitānyavaropayiṣyante 'varopyante ca tatsarvamekato 'bhisaṃkṣipya piṇḍayitvā tulayitvā niravaśeṣya niravaśeṣamagrayā anumodanayā anumodate
children.translated_text: And a bodhisattva, a great being, embraced by <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means, gathers into one, collects, weighs, and leaves nothing out of the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation of the past, future, and present Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and of those persons of the bodhisattva, <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, and <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicles, and whatever roots of good have been planted, will be planted, and are being planted there by any other beings; having done so, he rejoices in all of it with a rejoicing that is foremost and complete,

children.text: śreṣṭhayā jyeṣṭhayā varayā pravarayā praṇītayā uttamayā anuttamayā niruttamayā uttarottarayā asamayā asamasamayā apratisamayā acintyayā anumodanayā anumodate
children.translated_text: he rejoices with a rejoicing that is best, eldest, excellent, most excellent, exalted, highest, unsurpassed, unexcelled, ever higher, unequaled, equal to the unequaled, incomparable, and inconceivable.

children.text: anumodya anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherāhārakaṃ bhavatviti
children.translated_text: Having rejoiced, he dedicates the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing to unsurpassed perfect awakening, thinking, "May it become nourishment for unsurpassed perfect awakening."

children.text: asyānumodanāpariṇāmanāsahagatasya puṇyakriyāvastunaḥ so 'pi paurvaka aupalambhikānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ śatatamīm api kalāṃ nopaiti sahasratamīm api śatasahasratamīm api koṭītamīm api koṭīśatatamīm api koṭīsahasratamīm api koṭīśatasahasratamīm api koṭīniyutaśatasahasratamīm api kalāṃ nopaiti saṃkhyām api kalām api gaṇanām api upamām api aupamyam api upanisām api upaniṣadam api na kṣamate
children.translated_text: Even that former accumulation of merit of the bodhisattvas who apprehend things does not approach even a hundredth part of this basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing and dedication, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor a ten-millionth part, nor a hundred ten-millionth part, nor a thousand ten-millionth part, nor a hundred-thousand ten-millionth part, nor a hundred-thousand niyuta ten-millionth part; it does not bear comparison by number, fraction, calculation, simile, likeness, approach, or approximation.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi te bodhisattvāḥ sarve 'pyupalambhasaṃjñino dānaṃ dadati ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? For all those <s>bodhisattvas</s> give gifts with the perception of apprehending something.

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat yadbhagavānevamāha atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ sarveṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ bodhisattvapratyekabuddhaśrāvakasaṃghānāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ ca atītānāgatapratyutpannaṃ yannāma kuśalamūlaṃ tatsarvamekato 'bhisaṃkṣipya piṇḍayitvā tulayitvā niravaśeṣya niravaśeṣamanumodate agrayā anumodanayā
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: "The Blessed One has said this: 'Whatever root of good there is in the past, future, and present belonging to all Buddhas, Blessed Ones, to the communities of bodhisattvas, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>śrāvakas</s>, and to all beings, having gathered all of that past, future, and present root of good into one, collected it, weighed it, and left nothing out, he rejoices in it completely and without remainder with the foremost rejoicing,'

children.text: śreṣṭhayā jyeṣṭhayā varayā pravarayā praṇītayā uttamayā anuttamayā niruttamayā uttarottarayā asamayā asamasamayā apratisamayā acintyayā anumodate iti
children.translated_text: that is, with the best, the highest, the choicest, the most excellent, the sublime, the supreme, the unsurpassed, the unequaled, the ever higher, the incomparable, the equal of the incomparable, the matchless, and the inconceivable rejoicing.

children.text: tatra kiyatā bhagavan agrānumodanā bhavati evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat yadi subhūte bodhisattvayānikaḥ pudgalo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannān gṛhṇīte na manyate nopalabhate na kalpayati na vikalpayati na paśyati na samanupaśyati evaṃ cainān dharmānupaparīkṣate kalpanāviṭhapitāḥ sarvadharmāḥ ajātā anirjātā anāgatikā agatikāḥ
children.translated_text: "In that case, Blessed One, to what extent is there foremost rejoicing?" When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "<s>Subhūti</s>, if a person belonging to the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle does not seize upon, does not think, does not apprehend, does not imagine, does not discriminate, does not see, and does not behold the past, future, and present, and examines those dharmas in this way: 'All dharmas are constructed by imagination; they are unborn, unproduced, without coming, and without going.

children.text: nātra kaściddharma utpanno nāpi kaściddharma utpatsyate nāpi kaściddharma utpadyate nāpi kaściddharmo niruddho nāpi kaściddharmo nirutsyate nāpi kaściddharmo nirudhyate
children.translated_text: No <s>dharma</s> has arisen here, no <s>dharma</s> will arise, and no <s>dharma</s> is arising; no <s>dharma</s> has ceased, no <s>dharma</s> will cease, and no <s>dharma</s> is ceasing,'

children.text: ityevametān dharmānupaparīkṣya yathaiṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā tathānumodate
children.translated_text: having examined those dharmas in just this way, he rejoices according to the true nature of those dharmas.

children.text: anumodya tathaiva pariṇāmayatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: Having rejoiced, he dedicates it in just that way to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: iyatā subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya agrā anumodanā bhavati
children.translated_text: To this extent, <s>Subhūti</s>, the rejoicing of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, a great being, is foremost.

children.text: asya subhūte kuśalamūlapariṇāmasya teṣāṃ paurvakāṇāṃ bodhisattvānām upalambhasaṃjñinām upalambhadṛṣṭikāṇāṃ taddānamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu śatatamīm api kalāṃ nopaiti sahasratamīm api śatasahasratamīm api koṭītamīm api koṭīśatatamīm api koṭīsahasratamīm api koṭīśatasahasratamīm api koṭīniyutaśatasahasratamīm api kalāṃ nopaiti saṃkhyām api kalām api gaṇanām api upamām api aupamyam api upanisām api upaniṣadam api na kṣamate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s>, the gift-produced basis of meritorious action of those former bodhisattvas who had the perception of apprehension and the view of apprehension does not approach even a hundredth part of this dedication of a root of good, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor a ten-millionth part, nor a hundred ten-millionth part, nor a thousand ten-millionth part, nor a hundred-thousand ten-millionth part, nor a hundred-thousand niyuta ten-millionth part; it does not bear comparison by number, fraction, calculation, simile, likeness, approach, or approximation.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvayānikena pudgalena atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ sarveṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dānamanumoditukāmena śīlamanumoditukāmena kṣāntimanumoditukāmena vīryamanumoditukāmena dhyānamanumoditukāmena prajñāmanumoditakāmena evamanumoditavyam yathā vimuktistathā dānam yathā vimuktistathā śīlaṃ yathā vimuktistathā kṣāntiḥ yathā vimuktistathā vīryam yathā vimuktistathā dhyānam yathā vimuktistathā prajñā yathā vimuktistathā vimuktijñānadarśanam yathā vimuktistathā anumodanā yathā vimuktistathā anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu yathā vimuktistathā pariṇāmanā yathā vimuktistathā buddhā bhagavantaḥ pratyekabuddhāśca yathā vimuktistathā teṣāṃ śrāvakā ye parinirvṛtāḥ yathā vimuktistathā te dharmā ye 'tītā niruddhāḥ yathā vimuktistathā te dharmā ye 'nāgatā anutpannāḥ yathā vimuktistathā te dharmā ye etarhi pratyutpannā vartamānāḥ yathā vimuktistathā te 'tītā buddhā bhagavantasteṣāṃ ca śrāvakāḥ yathā vimuktistathā te 'nāgatā buddhā bhagavantasteṣāṃ ca śrāvakāḥ yathā vimuktistathā te pratyutpannā buddhā bhagavantasteṣāṃ ca śrāvakāḥ ye etarhyaprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti yathā vimuktistathātītānāgatapratyutpannā buddhā bhagavantaḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, a person belonging to the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle who wishes to rejoice in the giving, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and <s>prajñā</s> of all past, future, and present Buddhas, Blessed Ones, should rejoice in this way: just as liberation is, so is giving; just as liberation is, so is morality; just as liberation is, so is patience; just as liberation is, so is vigor; just as liberation is, so is meditation; just as liberation is, so is <s>prajñā</s>; just as liberation is, so is the knowledge and vision of liberation; just as liberation is, so is rejoicing; just as liberation is, so is the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing; just as liberation is, so is dedication; just as liberation is, so are the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>; just as liberation is, so are their <s>śrāvakas</s> who have passed into final <s>nirvāṇa</s>; just as liberation is, so are the dharmas that are past and ceased; just as liberation is, so are the dharmas that are future and not yet arisen; just as liberation is, so are the dharmas that are present and now existing; just as liberation is, so are the past Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and their <s>śrāvakas</s>; just as liberation is, so are the future Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and their <s>śrāvakas</s>; just as liberation is, so are the present Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and their <s>śrāvakas</s>, who now remain, live, and pass their time in immeasurable and incalculable world-systems; just as liberation is, so are the past, future, and present Buddhas, Blessed Ones.

children.text: evameteṣāṃ dharmāṇām abaddhānām amuktānām asaktānāṃ yā dharmatā tāmanuttarayā anumodanayā anumode
children.translated_text: Thus I rejoice, with unsurpassed rejoicing, in the true nature of these dharmas, which are not bound, not liberated, and unattached.

children.text: anumodya anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayāmi apariṇāmanāyogena asaṃkrāntito 'viṃnāśata iti
children.translated_text: Having rejoiced, I dedicate the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing to unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>, by the method of non-dedication, because it does not pass over and is not destroyed.

children.text: iyatā subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya agrā anumodanā bhavati
children.translated_text: To this extent, <s>Subhūti</s>, the rejoicing of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, a great being, is supreme.

children.text: tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ subhūte te 'pi ye 'nyeṣvanyeṣu gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samprasthitāḥ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samprasthāya anyeṣvanyeṣu gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvānāṃ bodhāya cittamutpādya sarve 'pyekaiko bodhisattvaḥ ekaikasmai bodhisattvāya gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpāṃstiṣṭhan dānaṃ dadyādupalambhasaṃjñī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ sarvasukhasparśavihārair upatiṣṭhan anena paryāyeṇa sarve 'pi te sarvebhya upatiṣṭhantaḥ upalambhasaṃjñino dānaṃ dadyuḥ
children.translated_text: Let alone again, <s>Subhūti</s>, even those others who, in various great trichiliocosms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, are all beings who have set out toward unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>; having set out toward unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>, and having produced the thought for the awakening of all beings in various great trichiliocosms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, each and every <s>bodhisattva</s>, remaining for aeons as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, would give gifts to each <s>bodhisattva</s> while having the perception of apprehension, serving him with robes, alms-food, beds and seats, medicines and requisites for sickness, with every provision of happiness and every pleasant contact and dwelling. In this manner, all those, serving all of them, would give gifts while having the perception of apprehension.

children.text: ye subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te sarve 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃpratiṣṭheran
children.translated_text: All the beings, <s>Subhūti</s>, in great trichiliocosms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, would be established in unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>.

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃprasthāya gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpān kāyasucaritaṃ vāksucaritaṃ manaḥsucaritamupalambhasaṃjñinaḥ śīlaṃ samādāya varteran
children.translated_text: Having set out toward unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>, for aeons as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, while having the perception of apprehension, they would live having undertaken morality: good bodily conduct, good verbal conduct, and good mental conduct.

children.text: anena paryāyeṇa sarve 'pi te bodhisattvā ekaiko bodhisattvo gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpāṃstiṣṭhan gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpān kāyasucaritaṃ vāksucaritaṃ manaḥsucaritamupalambhasaṃjñī śīlaṃ samādāya varteta
children.translated_text: In this manner all those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, each and every <s>bodhisattva</s>, remaining for aeons as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, would live for aeons as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> having undertaken morality: good bodily conduct, good verbal conduct, and good mental conduct, while having the perception of apprehension.

children.text: etena paryāyeṇa sarve 'pi te bodhisattvā upalambhasaṃjñinaḥ śīlaṃ samādāya varteran
children.translated_text: In this way all those <s>bodhisattvas</s> would live having undertaken morality while having the perception of apprehension.

children.text: yaś ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalyaparigṛhīto 'tītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktivimuktijñānadarśanaskandhāṃsteṣāṃ ca pratyekabuddhānāṃ śīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktijñānadarśanaskandhāṃsteṣāṃ ca śrāvakāṇāṃ śīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktivimuktijñānadarśanaskandhān sarvasattvānāṃ ca atītānāgatapratyutpannaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ sarvamekato 'bhisaṃkṣipya piṇḍayitvā tulayitvā niravaśeṣya niravaśeṣamanumodate 'grayā anumodanayā
children.translated_text: But the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the great being, who is sustained by <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means, having gathered into one, collected, weighed, and left out nothing of the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and knowledge and vision of liberation of the past, future, and present Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; and the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and knowledge and vision of liberation of those <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>; and the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and knowledge and vision of liberation of those <s>śrāvakas</s>; and the root of good of all beings in the past, future, and present, rejoices in all of it completely and without remainder with the foremost rejoicing.

children.text: śreṣṭhayā jyeṣṭhayā varayā pravarayā praṇītayā uttamayā anuttamayā niruttamayā uttarottarayā asamayā asamasamayā apratisamayā acintyayā anumodanayā anumodate
children.translated_text: He rejoices with a rejoicing that is best, highest, choice, most excellent, exalted, supreme, unsurpassed, unexcelled, ever higher, unequalled, equal to the unequalled, without rival, and inconceivable.

children.text: anumodya anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati
children.translated_text: Having rejoiced, he dedicates the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing to unsurpassed perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>.

children.text: asya subhūte anumodanāsahagatasya puṇyakriyāvastuno 'sau paurvaka aupalambhikānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ śīlamayaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ śatatamīm api kalāṃ nopaiti sahasratamīm api śatasahasratamīm api koṭītamīm api koṭīśatatamīm api koṭīsahasratamīm api koṭīśatasahasratamīm api koṭīniyutaśatasahasratamīm api kalāṃ nopaiti saṃkhyām api kalām api gaṇanām api upamām api aupamyam api upanisām api upaniṣadam api na kṣamate
children.translated_text: Of this basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing, <s>Subhūti</s>, that former meritorious formation made of morality belonging to <s>bodhisattvas</s> with apprehension does not approach even a hundredth part, nor a thousandth, nor a hundred-thousandth, nor a ten-millionth, nor a hundred ten-millionth, nor a thousand ten-millionth, nor a hundred-thousand ten-millionth, nor a hundred-thousand niyuta ten-millionth part. It cannot bear numbering, fractioning, calculation, comparison, likeness, approximation, or analogy.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tathā hi te bodhisattvā upalambhasaṃjñinaḥ śīlaṃ samādāya vartanta iti
children.translated_text: Why is that? For those <s>bodhisattvas</s> live having undertaken morality while having the perception of apprehension.

children.text: tiṣṭhantu khalu punaḥ subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvasattvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃprasthitāḥ anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃprasthāya gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpān kāyasucaritaṃ vāksucaritaṃ manaḥsucaritaṃ śīlaṃ samādāya vartamānā upalambhasaṃjñinaḥ ye subhūte gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasreṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ te sarve anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃpratiṣṭheran
