children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a dog, after abandoning morsels from its master's presence, might think that a mouthful should be sought from a servant's presence, so too, <s>Subhūti</s>, in the future there will be some persons of the bodhisattva vehicle who, after abandoning this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the root of omniscient knowledge, will think that substance and excellence should be sought in the vehicle of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, which is like branches, leaves, and straw.

children.text: idam api subhūte teṣāṃ mārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as an act of <s>Māra</s> on their part.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ na hi te 'lpabuddhayo jñāsyanti prajñāpāramitā āhārikā sarvajñajñānasyeti
children.translated_text: Why is that? For those of little intelligence will not understand that <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is what nourishes omniscient knowledge.

children.text: te prajñāpāramitāṃ vivarjya utsṛjya chorayitvā tato 'nye sūtrāntā ye śrāvakabhūmimabhivadanti pratyekabuddhabhūmimabhivadanti tānadhikataraṃ paryavāptavyān maṃsyante
children.translated_text: Having avoided, abandoned, and cast aside <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, they will think that those other sūtras which teach the stage of the <s>śrāvaka</s> and the stage of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> should be mastered still more.

children.text: śākhāpatrapalālopamāḥ pratipannāste tathārūpā bodhisattvā veditavyāḥ
children.translated_text: Such <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be understood as having entered upon what is comparable to branches, leaves, and straw.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ na hi subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvenaivaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yathā śrāvakayānikāḥ pratyekabuddhayānikā vā pudgalāḥ śikṣante
children.translated_text: Why is that? For, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should not train in the way that persons of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle or the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle train.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte śrāvakayānikāḥ pratyekabuddhayānikā vā pudgalāḥ śikṣante teṣāṃ subhūte evaṃ bhavati ekamātmānaṃ damayiṣyāmaḥ ekamātmānaṃ śamayiṣyāmaḥ ekamātmānaṃ parinirvāpayiṣyāmaḥ ityātmadamaśamathaparinirvāṇāya sarvakuśalamūlābhisaṃskāraprayogānārabhante
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, do persons of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle or the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle train? <s>Subhūti</s>, this occurs to them: "We will tame ourselves alone; we will calm ourselves alone; we will bring ourselves alone to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>." Thus they undertake the efforts of forming all wholesome roots for the taming, calming, and <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the self.

children.text: na khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvenaivaṃ śikṣitavyam
children.translated_text: But, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should not train in this way.

children.text: api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvenaivaṃ śikṣitavyam ātmānaṃ ca tathatāyāṃ sthāpayiṣyāmi sarvalokānugrahāya sarvasattvān api tathatāyāṃ sthāpayiṣyāmi aprameyaṃ sattvadhātuṃ parinirvāpayiṣyāmīti
children.translated_text: Rather, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should train in this way: "I will establish myself in suchness for the benefit of the whole world; I will establish all beings too in suchness; I will bring the immeasurable realm of beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>."

children.text: sarvakuśalamūlābhisaṃskāraprayogā bodhisattvena mahāsattvenaivamārabdhavyāḥ na ca tairmantavyam
children.translated_text: The efforts of forming all wholesome roots should be undertaken by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> in this way; and by means of them he should not think further.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma subhūte kaścideva puruṣo hastinam apaśyan hastino varṇasaṃsthāne paryeṣeta
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, some man, while not seeing an elephant, might search for the elephant's color and shape.

children.text: so 'ndhakāre hastinaṃ labdhvā yena prakāśaṃ tenopanidhyāyeta
children.translated_text: He would be like someone who, having found an elephant in the darkness, would examine it by whatever light there was.

children.text: tenopanidhyāyan hastipadaṃ paryeṣitavyaṃ manyeta
children.translated_text: While examining it by that light, he would think that the elephant's footprint should be sought.

children.text: hastipadācca hastino varṇasaṃsthāne grahītavye manyeta
children.translated_text: And from the elephant's footprint he would think that the elephant's color and shape should be grasped.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu sa paṇḍitajātīyaḥ puruṣo bhavet subhūtirāha no hīdaṃ bhagavan
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Would that man be of the class of the wise? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavānāha evameva subhūte tathārūpāste bodhisattvayānikāḥ pudgalā veditavyāḥ ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām ajānānā aparipṛcchantastāṃ chorayitvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmā ye te sūtrāntāḥ śrāvakabhūmimabhivadanti pratyekabuddhabhūmimabhivadanti tān paryeṣitavyān maṃsyante
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: In just the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, such persons belonging to the <s>bodhisattvayāna</s> should be understood: not knowing this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, and not asking questions about it, they abandon it; although wishing to awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening, they will think that those discourses which speak of the śrāvaka stage and speak of the pratyekabuddha stage should be sought.

children.text: idam api subhūte teṣāṃ mārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as <s>Māra</s>'s work for them.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma subhūte ratnārthikaḥ puruṣo mahāsamudraṃ dṛṣṭvā nāvagāheta ratnāni na nidhyāyet nādhyālambeta
children.translated_text: It is like this, <s>Subhūti</s>: a man seeking jewels, having seen the great ocean, would not enter it, would not look for jewels, and would not lay hold of them.

children.text: sa ratnahetorgoṣpadaṃ paryeṣitavyaṃ manyeta
children.translated_text: For the sake of jewels he would think that a cow's hoof-print should be searched.

children.text: sa goṣpadodakena mahāsamudraṃ samīkartavyaṃ manyeta
children.translated_text: He would think that the great ocean should be equated with the water in a cow's hoof-print.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu sa paṇḍitajātīyaḥ puruṣo veditavyaḥ subhūtirāha no hīdaṃ bhagavan
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Should that man be understood as of the class of the wise? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavānāha evameva subhūte tathārūpāste bodhisattvayānikāḥ pudgalā veditavyāḥ ya imāṃ gambhīrāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ labdhvāpyanavagāhamānā avijānantastakṣyanti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: In just the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, such persons belonging to the <s>bodhisattvayāna</s> should be understood: even after obtaining this deep <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, they do not enter into it, do not understand it, and will abandon it.

children.text: ye ca sūtrāntāḥ śrāvakabhūmimabhivadanti pratyekabuddhabhūmimabhivadanti alpotsukavihāritayā tān paryeṣitavyān maṃsyante
children.translated_text: And because they dwell with little concern, they will think that those discourses which speak of the śrāvaka stage and speak of the pratyekabuddha stage should be sought.

children.text: yatra bodhisattvayānaṃ na saṃvarṇyate kevalamātmadamaśamathaparinirvāṇameva ity api pratisaṃlayanamiti
children.translated_text: There the <s>bodhisattvayāna</s> is not praised; it is only self-taming, self-calming, and one's own <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and this too is called retreat.

children.text: srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāpnuyāmiti sakṛdāgāmiphalamityanāgāmiphalamityarhattvaṃ prāpnuyāmiti pratyekabodhiṃ prāpnuyāmiti dṛṣṭa eva dharme anupādāya āsravebhyaścittaṃ vimocya parinirvāpayāmīti
children.translated_text: They think, 'May I obtain the fruit of stream-entry; may I obtain the fruit of once-returning; may I obtain the fruit of non-returning; may I obtain arhatship; may I obtain pratyekabodhi; in this very life, freeing the mind from the outflows without clinging, may I attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.'

children.text: idamucyate śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmipratisaṃyuktamiti
children.translated_text: This is called what is connected with the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

children.text: nātra bodhisattvairmahāsattvairevaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam
children.translated_text: Here <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> should not produce such a thought.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ mahāyānasamprasthitā hi subhūte bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Why is that? For, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who have set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> are clad in the great armor.

children.text: na taiḥ kadācidalpotsukatāyāṃ cittamutpādayitavyam
children.translated_text: They should never produce a thought directed toward little concern.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ lokapariṇāyakā hi bhavanti te satpuruṣā lokārthakarāḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? For those good men are guides of the world and makers of benefit for the world.

children.text: tasmāttairnityakālaṃ satatasamitaṃ ṣaṭpāramitāsu śikṣitavyam
children.translated_text: Therefore they must always, constantly, and continuously train in the six <s>pāramitās</s>.

children.text: ye ca khalu punaḥ subhūte aparipakvakuśalamūlāḥ parīttakubuddhikā mṛdukādhyāśayā bodhisattvayānikāḥ pudgalāḥ te ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktān sūtrāntān ajānānā anavabudhyamānā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ chorayitvā ye te sūtrāntāḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmimabhivandanti tān paryeṣitavyān maṃsyante
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, those persons belonging to the <s>bodhisattvayāna</s> whose wholesome roots are immature, whose understanding is slight and poor, and whose disposition is weak, not knowing and not comprehending the discourses connected with the six <s>pāramitās</s>, will abandon this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and think that those discourses which praise the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha stages should be sought.

children.text: idam api subhūte mārakarma veditavyaṃ teṣāṃ tathārūpāṇāṃ bodhisattvayānikānāṃ pudgalānām tadyathāpi nāma subhūte palagaṇḍo vā palagaṇḍāntevāsī vā vaijayantasya prāsādasya pramāṇena prāsādaṃ kartukāmo nirmātukāmaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as <s>Māra</s>'s work for such persons belonging to the <s>bodhisattvayāna</s>. It is like this, <s>Subhūti</s>: an artisan or an artisan's apprentice might wish to make and build a palace according to the measure of the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace.

children.text: sa sūryācandramasorvimānapramāṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ paryeṣeta
children.translated_text: He would seek, as a measure, a disk equal to the mansions of the sun and moon.

children.text: paryeṣamāṇaḥ sa sūryācandramasorvimānaṃ paśyet
children.translated_text: While seeking it, he would see the mansions of the sun and moon.

children.text: sa tataḥ pramāṇaṃ grahītavyaṃ manyate
children.translated_text: From that he thinks that a measure should be taken.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte vaijayantaprāsādapramāṇaṃ prāsādaṃ kartukāmena nirmātukāmena sūryācandramasorvimānātpramāṇaṃ grahītavyaṃ bhavati subhūtirāha no hīdaṃ bhagavan
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Should someone who wishes to make and build a palace according to the measure of the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace take the measure from the mansions of the sun and moon? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavānāha evameva subhūte bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani eke bodhisattvayānikāḥ pudgalāḥ ye prajñāpāramitāṃ śrutvā prajñāpāramitāṃ labdhvā prajñāpāramitāṃ riñcitvā prajñāpāramitāmutsṛjya śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmipratisaṃyuktaiḥ sūtrāntaiḥ sarvajñatāṃ paryeṣitavyāṃ maṃsyante ye te sūtrāntā evamabhivadanti ekamātmānaṃ damayiṣyāmaḥ ekamātmānaṃ śamayiṣyāmaḥ ekamātmānaṃ parinirvāpayiṣyāma iti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: In just the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, in the future time there will be some persons belonging to the <s>bodhisattvayāna</s> who, after hearing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and obtaining <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, will leave <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> behind and cast <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> away. They will think that omniscience should be sought through discourses connected with the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, those discourses which speak in this way: 'We will tame only ourselves; we will calm only ourselves; we will bring only ourselves to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.'

children.text: kevalamātmadamaśamathaparinirvāṇamevopanayanti tathārūpān sūtrāntān paryeṣyante tathā ca śikṣitavyaṃ maṃsyante
children.translated_text: They lead only to self-taming, self-calming, and one's own <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; they will seek such discourses and will think that one should train in that way.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu te paṇḍitajātīyāḥ bodhisattvā veditavyāḥ subhūtirāha no hīdaṃ bhagavan
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Should those bodhisattvas be understood as of the class of the wise? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavānāha idam api subhūte teṣāṃ mārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as <s>Māra</s>'s work for them.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma subhūte kaścideva puruṣo rājānaṃ ca cakravartinaṃ bhraṣṭukāmo bhavet sa rājānaṃ cakravartinaṃ paśyet
children.translated_text: It is like this, <s>Subhūti</s>: some man might wish to see a king, a wheel-turning monarch; he would see that king, the wheel-turning monarch.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca īdṛśo rājā cakravartī varṇena saṃsthānena tejasā ṛddhyā ceti nimittaṃ gṛhītvā koṭṭarājaṃ paśyet
children.translated_text: And, having seen that a wheel-turning king is such in color, form, splendor, miraculous power, and marks, one might take that mark and look at a <s>koṭṭarāja</s> (petty king).

children.text: sa tasya koṭṭarājasya varṇaṃ saṃsthānaṃ teja ṛddhiṃ ca nimittaṃ ca gṛhītvā apratibalo viśeṣagrahaṇaṃ prati evaṃ vadet īdṛśa eva sa rājā cakravartī varṇena saṃsthānena tejasā ṛddhyā ca nimittena ceti
children.translated_text: Taking the color, form, splendor, miraculous power, and marks of that <s>koṭṭarāja</s>, and being unable to grasp the distinction, he would say, "That wheel-turning king is just like this one in color, form, splendor, miraculous power, and marks."

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu sa paṇḍitajātīyaḥ puruṣo veditavyo yaścakravartinaṃ koṭṭarājena samīkartavyaṃ manyeta subhūtirāha no hīdaṃ bhagavan
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Should that man be known as wise by nature who would think that a wheel-turning king is to be compared with a <s>koṭṭarāja</s>? <s>Subhūti</s> said, "No indeed, Blessed One."

children.text: bhagavānāha evameva subhūte bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani eke bodhisattvayānikāḥ pudgalāḥ ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ śrutvā prajñāpāramitāṃ labdhvā prajñāpāramitāṃ riñcitvā prajñāpāramitāmutsṛjya śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmipratisaṃyuktaiḥ sūtrāntaiḥ sarvajñatāṃ paryeṣitavyāṃ maṃsyante
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, in a future time there will be some persons in the bodhisattva vehicle who, after hearing this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, after obtaining <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, will abandon <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, give up <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, and will think that omniscience is to be sought through sūtras connected with the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

children.text: idam api subhūte teṣāṃ mārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as <s>mārakarma</s> (Māra's work) on their part.

children.text: na khalu punarahaṃ subhūte ebhirevaṃrūpaiḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmipratisaṃyuktaiḥ sūtrāntairbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya sarvajñatāṃ paryeṣitavyāṃ vadāmi
children.translated_text: For I do not say, <s>Subhūti</s>, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should seek omniscience by means of just such sūtras connected with the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

children.text: api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte yattathāgatena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām upāyakauśalyamākhyātam tatrāśikṣitvā bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na niryāsyatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: Rather, <s>Subhūti</s>, without training in the <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skill in means) for bodhisattva mahāsattvas that was taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, a bodhisattva mahāsattva will not go forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ dhandhako hyanyeṣu sūtrānteṣu bodhisattvasamudāgamaḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? For the arising of a bodhisattva is sluggish in other sūtras.

children.text: tasmāttarhi subhūte tathāgata enāmanuśaṃsāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ paśyan anekaparyāyeṇa bodhisattvān mahāsattvānasyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati saṃniveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati evaṃ bodhisattvā mahāsattvā avinivartanīyā bhaveyuranuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheriti
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, seeing this advantage in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> in many ways shows bodhisattva mahāsattvas this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, causes them to take it up, rouses them, gladdens them, settles them in it, and establishes them in it, so that bodhisattva mahāsattvas may become irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu paṇḍitajātīyāste bodhisattvāḥ pratibhānti ye avinivartanīyayānaṃ mahāyānamavāpya samāsādya punareva tadvivarjya vivartya hīnayānaṃ paryeṣitavyaṃ maṃsyante subhūtirāha no hīdaṃ bhagavan
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Do those bodhisattvas appear wise who, after obtaining and reaching the irreversible vehicle, the Mahāyāna, would then again set that aside, turn away from it, and think that the inferior vehicle is to be sought? <s>Subhūti</s> said, "No indeed, Blessed One."

children.text: bhagavānāha tadyathāpi nāma subhūte bubhukṣitaḥ puruṣaḥ śatarasaṃ bhojanaṃ labdhvā hitavipākaṃ sukhavipākaṃ yāvadāyuḥparyantaṃ kṣutpipāsānivartakam tadapāsya ṣaṣṭikodanaṃ paryeṣitavyaṃ manyeta
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "It is as if, <s>Subhūti</s>, a hungry man, having obtained food of a hundred flavors, wholesome in its result, pleasant in its result, and able to ward off hunger and thirst until the end of life, were to put it aside and think that boiled <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice should be sought.

children.text: ṣaṣṭikodanaṃ labdhvā śatarasaṃ bhojanamutsṛjya vivarjya taṃ ṣaṣṭikodanaṃ paribhoktavyaṃ manyeta
children.translated_text: Having obtained boiled <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, he would abandon and set aside the food of a hundred flavors and think that boiled <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice should be eaten.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu sa puruṣaḥ paṇḍitajātīyo bhavet subhūtirāha no hīdaṃ bhagavan
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Would that man be wise by nature? <s>Subhūti</s> said, "No indeed, Blessed One."

children.text: bhagavānāha evameva subhūte bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani eke bodhisattvāḥ ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ śrutvā prajñāpāramitāṃ labdhvā prajñāpāramitāṃ riñciṣyanti prajñāpāramitāmutsrakṣyanti prajñāpāramitāṃ chorayiṣyanti prajñāpāramitāṃ dūrīkariṣyanti prajñāpāramitāṃ riñcitvā prajñāpāramitāmutsṛjya prajñāpāramitāṃ chorayitvā prajñāpāramitāṃ dūrīkṛtya tataḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānapratisaṃyuktān sūtrāntān paryeṣitavyān maṃsyante
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, in a future time there will be some bodhisattvas who, after hearing this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, after obtaining <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, will leave <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, cast off <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, throw away <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, remove <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> far from them; and after leaving, casting off, throwing away, and putting far away <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, they will think that sūtras connected with the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha vehicles are to be sought.

children.text: ye te sūtrāntāḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmimabhivadanti taiḥ sarvajñatāṃ paryeṣitavyāṃ maṃsyante
children.translated_text: They will think that omniscience is to be sought through those sūtras which speak of the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu paṇḍitajātīyāste bodhisattvā veditavyāḥ subhūtirāha no hīdaṃ bhagavan
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Should those bodhisattvas be known as wise by nature? <s>Subhūti</s> said, "No indeed, Blessed One."

children.text: bhagavānāha idam api subhūte teṣāṃ mārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as <s>mārakarma</s> (Māra's work) on their part.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma subhūte kaścideva puruṣo 'narghyaṃ maṇiratnaṃ labdhvā alpārghyeṇa alpasāreṇa maṇiratnena sārdhaṃ samīkartavyaṃ manyeta
children.translated_text: It is as if, <s>Subhūti</s>, some man, having obtained a priceless jewel, were to think it should be compared with a jewel of small price and little substance.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu sa paṇḍitajātīyaḥ puruṣo veditavyaḥ subhūtirāha no hīdaṃ bhagavan
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Should that man be known as wise by nature? <s>Subhūti</s> said, "No indeed, Blessed One."

children.text: bhagavānāha evameva subhūte bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani eke bodhisattvayānikāḥ pudgalāḥ ya idaṃ gambhīraṃ prabhāsvaraṃ prajñāpāramitāratnaṃ labdhvā śrutvā śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānena samīkartavyaṃ maṃsyante śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmau ca sarvajñatāmupāyakauśalyaṃ ca paryeṣitavyaṃ maṃsyante
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, in a future time there will be some persons in the bodhisattva vehicle who, after obtaining and hearing this deep, luminous jewel of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, will think it should be compared with the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha vehicle, and will think that omniscience and <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skill in means) are to be sought on the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha stage.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu paṇḍitajātīyāste bodhisattvā veditavyāḥ subhūtirāha no hīdaṃ bhagavan
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Should those bodhisattvas be known as wise by nature? <s>Subhūti</s> said, "No indeed, Blessed One."

children.text: bhagavānāha idam api subhūte teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as <s>mārakarma</s> (Māra's work) for those bodhisattva mahāsattvas."

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte asyāṃ gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ deśyamānāyām upadiśyamānāyām uddiśyamānāyām udgṛhyamāṇāyāṃ vācyamānāyāṃ svādhyāyyamānāyāmantaśo likhyamānāyām api bahūni pratibhānānyutpatsyante yāni cittavikṣepaṃ kariṣyanti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, while this deep <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being spoken, taught, explained, proclaimed, taken up, recited, studied, or even written down, many inspirations of eloquence will arise which will produce distraction of mind.

children.text: idam api subhūte teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mārakarma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known as a work of <s>Māra</s> for those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>. ||

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat śakyā punarbhagavan prajñāpāramitā likhitum bhagavānāha no hīdaṃ subhūte
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, then can the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> be written?" The Blessed One said: "No, <s>Subhūti</s>, this is not so.

children.text: ye kecitsubhūte prajñāpāramitāṃ lipyakṣarairlikhitvā prajñāpāramitā likhiteti maṃsyante asatīti vā akṣareṣu prajñāpāramitāmabhinivekṣyante anakṣareti vā idam api subhūte teṣāṃ mārakarma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: Those, <s>Subhūti</s>, who, after writing the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> with written letters and syllables, will think, "The <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> has been written," or "It exists," or who will fix their attention on the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> in the syllables, or think, "It is without syllables": this too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known as their work of <s>Māra</s>. ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte prajñāpāramitāyāṃ likhyamānāyāṃ deśamanasikārā utpatsyante grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīmanasikārā utpatsyante udyānamanasikārā utpatsyante gurumanasikārā utpatsyante ākhyānamanasikārā utpatsyante cauramanasikārā utpatsyante gulmasthānamanasikārā utpatsyante viśikhāmanasikārā utpatsyante śibikāmanasikārā utpatsyante sukhamanasikārā utpatsyante duḥkhamanasikārā utpatsyante bhayamanasikārā utpatsyante strīmanasikārā utpatsyante puruṣamanasikārā utpatsyante napuṃsakamanasikārā utpatsyante priyāpriyavyatyastamanasikārā utpatsyante mātāpitṛpratisaṃyuktā manasikārā utpatsyante bhrātṛbhaginīpratisaṃyuktā manasikārā utpatsyante mitrabāndhavasālohitāmātyapratisaṃyuktā manasikārā utpatsyante prajāpatiputraduhitṛpratisaṃyuktā manasikārā utpatsyante gṛhabhojanapānapratisaṃyuktā manasikārā utpatsyante cailamanasikārā utpatsyante śayanāsanamanasikārā jīvitamanasikārā itikartavyatāmanasikārā rāgamanasikārā dveṣamanasikārā mohamanasikārā ṛtumanasikārāḥ sukālamanasikārā duṣkālamanasikārā gītamanasikārā vādyamanasikārā nṛtyamanasikārāḥ kāvyanāṭaketihāsamanasikārāḥ śāstramanasikārā vyavahāramanasikārā hāsyamanasikārā lāsyamanasikārāḥ śokamanasikārā āyāsamanasikārā ātmamanasikārāḥ ityetāṃścānyāṃś ca subhūte manasikārān māraḥ pāpīyānupasaṃhariṣyati asyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ deśyamānāyām upadiśyamānāyām udgṛhyamāṇāyāṃ vācyamānāyām uddiśyamānāyāṃ svādhyāyyamānāyāmantaśo likhyamānāyām antarāyaṃ kariṣyati cittavikṣepaṃ kariṣyati bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, while the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being written, thoughts of countries will arise; thoughts of villages, cities, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, and capitals will arise; thoughts of parks will arise; thoughts of teachers will arise; thoughts of stories will arise; thoughts of thieves will arise; thoughts of guard-posts will arise; thoughts of streets will arise; thoughts of palanquins will arise; thoughts of pleasure will arise; thoughts of pain will arise; thoughts of fear will arise; thoughts of women will arise; thoughts of men will arise; thoughts of neuters will arise; thoughts in which dear and not-dear are confused will arise; thoughts connected with mother and father will arise; thoughts connected with brothers and sisters will arise; thoughts connected with friends, kinsmen, blood-relatives, and ministers will arise; thoughts connected with wife, sons, and daughters will arise; thoughts connected with house, food, and drink will arise; thoughts of clothing will arise; thoughts of beds and seats, thoughts of life, thoughts of what is to be done, thoughts of passion, thoughts of hatred, thoughts of delusion, thoughts of the season, thoughts of a good time, thoughts of a bad time, thoughts of song, thoughts of music, thoughts of dance, thoughts of poetry, drama, and history, thoughts of treatises, thoughts of business dealings, thoughts of laughter, thoughts of graceful play, thoughts of grief, thoughts of fatigue, and thoughts of self will arise. These and other thoughts, <s>Subhūti</s>, will be brought near by evil <s>Māra</s>. While this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being spoken, taught, explained, taken up, recited, proclaimed, studied, or even written down, he will make an obstacle; he will make a distraction of mind for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>.

children.text: tatra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mārakarmāṇi boddhavyāni
children.translated_text: In that matter the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should understand the works of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: buddhvā ca vivarjayitavyāni
children.translated_text: And after understanding them, he should avoid them.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte utpatsyante rājamanasikārāḥ kumāramanasikārā hastimanasikārā aśvamanasikārā rathamanasikārā gulmadarśanamanasikārāḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, thoughts of kings will arise, thoughts of princes, thoughts of elephants, thoughts of horses, thoughts of chariots, and thoughts of seeing troops.

children.text: idam api subhūte teṣāṃ mārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known as their work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte utpatsyante agnimanasikārā icchāmanasikārā dhanadhānyasamṛddhimanasikārāḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, thoughts of fire, thoughts of desire, and thoughts of abundance of wealth and grain will arise.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mārakarma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known as a work of <s>Māra</s> for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>. ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmutpatsyante lābhasatkāracīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāmantarāyā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣamāṇānāṃ deśayatāmupadiśatāmuddiśatāṃ svādhyāyatāmantaśo likhatāṃ lābhasatkāraślokasvādāścittotpīḍā vā
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, for <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who are speaking this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, teaching it, explaining it, proclaiming it, studying it, or even writing it, there will arise obstacles concerning gain and honor, robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines and requisites for the sick, or else a taste for gain, honor, and fame, or oppression of mind.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvairmahāsattvairmārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known by <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> as a work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: etāni taiḥ sarvāṇi mārakarmāṇi boddhavyāni buddhvā ca vivarjayitavyāni ||
children.translated_text: All these works of <s>Māra</s> should be understood by them, and after understanding them, they should be avoided. ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmimāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣamāṇānāṃ deśayatāmupadiśatāmuddiśatāṃ svādhyāyatāmantaśo likhatāṃ ye te gambhīrā gambhīrāḥ sūtrāntā bhaviṣyanti śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmipratisaṃyuktāḥ tān māraḥ pāpīyān bhikṣuveṣeṇopasaṃkramya upasaṃhariṣyati iha śikṣasva idaṃ likha idamuddiśa idaṃ svādhyāya itaḥ sarvajñatā niṣpatsyate iti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, when <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> are speaking this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, teaching it, explaining it, proclaiming it, studying it, or even writing it, evil <s>Māra</s> will approach in the guise of a monk and bring before them those deep, deep sūtrāntas that will be connected with the stages of the <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, saying, "Train in this; write this; proclaim this; study this; from this all-knowledge will be accomplished."

children.text: na khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena upāyakuśalena tebhyaḥ spṛhotpādayitavyā
children.translated_text: But, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who is skilled in means should not arouse longing for those.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ kiṃcāpi subhūte teṣu sūtrānteṣu śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitāni bhāṣitāni na khalu punarupāyakauśalyaṃ tatra bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmākhyātam
children.translated_text: Why is that? Although emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness are taught in those sūtras, nevertheless the skill in means of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> is not explained there.

children.text: tatra ye 'nabhijñā bhaviṣyanti bodhisattvā upāyakauśalyajñānaviśeṣasya te imāṃ gambhīrāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ riñcitavyāṃ maṃsyante
children.translated_text: There, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who will not be acquainted with the distinctive knowledge of skill in means will think that this deep <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> should be abandoned.

children.text: te imāṃ gambhīrāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ riñcitvā śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmipratisaṃyukteṣu sūtrānteṣu upāyakauśalyaṃ paryeṣitavyaṃ maṃsyante
children.translated_text: Having abandoned this deep <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, they will think that skill in means should be sought in sūtras connected with the grounds of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mārakarma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a work of <s>Māra</s>. ||

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte dhārmaśravaṇikaśchandiko bhaviṣyati prajñāpāramitām udgrahītukāmaḥ dharmabhāṇakaś ca kilāsī bhaviṣyati na dharmaṃ deśayitukāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, a Dharma-hearer will be eager and desirous of taking up the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, while the Dharma-preacher will be indolent and not desirous of teaching the Dharma.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena visāmagrīmārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a discordant work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte dharmabhāṇakaś ca akilāsī bhaviṣyati prajñāpāramitāṃ dātukāmaḥ dhārmaśravaṇikaś ca kilāsī vā bahukṛtyo vā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the Dharma-preacher will not be indolent and will wish to give the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, while the Dharma-hearer will be indolent or burdened with many duties.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena visāmagrīmārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a discordant work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte dhārmaśravaṇikaśchandiko bhaviṣyati prajñāpāramitāmudgrahītukāmo dhārayitukāmo vācayitukāmaḥ paryavāptukāmaḥ pravartayitukāmo 'ntaśo likhitukāmo 'pi bhaviṣyati gatimāṃś ca matimāṃś ca smṛtimāṃś ca bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, a Dharma-hearer will be eager, desirous of taking up the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, desirous of retaining it, reciting it, mastering it, setting it in motion, and even writing it; he will also be quick, intelligent, and mindful.

children.text: dharmabhāṇakaścānyaddeśāntaraṃ kṣepsyate nodghaṭṭitajño vā na vā vipañcitajñaḥ anabhijño vā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: But the Dharma-preacher will be sent off to another region, or he will not understand from a brief indication, or will not understand from detailed exposition, or will be inexperienced.

children.text: iyam api subhūte tatra visāmagrī bhaviṣyati prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ deśyamānāyām upadiśyamānāyām uddiśyamānāyāṃ svādhyāyyamānāyāṃ śikṣyamāṇāyāmantaśaḥ likhyamānāyām
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, will be a discord there, when the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being spoken, taught, explained, recited, studied, learned, and even written.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena visāmagrīmārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a discordant work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte dharmabhāṇakaś ca akilāsī bhaviṣyatyabhijño dātukāmo vācayitukāma imāṃ prajñāpāramitām dhārmaśravaṇikaś ca deśāntaraṃ prasthito bhaviṣyati nodghaṭṭitajño vā na vā vipañcitajño 'nabhijño vā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the Dharma-preacher will not be indolent, will be knowledgeable, and will wish to give and recite this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, while the Dharma-hearer will have set out for another region, or will not understand from a brief indication, or will not understand from detailed exposition, or will be inexperienced.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena visāmagrīmārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a discordant work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte dharmabhāṇakaś ca āmiṣaguruko lābhasatkāracīvaraguruko bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the Dharma-preacher will regard material offerings as weighty and will regard gain, honor, and robes as weighty.

children.text: dhārmaśravaṇikāś ca alpecchaḥ saṃtuṣṭaḥ pravivikto 'rthaṃ vā na dātukāmo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And the Dharma-hearers will have few wishes, be content and secluded, or will not wish to give material support.

children.text: iyam api subhūte tatra visāmagrī bhaviṣyati prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣyamāṇāyāṃ likhyamānāyām
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, will be a discord there when the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being learned and written.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte dhārmaśravaṇikaś ca śrāddho bhaviṣyati imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ śrotukāmo 'rthamavaboddhukāmo 'rthaṃ dātukāmo 'rthaṃ parityaktukāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the Dharma-hearer will be faithful, desirous of hearing this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, desirous of understanding its meaning, desirous of giving support, and desirous of relinquishing possessions.

children.text: dharmabhāṇakaś ca aśrāddho bhaviṣyati alpeccho vā na vā bhāṣitukāmaḥ
children.translated_text: But the Dharma-preacher will be faithless, or he will have little desire, or he will not wish to speak.

children.text: ato 'pi subhūte visāmagrīmārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: From this too, <s>Subhūti</s>, a discordant work of <s>Māra</s> should be known.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte dhārmaśravaṇikaś ca śrāddho bhaviṣyati śrotukāmo 'rthamavaboddhukāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the Dharma-hearer will be faithful, desirous of hearing, and desirous of understanding the meaning.

children.text: dharmabhāṇakasya ca tāni sūtrāṇi dharmāntarāyikatayā na sambhaviṣyanti nāvatariṣyanti
children.translated_text: But for the Dharma-preacher those sūtras will not arise and will not enter in, because of an obstruction to Dharma.

children.text: ato 'pi subhūte dhārmaśravaṇikasyāprāptadharmabhāṇinaḥ prativāṇī bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: From this too, <s>Subhūti</s>, the Dharma-hearer will meet with refusal from a Dharma-preacher who has not obtained the Dharma.

children.text: iyam api subhūte tatra visāmagrī bhaviṣyati prajñāpāramitāmudgṛhṇatāṃ dhārayatāṃ vācayatāṃ paryavāpnuvatāṃ pravartayatāmantaśo likhatām
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, will be a discord there among those taking up the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retaining it, reciting it, mastering it, setting it in motion, and even writing it.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte dharmabhāṇakaś ca bhāṣitukāmo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the Dharma-preacher will be desirous of speaking.

children.text: dhārmaśravaṇikaś ca acchandiko bhaviṣyati śravaṇāya
children.translated_text: But the Dharma-hearer will be without desire for hearing.

children.text: iyam api subhūte tatra visāmagrī bhaviṣyati prajñāpāramitāmudgrahītuṃ dhārayituṃ vācayituṃ paryavāptuṃ pravartayitumantaśo likhitum
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, will be a discord there for taking up the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retaining it, reciting it, mastering it, setting it in motion, and even writing it.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte dhārmaśravaṇiko middhaguruko bhaviṣyati kāyaguruko bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the Dharma-hearer will be overcome by sleepiness and weighed down in body.

children.text: sa tena middhagurukatvena samanvāgataḥ kāyaklamathena samanvāgato na śrotukāmo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Endowed with that heaviness of sleep and endowed with bodily fatigue, he will not wish to hear.

children.text: dharmabhāṇakaś ca bhāṣitukāmo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: But the Dharma-preacher will be desirous of speaking.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena visāmagrīmārakarma veditavyam
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a discordant work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte dharmabhāṇako middhaguruko bhaviṣyati kāyaguruko bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the Dharma-preacher will be overcome by sleepiness and weighed down in body.

children.text: sa tena middhagurukatvena samanvāgataḥ kāyaklamathena samanvāgato na bhāṣitukāmo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Because he is endowed with that heaviness of torpor, and endowed with bodily fatigue, he will not wish to speak.

children.text: dhārmaśravaṇikaś ca śrotukāmo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: But a hearer of the Dharma will wish to listen.

children.text: iyam api subhūte tatra visāmagrī bhaviṣyati likhanāya vācanāya paryavāptaye vā
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, will be a discord there for writing, recitation, or mastery.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mārakarma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as <s>Māra</s>'s work.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte prajñāpāramitāyāṃ likhyamānāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ śikṣyamāṇāyāṃ kaścideva tatrāgatya nirayāṇāmavarṇaṃ bhāṣiṣyate tiryagyoneravarṇaṃ bhāṣiṣyate pretaviṣayasyāvarṇaṃ bhāṣiṣyate asurakāyānāmavarṇaṃ bhāṣiṣyate evaṃduḥkhā nirayāḥ evaṃduḥkhā tiryagyoniḥ evaṃduḥkhaḥ pretaviṣayaḥ evaṃduḥkhā āsurāḥ kāyāḥ evaṃduḥkhāḥ saṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, while the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being written, spoken, or studied, someone may come there and speak dispraise of the hells, speak dispraise of animal birth, speak dispraise of the realm of pretas, and speak dispraise of the bodies of asuras: 'Thus painful are the hells; thus painful is animal birth; thus painful is the realm of pretas; thus painful are the asura bodies; thus painful are conditioned formations.'

children.text: ihaiva duḥkhasyāntaḥ karaṇīya iti
children.translated_text: The end of suffering must be made here itself.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena visāmagrīmārakarma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as discord and <s>Māra</s>'s work.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte prajñāpāramitāyāṃ likhyamānāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ śikṣyamāṇāyāṃ vā kaścideva tatrāgatya devānāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣiṣyate evaṃ sukhitā devāḥ evaṃsukhāḥ svargāḥ evaṃ kāmadhātau kāmāḥ sevitavyāḥ evaṃ rūpadhātau dhyānāni samāpattavyāni evamārūpyadhātau tatsamāpattayaḥ samāpattavyāḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, while the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being written, spoken, or studied, someone may come there and speak praise of the gods: 'Thus happy are the gods; thus pleasant are the heavens; thus, in the desire realm, pleasures should be enjoyed; thus, in the form realm, the meditations should be entered; thus, in the formless realm, those attainments should be entered.'

children.text: tad api ca sarvaṃ prajñatā vimṛśya sarvaiva duḥkhopapattiriti
children.translated_text: But all that too, when examined with wisdom, is only an arising into suffering.

children.text: uktaṃ hīdaṃ bhagavatā acchaṭāsaṃghātamātrakam apyahaṃ bhikṣavo bhavābhinirvṛttiṃ na varṇayāmi
children.translated_text: For this has been said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, I do not praise the production of existence even for the mere duration of a finger-snap.'

children.text: sarvaṃ hi saṃskṛtamanityaṃ sarvaṃ bhayāvagataṃ duḥkhaṃ sarvaṃ traidhātukaṃ śūnyaṃ sarvadharmā anātmānaḥ
children.translated_text: For everything conditioned is impermanent; everything involved with fear is suffering; the whole triple world is empty; all dharmas are without self.

children.text: tadevaṃ sarvamaśāśvatamanityaṃ duḥkhaṃ vipariṇāmadharmakaṃ viditvā paṇḍitairihaiva srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptavyam sakṛdāgāmiphalamanāgāmiphalam ihaivārhattvaṃ prāptavyam
children.translated_text: Knowing in this way that everything is unstable, impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, the wise should attain the fruit of stream-entry here itself, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and arhatship here itself.

children.text: mā no bhūyastābhiḥ saṃpattivipattibhirduḥkhabhūyiṣṭhābhiḥ samavadhānaṃ bhūditi
children.translated_text: May there be no further meeting for us with those gains and losses that are mostly suffering.

children.text: tatraike bodhisattvāḥ saṃvegamāpatsyante
children.translated_text: There some bodhisattvas will fall into spiritual agitation.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena visāmagrīmārakarma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as discord and <s>Māra</s>'s work.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte ye 'pi te bhikṣavo dharmabhāṇakāḥ te ekākitābhiratā bhaviṣyanti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, those monks who are Dharma-preachers will delight in solitude.

children.text: ye 'pi dhārmaśravaṇikāste 'pi parṣadgurukā bhaviṣyanti
children.translated_text: And those who are hearers of the Dharma will be attached to assemblies.

children.text: te 'pi dharmabhāṇakā evaṃ vakṣyanti ye māmanuvartsyanti tebhyo 'hamimāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ dāsyāmi
children.translated_text: Those Dharma-preachers too will say, 'I will give this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> to those who follow me.

children.text: ye māṃ nānuvartsyanti tebhyo na dāsyāmīti
children.translated_text: I will not give it to those who do not follow me.'

children.text: evaṃ te kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca arthikatayā chandikatayā dharmagauraveṇa taṃ dharmabhāṇakamanuvartsyanti na cāvakāśaṃ dāsyanti sa ca dharmabhāṇaka āmiṣakiṃcitkābhilāṣī te ca na dātukāmāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus those good sons and good daughters, because of need, desire, and reverence for the Dharma, will follow that Dharma-preacher and will give him no opening; and that Dharma-preacher will desire some material gain, while they will not wish to give it.

children.text: sa ca tena tena gamiṣyati yena yena durbhikṣaś ca ayogakṣemaś ca jīvitāntarāyaś ca bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And he will go wherever there is famine, lack of safety, and danger to life.

children.text: te ca dhārmaśravaṇikāḥ parebhyaḥ śroṣyanti asau pradeśo durbhikṣaś ca ayogakṣemaś ca
children.translated_text: Those hearers of the Dharma will hear from others, 'That region has famine and lack of safety.

children.text: tasmiṃś ca pradeśe jīvitāntarāyo bhavediti
children.translated_text: And in that region there may be danger to life.'

children.text: sa ca dharmabhāṇakastān kulaputrānevamabhivyāhariṣyati amuṣmin kulaputrāḥ pradeśe durbhikṣabhayam
children.translated_text: And that Dharma-preacher will address those good sons in this way: 'Good sons, in that region there is danger of famine.

children.text: kaccitkulaputrā yūyamāgamiṣyatha mā paścādvipratisāriṇo bhaviṣyatha durbhikṣabhayaṃ praviṣṭāḥ evaṃ te tena dharmabhāṇakena sūkṣmeṇopāyena pratikṣepsyate
children.translated_text: Good sons, will you come? Do not be remorseful later, after entering into the danger of famine.' In this way they will be turned away by that Dharma-preacher through a subtle means.

children.text: te ca nirviṇṇarūpā evaṃ jñāsyanti pratyākhyānanimittānyetāni naitāni dātukāmatānimittānīti
children.translated_text: And they, becoming dispirited, will understand, 'These are signs of refusal; these are not signs that he wishes to give.'

children.text: nāyaṃ dātukāma iti viditvā nānuvartsyanti
children.translated_text: Knowing, 'This one does not wish to give,' they will not follow him.

children.text: iyam api subhūte tatra visāmagrī bhaviṣyati prajñāpāramitāyāṃ likhyamānāyāṃ śikṣyamāṇāyāṃ deśyamānāyām upadiśyamānāyām uddiśyamānāyāṃ svādhyāyyamānāyām
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, will be a discord there while the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being written, studied, taught, explained, recited, and rehearsed.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mārakarma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as <s>Māra</s>'s work.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte dharmabhāṇako yena jantubhayaṃ yena vyālabhayaṃ yenāmanuṣyabhayaṃ tena samprasthito bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the Dharma-preacher will have set out toward a place where there is danger from creatures, danger from wild beasts, and danger from nonhuman beings.

children.text: sa tena caran viharan yena vyālakāntāraṃ sarīsṛpakāntāraṃ corakāntāraṃ pānīyakāntāraṃ durbhikṣakāntāraṃ tena prakramiṣyati
children.translated_text: While moving and dwelling there, he will proceed toward a wilderness of wild beasts, a wilderness of reptiles, a wilderness of thieves, a waterless wilderness, and a wilderness of famine.

children.text: sa tān dhārmaśravaṇikānevaṃ vakṣyati yatkhalu kulaputrā jānīdhvaṃ yasmin pradeśe jantubhayaṃ vyālabhayaṃ kravyādabhayaṃ sarīsṛpakāntāraṃ corakāntāraṃ pānīyakāntāraṃ durbhikṣakāntāraṃ tena vayaṃ samprasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: He will say to those hearers of the Dharma, 'Good sons, know this: we have set out toward a region where there is danger from creatures, danger from wild beasts, danger from flesh-eaters, a wilderness of reptiles, a wilderness of thieves, a waterless wilderness, and a wilderness of famine.

children.text: jānīdhvaṃ kulaputrāḥ śakyatha yūyametāni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavitum evaṃ tān sūkṣmeṇopāyena pratyākhyāsyati
children.translated_text: Know, good sons, whether you are able to experience these sufferings.' In this way he will reject them through a subtle means.

children.text: tataste nirvetsyante
children.translated_text: Then they will become disenchanted.

children.text: nirviṇṇāḥ santo nānuvartsyanti
children.translated_text: Being disenchanted, they will not follow along.

children.text: te punareva pratyudāvartsyante
children.translated_text: They will turn back again.

children.text: ayam api subhūte prajñāpāramitāyām antarāya utpatsyate uddiśyamānāyāḥ svādhyāyyamānāyāḥ yāvallikhyamānāyāḥ
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, will arise as an obstruction to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> while it is being recited, studied, and so on up to being written.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena visāmagrīmārakarma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a discordant work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte dharmabhāṇako bhikṣurmitrakulabhikṣādakulaguruko bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, a monk who is a Dharma-preacher will be one who gives weight to friendly households and alms-giving households.

children.text: sa tayā mitrakulabhikṣādakulagurukatayā abhīkṣṇaṃ mitrakulabhikṣādakulānyavalokayitavyāny upasaṃkramitavyāni maṃsyate
children.translated_text: Because he gives weight to those friendly households and alms-giving households, he will think that the friendly households and alms-giving households must be repeatedly looked in on and approached.

children.text: sa tayā abhīkṣṇāvalokanatayā bahukṛtyatayā tān dhārmaśravaṇikān pratyākhyāsyati asti tāvanme kiṃcid avalokayitavyam asti tāvanmamopasaṃkramitavyamiti
children.translated_text: Because he repeatedly looks in on them and has many duties, he will put off those hearers of Dharma, saying, 'For the moment I have something to look after; for the moment I have somewhere to go.'

children.text: iyam api subhūte tatra visāmagrī bhaviṣyati prajñāpāramitāyāṃ likhyamānāyāṃ paryavāpyamāṇāyām
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, will be a discord there while the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being written and mastered.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mārakarma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: iti hi subhūte māraḥ pāpīyāṃstaistaiḥ prakāraistathā tathā ceṣṭiṣyate yathemāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ na kaścidudgrahīṣyati na dhārayiṣyati na vācayiṣyati na paryavāpsyati na pravartayiṣyati na deśayiṣyati nopadekṣyati noddekṣyati na svādhyāsyati na lekhayiṣyati na likhiṣyati
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the evil one will strive in these and those various ways, acting by such and such means so that no one will take up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, set it in motion, teach it, explain it, point it out, rehearse it, have it copied, or copy it.

children.text: tasmāttarhi subhūte yāvanto 'ntarāyā visāmagryāṃ saṃvartante tāni sarvāṇi bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mārakarmāṇīti boddhavyāni buddhvā ca vivarjayitavyānīti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, whatever obstructions lead to discord, all of them should be understood by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as works of <s>Māra</s>; and having understood them, they should be avoided.

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat kimatra bhagavan kāraṇaṃ yadiha māraḥ pāpīyānevaṃ mahāntamudyogamāpatsyate tathā tathā copāyena ceṣṭiṣyate yathemāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ na kaścidudgrahīṣyati na dhārayiṣyati na vācayiṣyati na paryavāpsyati na pravartayiṣyati na deśayiṣyati nopadekṣyati noddekṣyati na svādhyāsyati na lekhayiṣyati na likhiṣyati evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat prajñāpāramitānirjātā hi subhūte buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sarvajñatā
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'What is the reason here, Blessed One, that <s>Māra</s> the evil one will undertake such great effort and will act by such and such means so that no one will take up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, set it in motion, teach it, explain it, point it out, rehearse it, have it copied, or copy it?' When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: '<s>Subhūti</s>, the omniscience of the blessed Buddhas is born from the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: sarvajñatānirjātaṃ ca tathāgataśāsanam
children.translated_text: And the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is born from omniscience.

children.text: tathāgataśāsananirjātaṃ ca aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ kleśaprahāṇam
children.translated_text: And from the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> comes the abandonment of the defilements by immeasurable, innumerable beings.

children.text: prahīṇakleśānāṃ ca māraḥ pāpīyānavatāraṃ na labhate
children.translated_text: And <s>Māra</s> the evil one finds no opening among those whose defilements have been abandoned.

children.text: alabhamāno duḥkhārto durmanāḥ śokaśalyaparigato bhavati
children.translated_text: Finding no opening, he becomes afflicted, dejected, and pierced by the dart of grief.

children.text: ataḥ sa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ likhyamānāyāṃ paryavāpyamāṇāyāṃ mahatā saṃvegena mahāntamudyogamāpadyate
children.translated_text: Therefore, while the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being written and mastered, he undertakes great effort with great agitation.

children.text: sa mahatodyogena tathā tathopāyena ceṣṭate yathā na kaścidimāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhedvā paryavāpnuyādveti ||
children.translated_text: With great effort he acts by such and such means so that no one may write or master this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte māraḥ pāpīyān śramaṇaveṣeṇāgatya bhedaṃ prakṣepsyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the evil one will come in the guise of an ascetic and sow division.

children.text: evaṃ ca navayānasamprasthitāḥ kulaputrā vivecayiṣyanti naiṣā prajñāpāramitā yāmāyuṣmantaḥ śṛṇvanti
children.translated_text: And he will separate the good sons newly set out in the vehicle in this way: 'This is not the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> that you venerable ones are hearing.

children.text: yathā punarmama sūtrāgataṃ sūtraparyāpannam iyaṃ sā prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: Rather, according to what has come down in my sūtras and is included in the sūtras, this is that <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

children.text: ityevaṃ subhūte māraḥ pāpīyān saṃśayaṃ prakṣepsyati
children.translated_text: In this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the evil one will sow doubt.

children.text: evaṃ ca punaḥ subhūte māraḥ pāpīyān śramaṇaveṣeṇāgatya bhedaṃ prakṣipya navayānasamprasthitān bodhisattvānalpabuddhikān mandabuddhikān parīttabuddhikān andhīkṛtān avyākṛtān anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃśayaṃ pātayiṣyati
children.translated_text: And again, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the evil one will come in the guise of an ascetic, sow division, and cast into doubt about unsurpassed complete awakening those bodhisattvas newly set out in the vehicle who are of little understanding, dull understanding, limited understanding, blinded, and uninstructed.

children.text: te saṃśayaprāptā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ nodgrahīṣyanti na dhārayiṣyanti na vācayiṣyanti na paryavāpsyanti na pravartayiṣyanti na deśayiṣyanti nopadekṣyanti noddekṣyanti na svādhyāsyanti na lekhayiṣyanti na likhiṣyanti
children.translated_text: Having fallen into doubt, they will not take up this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, set it in motion, teach it, explain it, point it out, rehearse it, have it copied, or copy it.

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mārakarma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte māraḥ pāpīyān bhikṣūnnirmāya buddhaveṣeṇāgatya evaṃ mārakarmopasaṃhariṣyati yo bodhisattvo gambhīreṣu dharmeṣu carati sa bhūtakoṭiṃ sākṣātkaroti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the evil one, having conjured monks and having come in the guise of a Buddha, will bring forward this work of <s>Māra</s>: 'A bodhisattva who courses in profound dharmas realizes the limit of reality.

children.text: sa śrāvako bhavati na bodhisattvo yathāyaṃ bodhisattva iti
children.translated_text: He becomes a <s>śrāvaka</s>, not a bodhisattva like this bodhisattva.'

children.text: idam api subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mārakarma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> as a work of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: evaṃ subhūte māraḥ pāpīyānevamādikāni subahūni anyāny api mārakarmāṇyutpādayiṣyati asyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ likhyamānāyāṃ paryavāpyamāṇāyām
children.translated_text: In this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the evil one will produce these and many other such works of <s>Māra</s> while this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being written and mastered.

children.text: tāni bodhisattvena mahāsattvena boddhavyāni
children.translated_text: They should be understood by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

children.text: buddhvā ca vivarjayitavyāni
children.translated_text: And having understood them, they should be avoided.

children.text: na bhaktavyāni
children.translated_text: They should not be followed.

children.text: ārabdhavīryeṇa smṛtimatā samprajānatā ca bhavitavyam ||
children.translated_text: One should be energetic, mindful, and clearly aware.

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat evametadbhagavan evametatsugata
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'So it is, Blessed One; so it is, <s>Sugata</s>.'

children.text: yāni tāni bhagavan mahāratnāni tāni bahupratyarthikāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: Those great jewels, Blessed One, are things that have many rivals and adversaries.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ yaduta durlabhatvānmahārghatvācca
children.translated_text: For what reason? Because they are rare and very precious.

children.text: agrāṇi hi tāni bhagavan bhavanti
children.translated_text: For they are foremost things, Blessed One.

children.text: tasmāttāni ca bahupratyarthikāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: Therefore they have many rivals and adversaries.

children.text: evameva bhagavan asyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ prāyeṇa bahavo 'ntarāyā utpatsyante
children.translated_text: In just the same way, Blessed One, for this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> many obstacles will generally arise.

children.text: tatra ye 'ntarāyavaśena kusīdā bhaviṣyanti veditavyamidaṃ bhagavan mārādhiṣṭhitāste bodhisattvā bhaviṣyanti navayānasamprasthitāś ca te bhagavan bhaviṣyanti alpabuddhayaś ca te bhagavan bhaviṣyanti mandabuddhayaś ca te bhagavan bhaviṣyanti parīttabuddhayaś ca te bhagavan bhaviṣyanti viparyastabuddhayaś ca te bhagavan bhaviṣyanti
children.translated_text: There, Blessed One, those who become indolent because of the force of obstacles should be known as bodhisattvas under the influence of <s>Māra</s>; and they, Blessed One, will be newly set out in the vehicle, of little understanding, dull in understanding, limited in understanding, and perverted in understanding.

children.text: nāpi teṣāmudārodāreṣu dharmeṣu cittaṃ prakramiṣyati ye imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ nodgrahītavyāṃ maṃsyante na dhārayitavyāṃ na vācayitavyāṃ na paryavāptavyāṃ na pravartayitavyāṃ na deśayitavyāṃ nopadeṣṭavyāṃ noddeṣṭavyāṃ na svādhyātavyāṃ na lekhayitavyām antaśo na likhitavyām api maṃsyante ||
children.translated_text: Nor will their minds proceed toward the lofty and most lofty dharmas, those who think that this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> should not be taken up, should not be retained, should not be recited, should not be mastered, should not be set in motion, should not be taught, should not be instructed, should not be expounded, should not be studied, should not be caused to be written, and should not even be written down.

children.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat evametatsubhūte evam etat
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>; so it is.

children.text: mārādhiṣṭhitāste subhūte bodhisattvā veditavyāḥ
children.translated_text: Those bodhisattvas, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be known as under the influence of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: navayānasamprasthitāś ca te subhūte bodhisattvā bhaviṣyanti alpabuddhayaś ca te bhaviṣyanti mandabuddhayaś ca te bhaviṣyanti parīttabuddhayaś ca te bhaviṣyanti viparyastabuddhayaś ca te bhaviṣyanti
children.translated_text: And those bodhisattvas, <s>Subhūti</s>, will be newly set out in the vehicle; they will be of little understanding, dull in understanding, limited in understanding, and perverted in understanding.

children.text: na ca teṣāmudārodāreṣu dharmeṣu cittaṃ prakramiṣyati ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ nodgrahītavyāṃ maṃsyante na dhārayitavyāṃ na vācayitavyāṃ na paryavāptavyāṃ na pravartayitavyāṃ nopadeṣṭavyāṃ noddeṣṭavyāṃ na svādhyātavyāṃ na lekhayitavyāmantaśo na likhitavyām api maṃsyante ||
children.translated_text: And the minds of those who think that this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> should not be taken up, should not be retained, should not be recited, should not be mastered, should not be set in motion, should not be instructed, should not be expounded, should not be studied, should not be caused to be written, and should not even be written down, will not proceed toward the lofty and most lofty dharmas.

children.text: kiṃcāpi subhūte imāni mārakarmāṇyutpatsyante subahavaścātra māradoṣā antarāyakarā utpatsyante
children.translated_text: Although, <s>Subhūti</s>, these works of <s>Māra</s> will arise, and very many faults of <s>Māra</s> that cause obstruction will arise here,

children.text: atha ca subhūte ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmudgrahītavyāṃ maṃsyante dhārayitavyāṃ vācayitavyāṃ paryavāptavyāṃ pravartayitavyāmupadeṣṭavyāmuddeṣṭavyāṃ svādhyātavyāṃ lekhayitavyāmantaśo likhitavyām api maṃsyante veditavyametatsubhūte buddhānubhāvena buddhādhiṣṭhānena te maṃsyante
children.translated_text: nevertheless, <s>Subhūti</s>, those who think that this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> should be taken up, retained, recited, mastered, set in motion, instructed, expounded, studied, caused to be written, and even written down, should be known, <s>Subhūti</s>, to think so through the power of the Buddhas and through the sustaining force of the Buddhas.

children.text: buddhaparigraheṇodgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti pravartayiṣyanti deśayiṣyantyupadekṣyantyuddekṣyanti svādhyāsyanti lekhayiṣyantyantaśo likhiṣyantīti
children.translated_text: Through the protection of the Buddhas they will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, set it in motion, teach it, instruct it, expound it, study it, cause it to be written, and even write it down.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ māro 'pi hyatra pāpīyān mahāntamudyogamāpatsyate antarāyakaraṇāya
children.translated_text: For what reason? For here too the wicked <s>Māra</s> will undertake a great effort to create obstruction.

children.text: tathāgato 'pyarhan samyaksaṃbuddha udyogamāpatsyate 'nuparigrahāyeti ||
children.translated_text: And the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, will also undertake an effort to protect it.

children.text: Chapter 12

atha khalu bhagavān punarapyāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimāmantrayate sma tadyathāpi nāma subhūte striyā bahavaḥ putrā bhaveyuḥ pañca vā daśa vā viṃśatirvā triṃśadvā catvāriṃśadvā pañcāśadvā śataṃ vā sahasraṃ vā
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again addressed venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: It is, <s>Subhūti</s>, just as if a woman had many sons, whether five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, or a thousand.

children.text: sarve te māturglānāyā udyogamāpadyeran kathamasmākaṃ māturjīvitāntarāyo na bhavediti kathamasmākaṃ mātā ciraṃ jīvet kathamasmākaṃ mātuḥ kāyo na vinaśyet kathamasmākaṃ mātā cirasthitikā bhavet kathamasmākaṃ māturnāma avinaṣṭaṃ bhavet kathamasmākaṃ māturna duḥkhā vedanotpadyeta na cāsyā asparśavihāraḥ amanaāpaḥ kāye utpadyeta
children.translated_text: All of them, when their mother was ill, would undertake effort, thinking, 'How may there be no danger to our mother's life? How may our mother live long? How may our mother's body not perish? How may our mother remain long? How may our mother's name not be destroyed? How may no painful feeling arise for our mother, and may no unpleasant and disagreeable contact arise in her body?'

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ etayā hi vayaṃ janitāḥ
children.translated_text: For what reason? For we were born from her.

children.text: duṣkarakārikaiṣā asmākaṃ jīvitasya dātrī lokasya ca saṃdarśayitrī
children.translated_text: She has performed difficult deeds; she is the giver of our life and the one who showed us the world.

children.text: iti te putrāstāṃ mātaraṃ sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ sudhṛtāṃ dhārayeyuḥ sugopāyitāṃ gopāyeyuḥ sukelāyitāṃ kelāyeyuḥ mā khalvasyāḥ kācidduḥkhā vedanā duḥkho vā sparśa utpadyeta cakṣuṣo vā śrotrato vā ghrāṇato vā jihvāto vā kāyato vā manasto vā vātato vā pittato vā śleṣmato vā saṃnipātato vā daṃśato vā maśakato vā sarīsṛpato vā manuṣyato vā amanuṣyato vā āpātato vā utpātato vā aniṣṭanipātaḥ śarīre nipatet
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, those sons would sustain that mother with every provision for happiness; they would guard her as one well guarded and cherish her as one well cherished, thinking, 'May no painful feeling or painful contact arise for her from the eye, or from the ear, or from the nose, or from the tongue, or from the body, or from the mind, or from wind, or from bile, or from phlegm, or from a combination of humors, or from biting insects, or from mosquitoes, or from creeping creatures, or from humans, or from nonhumans, or from accident, or from calamity; may no undesirable blow fall upon her body.'

children.text: evaṃ te putrāstāṃ mātaraṃ sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ samanvāhṛtya kelāyeyur mamāyeyurgopāyeyuḥ eṣāsmākaṃ mātā janayitrī duṣkarakārikaiṣā asmākaṃ jīvitasya dātrī lokasya ca saṃdarśayitrīti
children.translated_text: In this way those sons, attending to that mother with every provision for happiness, would cherish her, make her their own, and guard her, thinking, 'This is our mother, our birth-giver; she has performed difficult deeds; she is the giver of our life and the one who showed us the world.'

children.text: evameva subhūte tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ samanvāharanti
children.translated_text: In just the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas, attend to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: ye 'pi te likhanti udgṛhṇanti dhārayanti vācayanti paryavāpnuvanti pravartayanti deśayantyupadiśantyuddiśanti svādhyāyanti sarve te tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyānubhāvena adhiṣṭhānena samanvāhāreṇa
children.translated_text: Those too who write it, take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, set it in motion, teach it, instruct in it, point it out, and study it, all do so through the power, sustaining resolve, and attentive regard of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one.

children.text: ye 'pi te 'nyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā etarhi tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca sarvasattvānāṃ cānukampakā anukampāmupādāya te 'pi sarve imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ samanvāharanti autsukyamāpadyante kimitīyaṃ prajñāpāramitā cirasthitikā bhavet kimityasyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā nāma avinaṣṭaṃ bhavet kimityasyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā bhāṣyamāṇāyā likhyamānāyāḥ śikṣyamāṇāyā māraḥ pāpīyān mārakāyikā vā devatā antarāyaṃ na kuryuriti
children.translated_text: And those other <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones, who at present remain, endure, and live in other world-systems for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the great body of people, of gods and humans, and who are compassionate toward all beings, having taken up compassion, all of them too attend to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and take concern: 'How may this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> remain for a long time? How may the name of this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> not be lost? How, while this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is being spoken, written, and studied, may <s>Māra</s> the evil one, or deities of <s>Māra</s>'s host, not make an obstruction?'

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā enāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ kelāyanti mamāyanti gopāyanti
children.translated_text: In this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones, cherish this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, hold it as their own, and protect it.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ eṣā hi mātā janayitrī tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānām
children.translated_text: Why is that? For she is the mother and begetter of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones.

children.text: asyāḥ sarvajñatāyā darśayitrī lokasya ca saṃdarśayitrī
children.translated_text: She is the revealer of this omniscience and the one who makes the world clearly seen.

children.text: atonirjātā hi subhūte tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: For from her, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones, have arisen.

children.text: prajñāpāramitā hi subhūte tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya sarvajñajñānasya janayitrī darśayitrī evamasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī
children.translated_text: For <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the begetter and revealer of this omniscient knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones; thus she is the one who makes this world clearly seen.

children.text: atonirjātā hi subhūte tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ sarvajñatā
children.translated_text: For from her, <s>Subhūti</s>, the omniscience of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones, has arisen.

children.text: ye 'pi kecitsubhūte atīte 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ te 'pi sarve enāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones in the past time fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, they all fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening by relying on this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: ye 'pi te subhūte bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante te 'pi sarve enāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante
children.translated_text: And whatever <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones there will be in the future time, <s>Subhūti</s>, who will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening, they all too will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening by relying on this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: ye 'pi te subhūte etarhi aprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā daśadiśi loke tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca anukampakā anukampāmupādāya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ te 'pi sarve enāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: And whatever <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones at present, <s>Subhūti</s>, remain, endure, and live in immeasurable, innumerable world-systems in the ten directions of the world for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the great body of people, of gods and humans, compassionate and having taken up compassion, and have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, they all too have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening by relying on this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: aham api subhūte etarhi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha enāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ
children.translated_text: I too, <s>Subhūti</s>, at present, as a <s>Tathāgata</s>, arhat, perfectly awakened one, have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening by relying on this very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: evamiyaṃ subhūte prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ janayitrī evamasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the begetter of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones, and thus the one who makes this world clearly seen.

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat yadbhagavānevamāha prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrīti kathaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī katamaś ca bhagavan lokastathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairākhyātaḥ evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat pañca subhūte skandhāḥ tathāgatena loka ityākhyātāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'When the Blessed One says that <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the one who makes this world clearly seen for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones, how, Blessed One, is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> the one who makes this world clearly seen for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones? And what, Blessed One, is the world declared by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones?' When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: '<s>Subhūti</s>, the five aggregates have been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be the world.'

children.text: katame pañca yaduta rūpaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārā vijñānam
children.translated_text: Which five? Namely, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness.

children.text: ime subhūte pañca skandhāstathāgatena loka ityākhyātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These five aggregates, <s>Subhūti</s>, have been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be the world.

children.text: subhūtirāha kathaṃ bhagavaṃstathāgatānāṃ prajñāpāramitayā pañca skandhā darśitāḥ kiṃ vā bhagavan prajñāpāramitayā darśitam evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat na lujyante na pralujyante iti subhūte pañca skandhā loka iti tathāgatānāṃ prajñāpāramitayā darśitāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'How, Blessed One, have the five aggregates been shown by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> through <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>? Or what, Blessed One, has been shown through <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>?' When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: '<s>Subhūti</s>, as they are not broken down and not completely broken down, the five aggregates have been shown by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> through <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> as the world.'

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ na lujyante na pralujyante iti darśitāḥ śūnyatāsvabhāvā hi subhūte pañca skandhāḥ asvabhāvatvāt
children.translated_text: Why is that? They have been shown as not broken down and not completely broken down because the five aggregates, <s>Subhūti</s>, are empty by nature, since they lack own-being.

children.text: na ca subhūte śūnyatā lujyate vā pralujyate vā
children.translated_text: And emptiness, <s>Subhūti</s>, is neither broken down nor completely broken down.

children.text: evamiyaṃ subhūte prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the one who makes this world clearly seen for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened ones.

children.text: na ca subhūte ānimittaṃ vā apraṇihitaṃ vā anabhisaṃskāro vā anutpādo vā abhāvo vā dharmadhāturvā lujyate vā pralujyate vā
children.translated_text: And, <s>Subhūti</s>, neither signlessness, nor wishlessness, nor non-fabrication, nor non-arising, nor non-existence, nor the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of reality) is broken down or completely broken down.

children.text: evamiyaṃ subhūte prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī ||
children.translated_text: In this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the revealer of this world for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ asaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvā iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is: beings are immeasurable, beings are innumerable.
