children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ asaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvā iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti sattvāsvabhāvatayā subhūte aprameyāḥ sattvā asaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvā iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is that beings are immeasurable and beings are innumerable? Because beings lack own-being, <s>Subhūti</s>, he knows as it really is that beings are immeasurable and beings are innumerable.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāḥ sattvā asaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvā iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is that beings are immeasurable and innumerable.

children.text: yāny api tāni subhūte aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ cittacaritāni tāny api subhūte tathāgataḥ sattvāsadbhāvatayaiva prajānāti
children.translated_text: And whatever mental activities there are of those immeasurable, innumerable beings, those too, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows precisely through the non-existence of beings.

children.text: evaṃ khalu subhūte prajñāpāramitāmāgamya tathāgato 'prameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmaprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni cittacaritāni ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as they really are the immeasurable and innumerable mental activities of immeasurable, innumerable beings.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī ||
children.translated_text: For in this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the revealer of this world for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃkṣiptāni cittāni saṃkṣiptāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the constricted minds of immeasurable, innumerable beings as constricted minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃkṣiptāni cittāni saṃkṣiptāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti sa saṃkṣepaṃ kṣayataḥ kṣayaṃ ca akṣayato yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the constricted minds of immeasurable, innumerable beings as constricted minds? He knows contraction as subject to exhaustion, and he knows exhaustion as inexhaustible, just as it really is.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃkṣiptāni cittāni saṃkṣiptāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the constricted minds of immeasurable, innumerable beings as constricted minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgatā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ vikṣiptāni cittāni vikṣiptāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> know as they really are the distracted minds of immeasurable, innumerable beings as distracted minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ vikṣiptāni cittāni vikṣiptāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti dharmatātaḥ subhūte tāni cittāni vikṣiptāni
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the distracted minds of immeasurable, innumerable beings as distracted minds? From the standpoint of <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature), <s>Subhūti</s>, those minds are distracted.

children.text: alakṣaṇāni hi tāni cittāni akṣīṇānyavikṣīṇānyavikṣiptāni tāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: For those minds are without marks; they are not exhausted, not dispersed, and not distracted. He knows as it really is: those are the minds.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgatā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāṃ vikṣiptāni cittāni vikṣiptāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> know as they really are the distracted minds of immeasurable, innumerable beings as distracted minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmaprameyākṣayāṇi cittānyaprameyākṣayāṇi cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the immeasurable and inexhaustible minds of immeasurable, innumerable beings as immeasurable and inexhaustible minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmaprameyākṣayāṇi cittāni aprameyākṣayāṇi cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti tasya subhūte tathāgatasyādhiṣṭhitaṃ bhavati taccittam anirodham anutpādam asthitam anāśrayam asamam aprameyam asaṃkhyeyam yenaiva yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ākāśāprameyākṣayatayā cittāprameyākṣayateti
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the immeasurable and inexhaustible minds of immeasurable, innumerable beings as immeasurable and inexhaustible minds? <s>Subhūti</s>, that mind of that <s>Tathāgata</s> is established as non-ceasing, non-arising, not standing, without support, unequaled, immeasurable, and innumerable; by that very means he knows as it really is that mind is immeasurable and inexhaustible because space is immeasurable and inexhaustible.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmaprameyākṣayāṇi cittānyaprameyākṣayāṇi cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the immeasurable and inexhaustible minds of immeasurable, innumerable beings as immeasurable and inexhaustible minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃkliṣṭāni cittāni saṃkliṣṭāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the defiled minds of immeasurable beings as defiled minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃkliṣṭāni cittāni saṃkliṣṭāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti asaṃkleśasaṃkliṣṭāni subhūte tāni cittāni asaṃketāni
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the defiled minds of immeasurable beings as defiled minds? <s>Subhūti</s>, those minds are defiled by non-defilement; they are without designation.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃkliṣṭāni cittāni saṃkliṣṭāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the defiled minds of immeasurable beings as defiled minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmasaṃkliṣṭāni cittānyasaṃkliṣṭāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the undefiled minds of immeasurable beings as undefiled minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmasaṃkliṣṭāni cittānyasaṃkliṣṭāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti prakṛtiprabhāsvarāṇi subhūte tāni cittāni
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having come to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as they really are the undefiled minds of immeasurable beings as undefiled minds? Those minds, <s>Subhūti</s>, are luminous by nature.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmasaṃkliṣṭāni cittānyasaṃkliṣṭāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having come to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, knows as they really are the undefiled minds of immeasurable beings as undefiled minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ līnāni cittāni līnāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having come to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, knows as they really are the sunken minds of immeasurable beings as sunken minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ līnāni cittāni līnāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti anālayalīnāni subhūte tāni cittāni
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having come to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as they really are the sunken minds of immeasurable beings as sunken minds? Those minds, <s>Subhūti</s>, are sunken without any resting-place.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ līnāni cittāni līnāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having come to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, knows as they really are the sunken minds of immeasurable beings as sunken minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ pragṛhītāni cittāni pragṛhītāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having come to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, knows as they really are the taken-up minds of immeasurable beings as taken-up minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ pragṛhītāni cittāni pragṛhītāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti agrāhyāṇi subhūte tāni cittāni pragrahītavyāni
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having come to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as they really are the taken-up minds of immeasurable beings as taken-up minds? Those minds, <s>Subhūti</s>, which are to be taken up, are not graspable.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ pragṛhītāni cittāni pragṛhītāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having come to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, knows as they really are the taken-up minds of immeasurable beings as taken-up minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sāsravāṇi cittāni sāsravāṇi cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having come to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, knows as they really are the minds of immeasurable beings with outflows as minds with outflows.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sāsravāṇi cittāni sāsravāṇi cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti asvabhāvāni subhūte tāni cittāni asatsaṃkalpāni

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmanidarśanāni cittānyanidarśanāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the minds of immeasurable beings that are without appearance as minds without appearance.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmanidarśanāni cittānyanidarśanāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti alakṣaṇatvādarthaviviktatvātsubhūte adṛśyaṃ taccittaṃ trayāṇāṃ cakṣuṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ vā anavabhāsagatam
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the minds of immeasurable beings that are without appearance as minds without appearance? Because it is signless and devoid of object, <s>Subhūti</s>, that mind is not seen by the three eyes, and it has gone beyond the illumination of all of them.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmanidarśanāni cittānyanidarśanāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the minds of immeasurable beings that are without appearance as minds without appearance.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sapratighāni cittāni sapratighāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the obstructed minds of immeasurable beings as obstructed minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sapratighāni cittāni sapratighāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti asatsaṃkalpitāni subhūte tāni cittāni śūnyānyārambaṇavaśikāni
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the obstructed minds of immeasurable beings as obstructed minds? Those minds, <s>Subhūti</s>, are falsely imagined, empty, and subject to the power of an object.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sapratighāni cittāni sapratighāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the obstructed minds of immeasurable beings as obstructed minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmapratighāni cittānyapratighāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the unobstructed minds of immeasurable beings as unobstructed minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmapratighāni cittānyapratighāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti advayabhūtāni subhūte tāni cittāni abhūtasaṃbhūtāni
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the unobstructed minds of immeasurable beings as unobstructed minds? Those minds, <s>Subhūti</s>, have become nondual; they have arisen as unreal.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmapratighāni cittānyapratighāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the unobstructed minds of immeasurable beings as unobstructed minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sottarāṇi cittāni sottarāṇi cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the surpassable minds of immeasurable beings as surpassable minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sottarāni cittāni sottarāṇi cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti yā subhūte sottarasya cittasya yathābhūtatā na tatrāsti manyamānatā
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, does he know as it really is the surpassable minds of immeasurable beings as surpassable minds? <s>Subhūti</s>, in the reality-as-it-is of a surpassable mind there is no conceiving.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sottarāṇi cittāni sottarāṇi cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the surpassable minds of immeasurable beings as surpassable minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmanuttarāṇi cittānyanuttarāṇi cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the unsurpassed minds of immeasurable beings as unsurpassed minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmanuttarāṇi cittānyanuttarāṇi cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti aṇv api hi subhūte cittamanupalabdham
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the unsurpassed minds of immeasurable beings as unsurpassed minds? For even the smallest mind, <s>Subhūti</s>, is not apprehended.

children.text: tato niṣprapañcāni tāni cittāni
children.translated_text: Therefore those minds are free from conceptual proliferation.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmanuttarāṇi cittānyanuttarāṇi cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the unsurpassed minds of immeasurable beings as unsurpassed minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmasamāhitāni cittānyasamāhitāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the unconcentrated minds of immeasurable beings as unconcentrated minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmasamāhitāni cittānyasamāhitāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti asamasamāni hi subhūte tāni cittāni asamavahitāni evamasamāhitāni tāni cittāni
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the unconcentrated minds of immeasurable beings as unconcentrated minds? For those minds, <s>Subhūti</s>, are equal to the unequal and are not gathered together; thus those minds are unconcentrated.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmasamāhitāni cittānyasamāhitāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the unconcentrated minds of immeasurable beings as unconcentrated minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ samāhitāni cittāni samāhitāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the concentrated minds of immeasurable beings as concentrated minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ samāhitāni cittāni samāhitāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti samasamāni hi subhūte tāni cittāni samavahitāni
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the concentrated minds of immeasurable beings as concentrated minds? For those minds, <s>Subhūti</s>, are equally equal and are gathered together.

children.text: evaṃ samāhitāni cittānyākāśasamāni
children.translated_text: In this way the concentrated minds are equal to space.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ samāhitāni cittāni samāhitāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the concentrated minds of immeasurable beings as concentrated minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmavimuktāni cittānyavimuktāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the unliberated minds of immeasurable beings as unliberated minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmavimuktāni cittānyavimuktāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti svabhāvavimuktāni subhūte tāni cittāni abhāvasvabhāvāni
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the unliberated minds of immeasurable beings as unliberated minds? Those minds, <s>Subhūti</s>, are liberated by nature and have non-being as their nature.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmavimuktāni cittānyavimuktāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the unliberated minds of immeasurable beings as unliberated minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ vimuktāni cittāni vimuktāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the liberated minds of immeasurable beings as liberated minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ vimuktāni cittāni vimuktāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti cittaḥ hi subhūte tathāgatena na atītamupalabdhaṃ na anāgatam na pratyutpannamupalabdham asattvāccittasya
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the liberated minds of immeasurable beings as liberated minds? For the mind, <s>Subhūti</s>, has not been apprehended by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as past, nor as future, nor as present, because of the non-existence of mind.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ vimuktāni cittāni vimuktāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the liberated minds of immeasurable beings as liberated minds.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmadṛśyāni cittānyadṛśyāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the invisible minds of immeasurable beings as invisible minds.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmadṛśyāni cittānyadṛśyāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti asattvātsubhūte adṛśyaṃ taccittam
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as it really is the invisible minds of immeasurable beings as invisible minds? Because it does not exist, <s>Subhūti</s>, that mind is invisible.

children.text: abhūtatvādavijñeyam apariniṣpattito 'grāhyaṃ prajñācakṣuṣā divyena cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: Because it is unreal, it is unknowable; because it is unproduced, it is ungraspable by the eye of wisdom and by the divine eye.

children.text: kutaḥ punarmāṃsacakṣuṣā sarveṣāmanavabhāsagatatvāt
children.translated_text: How much less by the fleshly eye, since all things have gone beyond manifestation.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmadṛśyāni cittānyadṛśyāni cittānīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as it really is the invisible minds of immeasurable beings as invisible minds.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī ||
children.translated_text: For in this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the revealer of this world for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāmunmiñjitanimiñjitāni yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as they really are the opening and closing of the eyes of immeasurable, innumerable other beings and other persons.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyāṇāṃ parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāmunmiñjitanimiñjitāni yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti sarvāṇi tāni subhūte rūpaniśritāni utpadyamānānyutpadyante iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, know as they really are the opening and closing of the eyes of immeasurable, innumerable other beings and other persons? All those, <s>Subhūti</s>, arise, when they arise, dependent on form; thus he knows them as they really are.

children.text: evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: sarvāṇi tāni vijñānaniśritāni utpadyamānānyutpadyante iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: All these, when they arise dependent on consciousness, arise; he knows this as it really is.

children.text: tatra subhūte kathaṃ tathāgatena tānyunmiñjitanimiñjitāni rūpaniśritāni vijñātāni bhavanti evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ kathaṃ tathāgatena tānyunmiñjitanimiñjitāni vijñānaniśritāni vijñātāni bhavanti bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: There, <s>Subhūti</s>, how have those openings and closings of the eyes been known by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as dependent on form? So too feeling, perception, and formations. How have those openings and closings of the eyes been known by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as dependent on consciousness? The view, 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> exists after death,' pertains to form.

children.text: na bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> does not exist after death,' pertains to form.

children.text: bhavati ca na bhavati ca tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> both exists and does not exist after death,' pertains to form.

children.text: naiva bhavati na na bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> neither exists nor does not exist after death,' pertains to form.

children.text: evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> exists after death,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: na bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> does not exist after death,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: bhavati ca na bhavati ca tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> both exists and does not exist after death,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: naiva bhavati na na bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> neither exists nor does not exist after death,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: śāśvata ātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are eternal; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to form.

children.text: aśāśvata ātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are not eternal; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to form.

children.text: śāśvataś ca aśāśvata ātmāvalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are both eternal and not eternal; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to form.

children.text: naiva śāśvato nāśāśvata ātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are neither eternal nor not eternal; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to form.

children.text: evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: śāśvata ātmāvalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are eternal; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: aśāśvata ātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are not eternal; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: śāśvataścāśāśvata ātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are both eternal and not eternal; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: naiva śāśvato nāśāśvata ātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are neither eternal nor not eternal; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: antavānātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are finite; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to form.

children.text: anantavānātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are infinite; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to form.

children.text: antavāṃś ca anantavāṃścātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are both finite and infinite; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to form.

children.text: naivāntavān nānantavānātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are neither finite nor infinite; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to form.

children.text: evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: antavānātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are finite; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: anantavānātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are infinite; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: antavāṃś ca anantavāṃścātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are both finite and infinite; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: naivāntavān nānantavānātmā avalokaś ca idameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The self and the world are neither finite nor infinite; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: sa jīvastaccharīramidameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The life-principle is that body itself; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to form.

children.text: anyo jīvo 'nyaccharīramidameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi rūpagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The life-principle is one thing and the body another; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to form.

children.text: evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: sa jīvastaccharīramidameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The life-principle is that body itself; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: anyo jīvo 'nyaccharīramidameva satyaṃ mohamanyaditi vijñānagatam etat
children.translated_text: The view, 'The life-principle is one thing and the body another; this alone is true, anything else is delusion,' pertains to consciousness.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ tānyunmiñjitanimiñjitāni rūpaniśritāni vijñātāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: In this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one, has known those openings and closings of the eyes of immeasurable, innumerable other beings and other persons as dependent on form.

children.text: evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: tānyunmiñjitanimiñjitāni vijñānaniśritāni vijñātāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Those openings and closings of the eyes have been known as dependent on consciousness.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāmamasaṃkhyeyānāṃ parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ tānyunmiñjitanimiñjitāni yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as they really are those openings and closings of the eyes of immeasurable, innumerable other beings and other persons.

children.text: iha subhūte tathāgato rūpaṃ jānāti
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows form.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgato rūpaṃ jānāti tathā subhūte tathāgato rūpaṃ jānāti yathā tathatā
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s> know form? In such a way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows form: just as suchness is.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgato rūpaṃ jānāti
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows form.

children.text: evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: iha subhūte tathāgato vijñānaṃ jānāti
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows consciousness.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte tathāgato vijñānaṃ jānāti tathā subhūte tathāgato vijñānaṃ jānāti yathā tathatā
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s> know consciousness? In such a way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows consciousness: just as suchness is.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgato vijñānaṃ jānāti
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows consciousness.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgata imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ tānyunmiñjitanimiñjitāni yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, by resorting to this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows as they really are those openings and closings of the eyes of immeasurable, innumerable other beings and other persons.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgatastathāgatatathatayā ca skandhatathatayā ca unmiñjitanimiñjitatathatayā ca tathatāṃ prajñapayati
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, by the suchness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by the suchness of the aggregates, and by the suchness of the openings and closings of the eyes, the <s>Tathāgata</s> makes suchness known.

children.text: yaiva ca subhūte skandhatathatā saiva lokasyāpi tathatā
children.translated_text: And whatever is the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the aggregates, <s>Subhūti</s>, that itself is also the suchness of the world.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ uktaṃ hyetatsubhūte tathāgatena pañca skandhā loka iti saṃjñātāḥ iti
children.translated_text: For what reason? For this was said by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>: 'The five aggregates are designated as the world.'

children.text: tasmāttarhi subhūte yā skandhatathatā sā lokatathatā
children.translated_text: Therefore then, <s>Subhūti</s>, what is the suchness of the aggregates is the suchness of the world.

children.text: yā lokatathatā sā sarvadharmatathatā
children.translated_text: What is the suchness of the world is the suchness of all <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: yā sarvadharmatathatā sā srotaāpattiphalatathatā
children.translated_text: What is the suchness of all <s>dharmas</s> is the suchness of the fruit of stream-entry.

children.text: yā srotaāpattiphalatathatā sā sakṛdāgāmiphalatathatā
children.translated_text: What is the suchness of the fruit of stream-entry is the suchness of the fruit of once-returning.

children.text: yā sakṛdāgāmiphalatathatā sā anāgāmiphalatathatā
children.translated_text: What is the suchness of the fruit of once-returning is the suchness of the fruit of non-returning.

children.text: yā anāgamiphalatathatā sā arhattvaphalatathatā
children.translated_text: What is the suchness of the fruit of non-returning is the suchness of the fruit of arhatship.

children.text: yā arhattvaphalatathatā sā pratyekabuddhatvatathatā
children.translated_text: What is the suchness of the fruit of arhatship is the suchness of pratyekabuddhahood.

children.text: yā pratyekabuddhatvatathatā sā tathāgatatathatā
children.translated_text: What is the suchness of pratyekabuddhahood is the suchness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: iti hi tathāgatatathatā ca skandhatathatā ca sarvadharmatathatā ca sarvāryaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatathatā ca ekaivaiṣā tathatā anekabhāvābhāvāpagatā anekatvādanānātvādakṣayatvādavikāratvādadvayatvādadvaidhīkāratvāt
children.translated_text: Thus the suchness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the suchness of the aggregates, the suchness of all <s>dharmas</s>, and the suchness of all noble disciples and pratyekabuddhas are this one suchness, free from manifold states and non-states, because it is not multiple, not diverse, inexhaustible, unchanging, nondual, and not divided in two.

children.text: evameṣā subhūte tathatā tathāgatena prajñāpāramitāmāgamya abhisaṃbuddhā
children.translated_text: In this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, this suchness has been fully awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s> by resorting to <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī
children.translated_text: For in this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the revealer of this world for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgato 'sya lokasya lokaṃ saṃdarśayati
children.translated_text: For in this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> shows this world as the world.

children.text: evaṃ cāsya lokasya darśanaṃ bhavati evaṃ hi subhūte prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ mātā jananī janayitrī
children.translated_text: And in this way there is the seeing of this world. For in this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the mother, progenitress, and begetter of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte tathāgatastathatāmabhisaṃbudhya lokasya tathatāṃ jānāti avitathatāṃ jānāti ananyatathatāṃ jānāti
children.translated_text: For in this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, having fully awakened to suchness, the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows the suchness of the world; he knows its non-falseness; he knows its non-other suchness.

children.text: evaṃ ca subhūte tathāgatastathatāmabhisaṃbuddhaḥ saṃstathāgata ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: And in this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, because the <s>Tathāgata</s> has fully awakened to suchness, he is called 'the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

children.text: sthaviraḥ subhūtirāha gambhīrā bhagavaṃstathatā
children.translated_text: The elder <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Deep, Blessed One, is suchness.

children.text: ato bhagavaṃstathatāto buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ bodhiḥ prabhāvyate prakāśyate
children.translated_text: From suchness, Blessed One, the awakening of the blessed Buddhas is brought forth and made manifest.

children.text: ko 'tra bhagavan anyo 'dhimokṣyate 'vinivartanīyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'rhan vā paripūrṇasaṃkalpo dṛṣṭisaṃpanno vā pudgalaḥ tathā hi bhagavan imāni sthānāni paramagambhīrāṇi tathāgatenābhisaṃbudhya ākhyātāni
children.translated_text: Who else here, Blessed One, will have faith in this, apart from an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva, or an arhat whose intention is fulfilled, or a person endowed with right view? For these points, Blessed One, are exceedingly deep, having been fully awakened to and declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

children.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat evametatsubhūte evam etat
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is.

children.text: paramagambhīrāṇīmāni sthānāni tathāgatenābhisaṃbudhya ākhyātāni
children.translated_text: These points are exceedingly deep, having been fully awakened to and declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tathā hi subhūte akṣayaiṣā tathatā yā tathāgatenābhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhya akṣayākṣayaivākhyātā ||
children.translated_text: For thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, this suchness that has been fully awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s> is inexhaustible; having fully awakened to it, he has declared it as inexhaustible, indeed inexhaustible.'

children.text: atha khalu śakradevendrapramukhāḥ kāmāvacarā rūpāvarāś ca devaputrā brahmakāyikānāṃ ca viṃśatidevaputrasahasrāṇi yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya ekānte tasthuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the sons of the gods of the desire realm, headed by <s>Śakra</s>, and the sons of the gods of the form realm, together with twenty thousand sons of the gods belonging to the Brahmā hosts, approached the Blessed One, bowed their heads to the Blessed One's feet, and stood to one side.

children.text: ekāntasthitāś ca te kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarāś ca devaputrā bhagavantametadavocan gambhīrā bhagavan dharmāḥ prakāśyante
children.translated_text: Standing to one side, those sons of the gods of the desire realm and of the form realm said this to the Blessed One: 'Deep, Blessed One, are the <s>dharmas</s> that are being revealed.

children.text: kathaṃ bhagavan atra lakṣaṇāni sthāpyante bhagavānāha śūnyamiti devaputrā atra lakṣaṇāni sthāpyante
children.translated_text: How, Blessed One, are marks established here?' The Blessed One said: 'Sons of the gods, the marks here are established as empty.

children.text: ānimittamiti apraṇihitamiti devaputrā atra lakṣaṇāni sthāpyante
children.translated_text: Sons of the gods, the marks here are established as signless and as wishless.

children.text: anabhisaṃskāra iti anutpāda iti anirodha iti asaṃkleśa iti avyavadānamiti abhāva iti nirvāṇamiti dharmadhāturiti tathateti devaputrā atra lakṣaṇāni sthāpyante
children.translated_text: Sons of the gods, the marks here are established as without formation, as non-production, as non-cessation, as non-defilement, as non-purification, as non-existence, as nirvāṇa, as the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas), and as suchness.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ aniśritāni hi devaputrā etāni lakṣaṇāni
children.translated_text: For what reason? For these marks, sons of the gods, are unsupported.

children.text: ākāśasadṛśāni hi devaputrā etāni lakṣaṇāni
children.translated_text: For these marks, sons of the gods, are like space.

children.text: naitāni lakṣaṇāni tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena sthāpitāni
children.translated_text: These marks were not established by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: naitāni lakṣaṇāni rūpasaṃkhyātāni
children.translated_text: These marks are not reckoned as form.

children.text: evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānasaṃkhyātāni
children.translated_text: In the same way, they are not reckoned as feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness.

children.text: naitāni lakṣaṇāni rūpaniśritāni na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānaniśritāni
children.translated_text: These marks do not depend on form, and they do not depend on feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness.

children.text: naitāni lakṣaṇāni devairvā nāgairvā manuṣyairvā amanuṣyairvā sthāpitāni
children.translated_text: These marks were not established by gods, nāgas, humans, or nonhumans.

children.text: naitāni lakṣaṇāni sadevamānuṣāsureṇa lokena śakyāni cālayitum
children.translated_text: These marks cannot be shaken by the world together with its gods, humans, and asuras.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ sadevamānuṣāsuro 'pi hi loka etallakṣaṇa eva
children.translated_text: For what reason? For even the world together with its gods, humans, and asuras has just this mark.

children.text: nāpyetāni lakṣaṇāni kenāpi hastena sthāpitāni
children.translated_text: Nor were these marks established by anyone with a hand.

children.text: yo devaputrā evaṃ vadet idamākāśaṃ kenāpi sthāpitamiti api nu sa devaputrāḥ samyagvadan vadet evamukte kāmāvacarā rūpāvarāś ca devaputrā bhagavantametadavocan na bhagavan ākāśaṃ kenacitsthāpitam
children.translated_text: Sons of the gods, if someone were to say, "This space has been established by someone," would he, sons of the gods, be speaking rightly?' When this had been said, the sons of the gods of the desire realm and of the form realm said this to the Blessed One: 'No, Blessed One; space has not been established by anyone.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ asaṃskṛtatvādbhagavan ākāśasya nākāśaṃ kenacitsthāpitam ||
children.translated_text: For what reason? Because, Blessed One, space is unconditioned; space has not been established by anyone.'

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstān kāmāvacarān rūpāvarāṃś ca devaputrānāmantrayate sma evametaddevaputrāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed those sons of the gods of the desire realm and of the form realm:

children.text: utpādādvā tathāgatānāmanutpādādvā tathaivaitāni lakṣaṇāni sthitāni
children.translated_text: 'So it is, sons of the gods. Whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or do not arise, these marks stand just so.'

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ yathaitāni hi sthitāni tathābhūtāni tathāgatenābhisaṃbudhya ākhyātāni
children.translated_text: For what reason? For, just as these things stand, in just that way, as they really are, they were fully awakened to and declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tasmāddevaputrāstathāgatastathāgata ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, sons of the gods, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is called the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat gambhīrāṇi bhagavan imāni lakṣaṇāni tathāgatenābhisaṃbuddhāni
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Deep, Blessed One, are these characteristics that have been fully awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tathāgatānāṃ cāsaṅgajñānaṃ yaduta prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: And the unobstructed knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is, namely, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: asaṅgajñānāya prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāṃ gocaraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, for the sake of unobstructed knowledge, is the sphere of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>."

children.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat evametatsubhūte evam etat
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī
children.translated_text: For thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the revealer of this world for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas.

children.text: yathā subhūte tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā imāṃ dharmaṃ prajñāpāramitāmupaniśritya viharanti tathaivaite dharmāḥ sadā sthitāḥ asthānatastathāgatairabhisaṃbuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas, abide relying upon this <s>dharma</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, so these dharmas are always established, awakened to by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> from non-establishment.

children.text: ataste dharmamevopaniśritya viharanti dharmaṃ satkurvanti gurukurvanti mānayanti pūjayantyarcayantyapacāyanti
children.translated_text: Therefore they abide relying on the <s>dharma</s> itself; they honor the <s>dharma</s>, hold it weighty, esteem it, worship it, venerate it, and show reverence to it.

children.text: prajñāpāramitaivaiṣā subhūte dharmāṇāṃ dharmateti tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ satkurvanti gurukurvanti mānayanti pūjayantyarcayantyapacāyanti
children.translated_text: This very <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the dharmatā (true nature) of dharmas; therefore the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas, honor <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, hold it weighty, esteem it, worship it, venerate it, and show reverence to it.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ ato hi subhūte prajñāpāramitātastathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ sarvajñatāyāḥ prabhāvanā bhavati
children.translated_text: For what reason? Because from <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, comes the manifestation of the omniscience of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas.

children.text: kṛtajñāḥ kṛtavedinaś ca tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas, are grateful and mindful of what has been done.

children.text: yatkhalu subhūte samyagvadanto vadeyuḥ kṛtajñaḥ kṛtavedīti tattathāgataṃ hi te samyagvadanto vadanti kṛtajñaḥ kṛtavedīti
children.translated_text: If, <s>Subhūti</s>, people speaking correctly should say, 'He is grateful and mindful of what has been done,' then speaking correctly they say precisely this of the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'He is grateful and mindful of what has been done.'

children.text: yatkhalu subhūte tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho yena yena yānenāgataḥ yayā yayā pratipadā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ tathāgatastadeva yānaṃ tāmeva pratipadamanugṛhṇīte anuparipālayati tayaiva kṛtajñatayā kṛtaveditayā
children.translated_text: For, <s>Subhūti</s>, by whatever vehicle the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, has come, and by whatever practice he has fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, the <s>Tathāgata</s> favors and preserves that very vehicle and that very practice, through that very gratitude and mindfulness of what has been done.

children.text: iyaṃ subhūte tathāgatasya kṛtajñatā kṛtaveditā draṣṭavyā
children.translated_text: This, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be seen as the gratitude and mindfulness of what has been done on the part of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte tathāgatena sarvadharmā akṛtā akṛtā ityabhisaṃbuddhāḥ avikṛtā avikṛtā ityabhisaṃbuddhāḥ anabhisaṃskṛtā anabhisaṃskṛtā ityabhisaṃbuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has fully awakened to all dharmas as 'unmade, unmade,' as 'unmodified, unmodified,' as 'uncompounded, uncompounded.'

children.text: iyam api subhūte tathāgatasya kṛtajñatā kṛtaveditā draṣṭavyā
children.translated_text: This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be seen as the gratitude and mindfulness of what has been done on the part of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: prajñāpāramitāṃ hyāgamya subhūte tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya evaṃ sarvadharmeṣu jñānaṃ pravṛttam
children.translated_text: For, having come to <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, such knowledge of all dharmas has arisen for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: anenāpi subhūte paryāyeṇa prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī ||
children.translated_text: For this reason also, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the revealer of this world for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas."

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat yadā bhagavan sarvadharmā ajānakā apaśyakāḥ tadā kathaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat sādhu sādhu subhūte yastvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhametamarthaṃ paripraśnīkartavyaṃ manyase
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: "When, Blessed One, all dharmas do not know and do not see, then how, Blessed One, is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> the revealer of this world for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas?" When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Good, good, <s>Subhūti</s>, that you think the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, should be questioned about this matter.

children.text: subhūtirevamāha sarvadharmā ajānakā apaśyakā iti
children.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said, 'All dharmas do not know and do not see.'

children.text: evametatsubhūte evam etat
children.translated_text: So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is.

children.text: sarvadharmā ajānakā apaśyakāḥ
children.translated_text: All dharmas do not know and do not see.

children.text: kathaṃ subhūte sarvadharmā ajānakā apaśyakāḥ sarvadharmā hi subhūte śūnyāḥ
children.translated_text: How, <s>Subhūti</s>, do all dharmas not know and not see? For all dharmas, <s>Subhūti</s>, are empty.

children.text: sarvadharmā hi subhūte aniśritāḥ
children.translated_text: For all dharmas, <s>Subhūti</s>, are without support.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte sarvadharmā ajānakā apaśyakāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, all dharmas do not know and do not see.

children.text: evamete subhūte sarvadharmāḥ prajñāpāramitāmāgamya tathāgatairabhisaṃbuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: In this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, all these dharmas, having come to <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, have been fully awakened to by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.text: evam api subhūte prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī rūpasyādṛṣṭatvāt
children.translated_text: Thus too, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the revealer of this world for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas, because form is unseen.

children.text: evaṃ vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ vijñānasyādṛṣṭatvātsaṃdarśayitrī
children.translated_text: So also, because feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are unseen, it is the revealer.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> becomes the revealer of this world for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas."

children.text: subhūtirāha kathaṃ bhagavan rūpasyādṛṣṭatā bhavati kathaṃ vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām kathaṃ bhagavan vijñānasyādṛṣṭatā bhavati bhagavānāha yadi subhūte na rūpārambaṇaṃ vijñānamutpadyate evaṃ rūpasyādṛṣṭatā bhavati
children.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: "How, Blessed One, does form come to be unseen? How does feeling, perception, and formations; how, Blessed One, does consciousness come to be unseen?" The Blessed One said: "If, <s>Subhūti</s>, consciousness does not arise with form as its object, in this way form comes to be unseen.

children.text: evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: So too with feeling, perception, and formations.

children.text: yadi subhūte na vijñānārambaṇaṃ vijñānamutpadyate evaṃ vijñānasyādṛṣṭatā bhavati
children.translated_text: If, <s>Subhūti</s>, consciousness does not arise with consciousness as its object, in this way consciousness comes to be unseen.

children.text: yā ca subhūte rūpasyādṛṣṭatā yā ca vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām yā ca subhūte vijñānasyādṛṣṭatā saiva lokasya dṛṣṭatā bhavati
children.translated_text: And that unseenness of form, <s>Subhūti</s>, that unseenness of feeling, perception, and formations, and that unseenness of consciousness, <s>Subhūti</s>, is itself the seeing of the world.

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte lokastathāgatena dṛṣṭo bhavati
children.translated_text: For in this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the world is seen by the <s>Tathāgata</s>."

children.text: evaṃ hi subhūte prajñāpāramitā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmasya lokasya saṃdarśayitrī
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the revealer of this world for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arhats, the perfectly awakened Buddhas.

children.text: kathaṃ ca subhūte prajñāpāramitā lokaṃ saṃdarśayati iti lokaḥ śūnya iti lokaṃ sūcayati evaṃ prajñāpayati evaṃ lokaṃ saṃdarśayati
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> reveal the world? Saying, 'The world is empty,' it indicates the world; in this way it makes it known, in this way it reveals the world.

children.text: iti loko 'cintya iti lokaḥ śānta iti loko vivikta iti lokaviśuddhyā lokaṃ sūcayati
children.translated_text: Saying, 'The world is inconceivable; the world is peaceful; the world is secluded,' it indicates the world through the purification of the world.

children.text: evaṃ lokaṃ prajñāpayati evaṃ saṃdarśayatīti ||
children.translated_text: In this way it makes the world known; in this way it reveals it.
